f9cc74c866ba.title: ArchiMate models — every view, element and relationship a node
f9cc74c866ba.content: Skill id: archimate-models · Package: ui-core · Subgraph: cat-harness/archimate/ · Tools: archimate-check, archimate-metamodel, archimate-blocks, archimate-pages, archimate-crossings, archimate-detangle, archimate-actors · Process: archimate-publish (processes/ui/archimate-publish.bpmn) .

94aee331ac65.title: The rule
94aee331ac65.content: An ArchiMate model is content, and every view, element and relationship in it is a node. The model is authored in Archi and committed where it is held. Everything a reader sees is made from it on each build, by the archimate subgraph, in TypeScript, with no tool installed: . | node | IRI (under the graph’s path) | page |   | . | model | <m>.jsonld | <m>/ | views; elements by layer | . | view | <m>/views/<id>.jsonld | <m>/views/<slug>/ | the drawing, <m>/views/<id>.svg | . | element | <m>/elements/<id>.jsonld | <m>/elements/<slug>/ | documentation, properties, relationships, views it is in | . | relationship | <m>/relationships/<id>.jsonld | <m>/relationships/<id>/ | its ends, the views it is drawn in | . Ids are Archi’s own (id-<32 hex>). An element therefore keeps its IRI across a model’s versions wherever Archi kept its id — the property the RA mapper’s mappings already depend on. Never rewrite one; the reader refuses an id that is not filename-safe rather than minting one nobody chose.

f4b32501afdd.title: Readable page paths: slugs, worked out each build
f4b32501afdd.content: The IRI stays the id; only the page is at a slug. A view’s or element’s page is at <m>/views/1-central-health-workforce-registry/, while its node keeps <m>/views/<id>.jsonld. Cite the IRI when a link must last: the page path is for reading. Relationships keep id paths, since almost none are named. Slugs are worked out from the names on every build (cat-harness-tools/archimate/schemas/slugs.ts). Nothing is committed and nothing redirects, so: . | a rename moves the page, and the old path is gone (a clean break; there are no <m>/views/<id>/ page paths); | on a clash the object first in the model keeps the plain slug and a later one gets -<first hex of its id>; | an author can choose a slug in Archi with a slug property (lower-case words joined by -); a malformed one, or two objects choosing the same one, is refused rather than rewritten; | an object with no readable name keeps its id as its path. | . Do not put slugs in the IRIs: the mapper keys on the ids, and a rename would move an IRI.

2ce486d85270.title: The metamodel is derived, never drawn
2ce486d85270.content: Do not draw a metamodel view. Which element types a model uses, and which relationships it draws between them, is computed from the model by the Tool archimate-metamodel (cat-harness-tools/archimate/schemas/metamodel.ts): . | every element type, with how many elements it has; | every pattern (source type, relationship, target type), with its count and the ids of the relationships that follow it; | for each pattern, whether ArchiMate allows it, from Appendix B of ArchiMate 3.2 as Archi holds it (archimate/schemas/archimate-relationships.json, MIT, written only by scripts/import-archi-relationships.ts; to adopt a newer table, re-run it on a newer Archi checkout); | the placeholder elements: an element named after its own type (“Goal”, “Application Component (MS)”). They are how a metamodel gets drawn by hand inside a model, so they and their relationships are listed and kept out of the patterns. A Grouping or Junction left with its default name is not one. | . archimate-pages draws the same result on each model’s Metamodel in use page (<m>/metamodel/), linked from the model page and the rail: a class diagram laid out from DOT by Graphviz in WebAssembly (@hpcc-js/wasm-graphviz, no binary, no JVM), with the same diagram as DOT, Mermaid and JSON beside it (<m>/metamodel.dot|.mmd|.json|.svg), and tables of the types and patterns, each pattern linking its relationships. archimate-metamodel --check fails when a relationship follows a pattern ArchiMate does not allow. Placeholders are reported, never fatal: a model is its authors’, so removing a hand-drawn metamodel view is their call. Cite the derived page instead of the view in the meantime. The steps run in this order, all in the pipeline lane of process archimate-publish: archimate-check, then archimate-metamodel --check, then archimate-pages. A refused relationship goes back to the model’s author.

fd07b5316061.title: Actors come first; the model points at them
fd07b5316061.content: The SMART Guidelines order is fixed: a DAK’s L2 generic personas become the IG’s L3 FHIR ActorDefinitions, and the architecture realizes them (DPI-H RA §4.3.2). So the ActorDefinitions are written in the IG, from the DAK personas, and the model only points at them. A model author tags the box that realizes an actor in Archi with the property fhir-actor, whose value is the actor’s canonical URL (fhir-actor = http://smart.who.int/ra/ActorDefinition/FacilityRegistry), the same way an element carries skosConcept. | Never generate an ActorDefinition, or any FSH, from the model. When the model has a box with no actor, the actor is missing from the IG: add it there, from the persona, then tag the box. | Never decide which box realizes which actor from names. That is the model authors’ call, made in Archi. A box may realize several actors (one tag each), and an actor may be realized by several boxes. | A #system actor goes on an application or technology element (an ApplicationComponent, an ApplicationInterface, a Node). A #person actor goes on a BusinessActor or BusinessRole. Any other kind of element cannot realize an actor. | Check the tags with the Tool archimate-actors: bun run cat archimate:actors --instance . --model <id>. It fails on a value that is not a canonical URL, a tag that names no ActorDefinition of the IG, an element kind that cannot be an actor, and a type mismatch. It warns about each ActorDefinition that no element realizes. With --strict that warning becomes a failure. --json gives element → actors and actor → elements, for the pages’ back-links. | . Data objects follow the same rule. A data object points at an existing logical model with logical-model = <canonical>. Write the logical model in the IG first. Never derive a logical model from the model’s boxes. The data object’s class diagram will be generated from that logical model once the IG holds one, so tag the data object now and do not draw the diagram.

1ec76b0feeda.title: A document’s tables and figures are drawn, not typed
1ec76b0feeda.content: A table or figure in the document that restates the model is generated from data by the Tool archimate-blocks, and --check keeps it from drifting. | Relationship rules and types live once, as an archimate-relationship-rules/v1 file in the archimate directory (cat-harness-tools/archimate/schemas/rules.ts). The document’s rules table and relationship-types table are drawn from it (config tables), with the caption and footnotes left as the editors wrote them. | The rules are in charge, not the model. For a rules table that names a model, the Tool reports rules the model never uses, relationships no rule covers, rules ArchiMate’s own table refuses, and relationship types the rules use but the document never explains. The editors decide, link by link, whether to fix the model or add a rule; nothing is rewritten from the model. | A figure that is a view names an svg in its figures entry. The Tool writes the view there with the same renderer as the view’s page, and the block shows that SVG instead of a picture. Check the drawing against the published figure first: element names in the model must match the document’s. | .

034034dd8245.title: Untangle every view you touch
034034dd8245.content: A change to a view never adds tangles, and every view you touch leaves with no more than it came with. A tangle is a line crossing another line, or a line running through a box that is not one of its ends and does not hold one. Groups (bands) are not boxes here; a line may cross a band. Every time you add, move or re-route anything in a view: . | Count before. bun run cat archimate:crossings --model <file> --view <id or page slug> lists each tangle by the boxes it joins. | Make the change. | Let the tool lower it. bun run cat archimate:detangle --model <file> --view <id or page slug> reports what it would do: re-route lines (straight, an L, or a Z through a free lane between rows) and swap same-size boxes in the same row or column. It keeps a change only if the count goes down. Add --apply to write it, or --routes-only when the boxes’ places carry meaning (an order, a flow). | Look at the drawing (gen-archimate-pages.ts --out, or the view’s SVG) before and after. The count is a gate, not taste: undo a swap that breaks a reading order, and fix by hand what the tool cannot (it never adds, resizes or regroups boxes). | Count after, and say both numbers in the PR: “view X: 10 crossings, 13 through a box → 1, 2”. More tangles after than before is a finding to fix before review, not a note. | . Ways to untangle by hand, in the order to try them: . | Put a box beside the boxes it is joined to: a line’s ends in neighbouring rows, not across the view. | Order a row like the row it connects to (the order of the boxes above), so lines between the two rows run parallel. | Route a long line along the gap between rows or bands, with right-angle bendpoints, rather than diagonally across boxes. | Nest instead of drawing a line where the notation allows it (composition, aggregation, assignment, realization): a box drawn inside another already says how they relate, and the renderer draws no line for it. | When nothing else works, a view shows too much: split it. | .

d1d3f83d8a7b.title: Every view carries a key for readers who do not know ArchiMate
d1d3f83d8a7b.content: Readers of a view are mostly not architects. Every rendered view carries a plain-language key below it, saying what each colour, shape, line and end used ON THAT VIEW means, in words a reader without ArchiMate understands (“Realization: makes real, or achieves”), not the specification’s terms alone. render-view.ts draws it by default, keyed only to what the view uses. Do not turn it off for a published view, and do not export a view without it. When the renderer gains a new mark, the key gains its line in the same change.

68e3ff08389d.title: Names are the source’s own terms, linked to their concept
68e3ff08389d.content: An element or view named from a source uses the source’s own term, and links to that term’s SKOS concept. Not our paraphrase, shortening or merger of two terms. When a model depicts a module of a handbook, the box is named as the handbook names it, and the element carries the concept’s IRI (a property, e.g. concept = the skos:Concept IRI in the source’s glossary scheme) so its page links to the definition. | No concept for the term yet: add it to the source’s glossary scheme first, from the source’s own words, then name the element. | The source’s term is too long for a box: keep the full term as the name and let the renderer wrap it; a short form goes in skos:altLabel, never in place of the name. | Our term and the source’s disagree: that is a content decision (term-disagreement), not something to settle by renaming in Archi. | .

65fb4873a1c3.title: The model is never a source of the glossary
65fb4873a1c3.content: An authored model depicts concepts; it never defines them. Meaning lives in the SKOS glossary, read from the source documents. So: . | Never write a term, label, definition, focus or relationship into a glossary from a model someone authored in Archi. An element with no term is a term to add from the source’s own words, not from the box. | The glossary may drive the model (archimate-from-glossary, a content layer’s Tool): names, documentation and relationships flow from the terms into the model, and Archi keeps the layout. | The term pages’ “depicted by” links read skosConcept on each build and write nothing into the glossary, so they are allowed. | The one exception is an ingested model, received from elsewhere and held as a source under the instance’s library/. It may seed the glossary once (archimate-from-glossary --seed --from library/…), like any other ingested source. The Tool refuses --seed on any model outside library/. | .

646ee213fc4f.title: No Java, no Archi CLI, no Archi report — ever
646ee213fc4f.content: The Archi command line (com.archimatetool.commandline.app) renders an HTML report and view images, and it is not part of any pipeline here: . | it needs a JVM, a virtual display (xvfb) and a ~200 MB download on every run — too heavy for CI, and impossible in a web client, which is where an agent or a reader working in the browser is; | its views are raster images nobody can link into, and its pages are not nodes: nothing it writes has an IRI in the graph. | . render-view.ts draws the same views from the same coordinates — the bounds Archi stores for every box (made absolute, since Archi nests a child’s bounds in its parent’s) and the relative bendpoints it stores for every line — into SVG in ArchiMate’s notation, every box a link to its element. The reader handles Archi’s native XML and its zipped archive with node:zlib. If a view ever needs something the renderer does not draw, extend the renderer; do not bring Archi back into a workflow. The same reasoning applies to any other Java-only ArchiMate tooling (jArchi scripts, coArchi). Authors use Archi on their own machines; the pipeline never does.

b4cced9304e3.title: What an instance declares
b4cced9304e3.content: . | A directory of graph typology archimate in its <instance>.json, with a coverage.visualiser naming <dir>/index.html so the navbar carries a tile to it (harness-tiles). served: true only if the pages are written into the graph rather than a site build. | cat-archimate.config.json, at the instance root or inside that directory: { "$schema": "cat-archimate-config/v1", "directory": "<id>", "models": [{ "id", "file", "title"?, "description"? }] }. | cat-harness in its needs, directly or through its closure. | . Order matters when a platform is pinned. A declaration naming the archimate typology throws in every platform reader that does not know the kind yet (cat-harness.ts: unknown graph typology). Move the instance’s pin of cat-harness to a commit carrying this subgraph first, then declare.

b97f37c31321.title: Versions — one folder per SemVer version
b97f37c31321.content: A model is named for the version of the thing it describes. In a WHO IG repository that is the version: in sushi-config.yaml: archimate/0.2.0/, with earlier drafts as SemVer pre-releases (0.2.0-draft.1, …). The model id in the config is that version, so …/archimate/0.2.0/elements/<id>.jsonld is both versioned and stable. Never name a folder v2, prev1 or current: a label that says nothing about what it is a version of invites two identical models under two names.

fbba9a02c7ce.title: In a folio’s build
fbba9a02c7ce.content: bun run <platform>/cat-harness-tools/archimate/scripts/check-archimate.ts --instance . bun run <platform>/cat-harness-tools/archimate/scripts/gen-archimate-pages.ts --instance . --out _site . Run both in the staging build, after the document site is built and before the navbar pass, so the pages are railed like every other page. --out is the normal mode: a few models yield thousands of pages, which belong in a build, not a commit. gen-archimate-pages.ts without --out writes into the graph and --check gates it, as the openapi subgraph does, for an instance small enough to commit its pages.

debb896a17bc.title: Citing the model from prose
debb896a17bc.content: Link the element’s or the view’s page, never a copy of a picture. A view’s SVG links relative to its own address, so it can also be embedded in a document as a figure (<m>/views/<id>.svg) and stay current with the model. Where the document and the model disagree — a figure in the text that is not a view in the model — that is a finding for the model’s authors, not something to paper over with an exported image.

182df38f118c.title: What is not read yet
182df38f118c.content: The Open Group exchange format; custom images and fonts on a diagram (each box names its type in its corner instead of Archi’s icons — the icons are the tool’s artwork, not the notation’s); sketch and canvas views; ingesting a model from another repository. Each is an extension of schemas/archimate.ts or render-view.ts, in TypeScript.

1c1180f47c04.title: Do not
1c1180f47c04.content: . | Draw a metamodel, or any class diagram of the model’s types, by hand: cite the derived “Metamodel in use” page. | Run Archi, a JVM or xvfb in a workflow to render a model. | Commit exported view images beside a model; they go stale on the next edit. | Name model folders by anything but the version they describe. | Declare the archimate typology in an instance whose platform pin predates it. | Commit a change to a view without counting its tangles before and after. | Publish a view without its key, or name an element from a source in words the source does not use. | .

00f14e5ba008.title: Processes that run this skill
00f14e5ba008.content: | process | step(s) that name it | . | Publish an ArchiMate model — every picture derived from it | Check the model parses and resolves; Derive the metamodel in use; Fix the relationship in Archi; Write pages, drawings and the metamodel page | . | DTH authoring | Link to smart-ra ArchiMate (calls a sub-process) | .

2afd38db5371.title: ArchiMate models
2afd38db5371.content: Generated from cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/archimate-models.md — do not edit here. ✎ Edit this page’s source .

d53562f37231.title: The version suffix is part of the identity
d53562f37231.content: An arXiv id without a version (2602.12670) names the latest version, a moving target. A paper can gain a version after you cite it, and then: . | the section you quoted may have moved, been rewritten, or gone | a numbered result may refer to something else | the PDF you archived and the PDF a reader fetches are different documents with the same name | . Record the versioned id, always (2602.12670v4, what was read). If a source arrived without a version, resolve and record the version at capture time; do not leave it blank. The id is recorded as claimed, as filing-dublin-core states for identifiers generally.

d4ecf193efb5.title: What to keep beside the PDF
d4ecf193efb5.content: The PDF is only the rendering (compare archiving-web-pages): . | artefact | why | . | the versioned id and the abstract-page URL | the canonical handle, and where the metadata lives | . | the metadata record — title, authors, date, categories, abstract | this is the dcterms layer, and it is authoritative from arXiv rather than inferred from the PDF | . | the DOI, when the submission has one | many arXiv papers are also published; the DOI is a different identity for a possibly different version | . | the licence the submission declares | see below — it varies per paper | . | the e-print source, where the licence permits | the PDF is typeset output; re-extraction from source beats OCR of a rendering | .

6bd80b7d47dd.title: The licence is per submission, and it is not uniform
6bd80b7d47dd.content: arXiv hosting does not imply a redistributable licence; terms vary per submission. Record the declared licence with the capture. Whether this project may redistribute a source is a person’s decision, made from that record. The set a submitter chooses from . The submitter picks one, certifies they may grant it, and cannot change it afterwards. Record it as a source-licence record, the one licence vocabulary that a library manifest carries in meta.licence and an upload carries in intake.json. | as arXiv names it | id to record | may a folio redistribute it? | . | CC BY 4.0 | CC-BY-4.0 | yes, with attribution; commercial use allowed | . | CC BY-SA 4.0 | CC-BY-SA-4.0 | yes, with attribution — derivatives must carry the same licence | . | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 | CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 | non-commercially, share-alike | . | CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 | CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0 | verbatim only, non-commercially — no derivatives, so an extracted-and-restructured L1 entry is not covered | . | CC Zero | CC0-1.0 | yes, unconditionally | . | arXiv.org perpetual, non-exclusive licence 1.0 | http://arxiv.org/licenses/nonexclusive-distrib/1.0/ | no. It licenses arXiv to distribute, and limits re-use by anyone else | . | (pre-2004 submissions) | http://arxiv.org/licenses/assumed-1991-2003/ | no. Same effect — see below | . The last two have no SPDX identifier (the schema says “SPDX where one exists”): record the licence URI as the id, never an invented SPDX-shaped string. A CC BY-NC-ND source can be cited and quoted, but not restructured into content blocks and shipped: ingestion’s restructuring is what “NoDerivatives” withholds. Four readings that look right and are not . An arXiv licence is not an open licence. The “arXiv.org perpetual, non-exclusive licence” grants arXiv the right to distribute, not the reader. Absence is not permission. Submissions before January 2004 predate explicit licensing, so arXiv operates on an assumed licence equivalent to its own. That is a determined fact, so the record is stated with the assumed-licence URI and a basis naming the submission’s date — not unknown (unknown asserts that somebody looked and could not establish it). The licence belongs to the version, not to the paper (the version-suffix rule): versions of one submission may carry different licences. Record the licence of the version archived (2602.12670v4), not v1’s from the abstract page. The metadata field may understate the rights. An author whose required licence is not on arXiv’s list may select the arXiv licence and state the real one on the first page of the article; publisher permissions land there too. If page one carries a licence or copyright statement, it is part of the answer, and the basis says which of the two was read. What is always safe . Article metadata is dedicated to CC0 1.0, whatever the article’s own licence. Title, authors, date, categories and abstract can be recorded and republished even when the full text cannot, so an entry blocked on redistribution still carries a complete dcterms layer. A recorded arXiv licence does not go stale. The choice is irrevocable per version, so it needs no re-checking; only archiving a different version changes it. These facts are arXiv’s, stated at https://info.arxiv.org/help/license/index.html and https://arxiv.org/licenses/assumed-1991-2003/license.html, and captured in uploads/arxiv-license-information/ and uploads/arxiv-licence-assumed-1991-2003/. When a decision turns on the wording, read them there rather than this table.

3537d17a370a.title: What must be read, not recalled
3537d17a370a.content: Do not write arXiv API endpoints, query parameters or response field names from memory into code or into this page. Look them up: an almost-right field name parses to undefined, and the record silently loses its authors. arXiv has two identifier schemes (an older one with a subject prefix, a newer numeric one). Check any parser against the published identifier specification, not against sample files. This is the rule how-much-of-this-does-dublin-core-carry.md states for vocabularies, applied to an API.

bc8380ff787a.title: Where it lands
bc8380ff787a.content: A materialized paper is a queued unit, not corpus. It arrives in uploads/ with its capture record, and the uploads view counts it as waiting until l1-document-ingestion has made an L1 entry from it. Never write straight into library/: the completeness gate decides an entry is finished, and a source that skipped the queue skipped the gate. On failure the pipeline keeps the document in uploads/ and opens a bean.

760e1dad1f13.title: Materializing from arXiv
760e1dad1f13.content: Generated from folio-assistant-core/skills/library/cataloguing/archiving-arxiv.md — do not edit here. ✎ Edit this page’s source .

feba7c96482e.title: Archiving a web page
feba7c96482e.content: A URL is not an archive. It is a request you hope somebody else keeps answering.

d9437c510512.title: Two fidelities, and they are evidence of different things
d9437c510512.content: |   | PDF (or image) capture | zip / tarball (the page’s own bytes) | . | what it preserves | how the page LOOKED, at one moment, to one renderer | what the page WAS — markup, stylesheets, scripts, assets | . | what it is evidence of | appearance and layout | content and structure | . | reads without tooling | yes, anywhere, forever | no; needs unpacking, and often a browser | . | survives the site going dark | yes | yes | . | lets you re-extract text/tables later | badly — through OCR or PDF text, lossy | yes, from the source markup | . | citable as “this is what I saw” | yes, and this is its job | weakly — a reader cannot glance at it | . Neither substitutes for the other: a PDF-only capture has lost the page’s images, stylesheets and interactive content for good. The default is both; dropping one is a decision to record.

34582ce5858e.title: What the capture has to carry with it
34582ce5858e.content: A file with no capture record is an orphan the moment it is renamed. Record, as filing-dublin-core describes: . | the URL as requested, and the final URL if it redirected | when it was captured, to the timestamp | how — “printed to PDF from a logged-in browser” and “fetched unauthenticated” are different documents, and the second is what a reader can reproduce | what came with it — the asset list | the producer — which tool, which version | . The .extraction.json sidecars in an instance’s uploads/ carry container, method, capturedAt, producer, readAt and assets[]. Read one before inventing a shape.

7237a12c80d3.title: Things that are easy to get wrong
7237a12c80d3.content: A logged-in capture is not a public document. If the page was behind a session, the capture is of your view. Say so in the record, or a later reader will cite it as though anyone could have fetched it. Dynamic pages do not capture themselves. A page assembled by script after load may print as an empty shell. Check that the content is in the capture. Paywalls and licences. Being able to fetch something is not permission to redistribute it. Record the licence or its absence; holding and publishing an unlicensed capture are separate decisions, made by a person. A redirect chain is data. Shorteners and trackers in the requested URL are part of how the source was found, and the final URL is what should be cited.

038e6293f89e.title: What is NOT settled here
038e6293f89e.content: The archive format is not decided. WARC is the standard web archiving container and the obvious candidate; a plain zip of a single-page save is the cheap one. Which to adopt, and whether a capture must be replayable rather than merely stored, is settled against the published specification and available tooling, not from memory (the rule filing-dublin-core states for vocabularies). Until then, capture both fidelities and record how.

ffab15b0c0d5.title: Archiving a web page
ffab15b0c0d5.content: Generated from folio-assistant-core/skills/library/cataloguing/archiving-web-pages.md — do not edit here. ✎ Edit this page’s source .

9a8d4e1746fb.title: Artefact reachability — load is not evaluability, and a test is not a caller
9a8d4e1746fb.content: A declared executable artefact that nothing can reach is indistinguishable, from outside, from a decision nobody takes. That sentence is the whole skill. Run bun run cat audit:reachability before saying a decision table works, before saying a script has a caller, and before building any reachability report of your own. audit:reachability:check is a step in code-quality-gates.yml, so gates.ts derives it and bun run cat gates runs it. --strict is not wired: the self-declared entry points nothing runs are a backlog, and failOnNew is what makes a new one fail meanwhile. A check: alias never arrives ahead of its workflow step — gates.ts’s unrunScripts ratchet refuses one that no workflow runs — because an unwired gate must never read as a passing one.

0eb5256b7e76.title: Loading a table is not evaluating it
0eb5256b7e76.content: A table can load, carry a clean kg-qa verdict, and still be unevaluable by any caller: kg-audit’s decision-outcomes-used calls loadDecisionTable and possibleOutcomes, and neither parses a unary test, so a cell such as not("green") (which unaryTest throws on) passes. Likewise a script can be declared, documented and tested while nothing runs it. That is audit-coverage’s thesis in a new place: coverage is a relation between an instrument and the question it was built for. A loadability check measures loadability; evaluability is a different question.

be577a441122.title: Load is not evaluability — ask the EVALUATOR, never a grep
be577a441122.content: unreadableExpressions in src/workflow/decision-table.ts asks the question by running the evaluator over a probe, atom by atom. It lives beside the grammar rather than in the gate, and that placement is the rule: . A checker that restates a grammar is a second spelling of it, free to disagree with the first. Green on a table the engine refuses, or red on one it accepts — and nothing says which is wrong. Three things the walk had to get right, each of them a way to miss a finding: . | A comma-separated test cannot be handed to unaryTest whole. It is parts.some(…), so the first atom that matches ends the walk. 0, [1..5] reports clean if you ask once and 0 is the probe. | The probe is the number 0, the one value that reaches every branch without a type complaint. Under that probe a DecisionError is not “wrong fact type” — it is a rule that can never evaluate for any fact, such as > "a" — so it is reported rather than swallowed. | Output cells count. evaluate calls literal on every output column and possibleOutcomes reads only the first, so an unreadable literal in a second output column is invisible to every existing reader. | . Keep unaryTest throwing. Its own comment says why — “so an expression this evaluator does not implement can never be mistaken for a rule that simply did not match”. That property is what makes an unevaluable table findable; an evaluator that returned false for what it cannot read would make a table route confidently and wrongly. An unevaluable table is a hard failure, not a finding. It fails --check, which runs on every push. That is a deliberate divergence from audit-coverage, where --check fails on staleness alone: there, every finding is an unmet ambition; here, a table nothing can evaluate is a broken artefact.

0f1f429ee0eb.title: A diagram is reachable when the ENGINE’s resolver reaches it
0f1f429ee0eb.content: Same discipline, one layer out. The denominator is every .bpmn that any instance declares; the numerator is processFiles — the list workflow_list prints and workflow_start resolves against. processFiles keys by file stem and keeps the first claimant (if (!seen.has(stem))). So a dependency’s diagram whose stem collides with the root’s is dropped from the list, and workflow_start cannot reach it by stem or by bpmn:process id, because the id fallback searches the same list. Nothing measured that. A reachability guard over a corpus that is reachable today locks in a property the repository has rather than demanding work. A calledElement naming a process no file defines is NOT a finding. The loader’s own comment settles it: a folio may legitimately call out to a process it does not host, and the call stays opaque by design. Reporting it would turn a modelling decision into a permanent red. What this does NOT re-answer . | question | whose it is | . | does every activity’s <bootstrap.processes:skill ref> resolve? | check:workflow-refs (hard on a dangling ref), and kg-audit’s skill-* criteria | . | is any gateway pointing at this decision at all? | kg-audit’s decision-outcomes-used | . | which audits reach which KIND of node? | audit-coverage | . | can a node of this kind be TYPED? | check:kind-validators | . A third reader of one relation is a third answer free to disagree with the other two. The reference counts are recorded in the sidecar and never graded, so the measurement is visible without a second verdict being minted.

0e50a11361d8.title: When a grep fails both ways, narrow the SUBJECT — not the signals
0e50a11361d8.content: Two approaches fail. Asking the broad question (is any module reached by nothing?) returns hundreds of findings, mostly corpora discovered by directory walk — content blocks, schema modules a registry names, the tests bun test globs — which no inference can tell from a module nobody can run, and a gate with hundreds of findings is switched off within a week. Narrowing the signals (require an invocation verb beside the mention) still leaves dozens, mostly schema modules a declaration points at. What works is narrowing the subject. A module with a #! shebang or an import.meta.main guard has said it is runnable. That is a declaration inside the file, which is what directory-conventions insists a contract must be — extension is a coincidence; a declaration inside the file is the contract — and “does anything run this?” then has one right answer. The corpus is counted on each run and the sidecar holds the number; a count in prose is the next thing to go stale. audit-coverage says prefer a declaration where inference fails in both directions. This adds the move you make when there is no declaration to prefer: find the declaration the corpus already carries, and make that the subject. A mention is not a caller, and that distinction decides everything . Crediting every textual mention credits a script whose only callers are <bpmn:documentation> prose (and the generated glossary JSON that carries that prose onward). A grep over mentions clears the very defect this tool exists to catch. So a mention counts only on a line that also carries an invocation: a runtime, a spawn, or this repo’s own in-process tool dispatch. It is coversIn’s rule again — a parser over text has to tell a use from a mention — and here the use has a verb beside it. Two things that follow: . | Read the dot-prefixed callers explicitly. gitFiles excludes every dot-prefixed segment, so .github/workflows/ and .claude/commands/ — where most invocation actually lives — are invisible to a corpus walk. Reading only code-quality-gates.yml reported minify-site.ts and staging-rotate.ts as run by nothing; feature-staging.yml runs both. | Exclude your own sidecar. Its findings QUOTE the paths it reports, so reading it credits every module named in a finding with being reached, and the report clears itself one run later, permanently. Derive the path from the constants that write the file, so a relocation cannot leave the exclusion pointing elsewhere. audit-coverage states the general rule: a measurement must not be a term in itself. | . Two unrun states, and one number for both would hide the worse one . | state | what it means | . | invoked | something runs it | . | declared | nothing runs it, and it SAYS how it is reached — @entrypoint | . | entry-point-orphan | nothing runs it and nothing but a test imports it: it exists only as a claim | . | entry-point-latent | nothing runs it, and it IS a live library: a dead CLI branch on a reached module | . The last two are different pieces of work, and merging them would bury a module nobody can run inside a list of unused --help branches. Same reasoning as audit-coverage’s typed-only: a state exists to keep two findings from collapsing into one. A test is not a caller. A test proves a module works; it does not make it reachable. @entrypoint — say how you ARE reached . * @entrypoint script:merge:steward * @entrypoint none — written for the merge-steward tile, not built yet * @entrypoint spawned by scripts/foo.sh . Exactly one space, the star, one space — a continuation or an indented example is a mention, for coversIn’s reason, and this skill’s own code block above is one. A script:<name> claim is verified against package.json, because a declaration that can be checked should be; the free-text forms are recorded as your assertion and not graded. Under-claiming is recoverable — the count says so out loud. Over-claiming looks like reachability, which is the defect.

4ed78c396eb5.title: Three rules for building any reachability report
4ed78c396eb5.content: Commit the relation, print the census . The sidecar holds which decisions are evaluable, which diagrams the resolver reaches, which entry points are run, and the gateways pointing at each decision. It does not hold module totals: a census moves on any commit that adds a file, and a gate stale by default is one people learn to regenerate without reading. Judge against a baseline; never compare a committed copy . The records live on the qa-reports branch, so <instance>/test/results/ is a working copy and not a record. A writer writes it, qa:publish pushes the tree once per CI run, and a gate reads the baseline through judgeQaResult — --against <ref> for the branch, and a baseline that cannot be asked is unknown: reported, never a pass, never a failure. Compose the path with qaResultPath(root, stem) and nothing else: no caller spells QA_RESULTS_DIR itself, so moving the working copy is one line. failOnNew is how a soft finding bites. It asks directly whether a new orphan shows up in a diff. The standing orphans are inherited and do not fail; the next one fails on the commit that introduces it. Do not use staleness of a committed sidecar as a proxy for a backlog: the records are not on main, so there is nothing committed to be stale. failOn is for broken artefacts, and this is the one divergence . audit:coverage fails --check only on what is new, because every finding it has is an unmet ambition. Here the hard families are broken artefacts — a table nothing can evaluate, a diagram the resolver cannot reach, two diagrams answering to one name — so they go in failOn and fail whether or not a baseline calls them new. A defect is not less of one for having been there yesterday. --strict promotes entry-point-orphan to the same footing for the day the backlog closes. A sweep prints its own denominator, and a checker does not write . generalise-the-fix §1.2a: a report over zero diagrams passes every assertion in it. This refuses with EXAMINED NOTHING rather than reporting clean. And --check does not write. A checker that repairs the staleness it reports cannot be falsified — red once, green on the rerun, the file still stale in the repository.

af0b4b1bf0e3.title: Adding an artefact
af0b4b1bf0e3.content: . | A new .dmn: it is examined the moment any instance declares the directory it sits in. Expect unevaluable until every cell is in the subset decision-table.ts documents, and widen the evaluator rather than weakening the gate. | A new .bpmn: give it a stem and a bpmn:process id nothing else uses. Two diagrams answering to one name means workflow_start resolves one and silently not the other. | A new script: wire it in the same change — a package.json script, a workflow step, or a command. If it is genuinely latent, say so with @entrypoint. The honest answer is never a shebang and silence. | .

883b5dc16b4c.title: Ask the person
883b5dc16b4c.content: The procedure behind Process_AskThePerson. Every diagram step that puts a choice to a person calls that subprocess, and the subprocess’s tasks name this skill. The rule itself, and why, is the box at the top of interaction-modality; this skill is how to carry it out.

521e81e6708b.title: Input and output
521e81e6708b.content: The contract is input.schema.json and output.schema.json. | In: decides (what will differ), context (why now, what it touches, what happens next), glossary, two to four options each with a letter, label, does, pro, con, downstream and reversibility, the recommends letter and because, ifSilent, the question, othersPending and whether the step is reversible. The fields match DecisionRequestSchema in decision-request.ts, plus the letter and the context. Nothing is optional. | Out: asked.chat and asked.card (the two copies), outcome (answered, silent or dismissed), chosen (a letter), quote (the answer verbatim), defaultTaken, and rule when the answer became a rule. | .

ad8090c6057c.title: Steps
ad8090c6057c.content: . | Compose the input. Can the reader answer without opening anything? If not, it is not ready. | Write it in the chat, whole: context, every option with its letter, one-line explanation and trade-off, the recommendation marked, and what happens with no answer. This is the copy that lasts, because an answered card shows only the choice. | Offer the card with the same letters and labels, recommended one marked. This holds for request_decision even though that tool’s own text says not to repeat the question. No card tool: say so in the chat. | Wait for the tap; keep working on the recommended option where that can be undone. Never ask for a typed reply. | Not the one talking with the person? If you are a sibling (a project thread, a subagent or a session spawned while someone else holds the discussion), steps 2 and 3 in your own channel are not enough: hand the composed input back with hand-back-to-discussion, so the discussion agent asks it where the person is, and the answer comes back to you. Your own thread is never the only copy. | Return the output. A dismissal is not an answer. A rule-level answer is written into the governing skill in the same turn (symbiotic-interaction §2). | .

00671958d440.title: Processes that run this skill
00671958d440.content: This skill has its own process: Ask the person. | process | step(s) that name it | . | Ask the person | Compose the full question; Discuss it with the person (calls a sub-process) | . | Hand back to the discussion | Compose the hand-back and post it in own thread; Ask the person (calls a sub-process) | . | Saturation meta-merge: land the ready PRs when the runners are full | Dry-run, then ask the owner naming every PR | .

cbca6621b994.title: Ask The Person
cbca6621b994.content: Skill id: ask-the-person . Generated from JSON Schema — do not edit by hand. Run bun run cat-harness-tools/scripts/gen-schema-docs.ts.

d4573f6cf776.title: Input
d4573f6cf776.content: One question for a person, complete enough to answer without opening anything. The same fields as DecisionRequestSchema in schemas/process/decision-request.ts, plus a letter per option so the chat text and the card use the same handles. Every field is required: a question with no comparison, no recommendation or no default does not validate. | Field | Type | Required | Description | . | decides | string | yes | What is being decided, stated as what will DIFFER depending on the answer. Not the name of the decision. (minLength: 1) | . | context | string | yes | Why it is being asked now and what happens next: the PRs, beans and pages it touches, each named in words. Links are for more, never where terms are defined. (minLength: 1) | . | glossary | object | yes | Every id, path and coined name used above, glossed. {} means nothing needs a gloss. | . | options | array | yes |   | . | recommends | string | yes | The letter of the recommended option; it is shown first and marked. (pattern: ^[A-D]$) | . | because | string | yes | minLength: 1 | . | ifSilent | string | yes | What will be done if no answer comes. Then it is done. (minLength: 1) | . | question | string | yes | The question itself, last. (minLength: 1) | . | othersPending | integer | yes | How many other decisions wait; given as a count, never as a list of option names. (min: 0) | . | reversible | boolean | yes | false when acting on the answer cannot be undone. Then the default is never taken on silence: the step waits. | . options[] . | Field | Type | Required | Description | . | letter | string | yes | The handle shown in BOTH the chat text and the card. (pattern: ^[A-D]$) | . | label | string | yes | Short noun phrase the person taps. (minLength: 1) | . | does | string | yes | minLength: 1 | . | pro | string | yes | minLength: 1 | . | con | string | yes | What it costs to do. (minLength: 1) | . | downstream | string | yes | What it changes for everything else, afterwards. (minLength: 1) | . | reversibility | string | yes | minLength: 1 | . Raw schema · ✎ Edit .

7f4cb3abd994.title: Output
7f4cb3abd994.content: What the calling step gets back: proof the question went out twice, and the person’s answer or the default taken. A dismissed card is not an answer. | Field | Type | Required | Description | . | asked | object | yes | Where the two copies went. The chat copy is posted first. | . | outcome | "answered" | "silent" | "dismissed" | yes | answered: the person chose. silent: no answer came. dismissed: the card was closed without a choice; the question stays open in the chat. | . | chosen | string | null | yes | The letter chosen; null unless outcome is answered. (pattern: ^[A-D]$) | . | quote | string | null | yes | The person’s answer, verbatim, with who and when; null unless answered. | . | defaultTaken | boolean | yes | true when the work went ahead on ifSilent. Never true for an irreversible step. | . | rule | string | no | When the answer settles how a kind of thing is decided: the skill it was written into, in the same turn. | . | stagingLinks | any | no | When the question asks the person to look at changed pages: the staging preview, one deep link per changed page with the same page on main, shown in the chat copy. When there is no preview, say so in missing. Rule: cat-harness sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/staging-review.md §”The deep-link rule”. | . asked . | Field | Type | Required | Description | . | chat | string | yes | Id or link of the chat message holding the full question. (minLength: 1) | . | card | string | null | yes | Id of the card offered after it; null only when the host has no card tool, which the chat text then says. | . Raw schema · ✎ Edit .

7664a3db2524.title: Asset extraction — the index goes in, the contents do not
7664a3db2524.content: A container arrives in uploads/: a zip of a saved web page, a PDF, a tarball. Something inside it is wanted. What enters the knowledge graph is the INDEX — what is in there, how big, what type, when it says it was written — and not the files. Contents are extracted only when a person explicitly asks. bun run cat-harness-tools/scripts/extract-assets.ts <container> bun run cat-harness-tools/scripts/extract-assets.ts <container> --extract <path> --because "<why>" . The first writes a folio-extraction/v1 record beside the container. The second additionally writes one named entry, and refuses without a reason.

9f7110f73bea.title: Why metadata is the default
9f7110f73bea.content: A container’s index is cheap and complete: a zip’s central directory carries every entry’s size, name and timestamp without decompressing a byte. That is enough to answer what is in here, how big is it, and is any of it what I want — which is every question asked before somebody decides to take a file. Extracting by default costs the opposite: a working tree full of files nobody chose, each of which now looks committed-on-purpose to the next reader, and none of which carries a reason. --because is required, and it is the point of the flag. An entry written to disk with no stated reason cannot be told from one nobody authorised. The schema refuses it (ExtractedAsset.superRefine), so this is not a habit that depends on remembering.

d871d71ff5c0.title: The three timestamps, and the one that gets confused
d871d71ff5c0.content: |   | says | . | dc.date.issued | when the PUBLISHER published the work | . | materializedAt | when WE brought the bytes local | . | capturedAt | when a TOOL produced this file out of something else | . An extraction timestamp is never a publication date. For example, a WHO IRIS capture: . zip entries 2026-09-20 07:42 (all 11 of them) page PDF CreationDate D:20260920074221 info PDF CreationDate D:20260920074925 . The style guide those files contain was published in 2020. Every timestamp in the capture is 2026, and every one of them is the moment somebody pressed save. Folding the two would date a 2020 publication to 2026 and lose the only evidence the artefact is second-hand. isSingleCapture() computes the distinction rather than asserting it: when every entry shares one minute, ONE ACT wrote the container and no entry’s date says anything about that asset’s own history. When they differ, the container preserved real dates and they can be read as such.

19abd691a18f.title: A producer string is evidence, and is recorded verbatim
19abd691a18f.content: Both captured PDFs carry Producer: Skia/PDF m152. That is Chrome’s print-to-PDF — so neither file is WHO’s own PDF, both are printed web pages, and nothing else in a file listing, a byte count or a checksum shows it. Recorded as written, never normalised to “Chrome”: the version is part of the evidence, and a normaliser is a place for the fact to get smaller. This is the mechanical half of a judgement the IRIS intake already records by hand — the page PDF is filed with role none, because “we looked and it is not what it appears to be” is a different fact from “nobody looked”.

3c15a4d0902c.title: What is NOT dropped silently
3c15a4d0902c.content: A zip written on macOS carries a __MACOSX/ shadow per entry. Skipping them quietly makes the asset count disagree with the container’s own, and a reader reconciling the two finds nothing to explain the gap. They go in omitted[] with a pattern, a reason and a count.

3668dd0151c3.title: Derived renderings — the artefact we MADE, out of bytes we hold
3668dd0151c3.content: A cover thumbnail, an OCR text layer, a page raster, a converted figure: none of these came from the source. They were produced here, from something the source supplied, and the catalogue records an artefact, not where it came from — so a derived file with a plausible name and a materialized state is indistinguishable from one the publisher shipped. DSpace makes this concrete. It generates a THUMBNAIL bundle of its own, so “a THUMBNAIL bitstream on an IRIS item” reads, to anything downstream, as IRIS’s thumbnail. The three WHO IRIS covers in this repository are not those: iris.who.int is egress-blocked here, nothing upstream was fetched, and each is page 1 of a PDF already held, rasterised by cat-harness-tools/scripts/pdf-cover.py. Three rules, in the order they bite: . | of names what it was DERIVED FROM, not what it is ABOUT. The Handle identifies the item; putting it on a cover we rendered asserts IRIS supplied the image. local:cat-harness/uploads/<file>.pdf#page=1 says the true thing and resolves to the true thing. | The declaration is authored, and the tool refuses without it. the content core’s scripts/gen-covers.ts will not write bytes for a THUMBNAIL whose materialization.note does not declare the derivation. Generating that sentence would make the check circular — a tool cannot attest to its own output. | purpose: working, never archival. A rendering is regenerable from bytes already held and answers no source-loss question; MaterializationSchema already refuses a working copy that claims to discharge sourceLoss, and this is the case that rule was written for. | . Take the determined division, not the clever one. pdf-cover.py renders page 1 and calls it the cover, for the same reason pdf-pages.py sections by page: page 1 is a determined answer and “the cover” is not. Covers differ in shape (portrait, landscape, a scanned title page), and a heuristic has no way to say when it is unsure. Record the geometry. Bitstream.pixelWidth/pixelHeight exist so a listing reserves the box before the bytes arrive. Absent is unmeasured, not square. Check the claim where the check can actually run. A gate that re-renders a derived artefact needs the backend that produced it, and the CI job that runs this repository’s gates installs ruff and nothing else (stated on ingest-stdlib’s Tool node). Do not install a backend in the gate job, and do not degrade to could-not-determine — that would report unknown on every CI run, which is a check nobody can read. Split the claim instead. Of the five things a node asserts about a derived image, four need no decoder at all: . | claim | needs the backend? | . | the bytes exist | no | . | their sha256 is the declared one | no | . | their length is the declared one | no | . | their pixel dimensions are the declared ones | no — a PNG’s IHDR puts width and height at bytes 16..24, big-endian | . | these bytes are what that source renders to | yes | . So the gate keeps its teeth everywhere and gains the last row where the backend happens to be present — and it says in its own output which of the two it ran, because “3 covers verified” would read identically either way and the two are different assurances.

87dcebaa8541.title: Where the record lives
87dcebaa8541.content: Beside the container, in uploads/. uploads/ is a state graph — a queue that ingestion drains — so an extraction record is not L1 corpus and does not read as one. What a THEME or a LIBRARY entry cites is the extracted file’s localPath, which exists only once somebody asked for it.

5c8c7285cc7b.title: Associate a harness
5c8c7285cc7b.content: associatedHarnesses is an optional list on any harness that inherits cat-harness, including cat-harness itself. It names a harness published from its own repository, without publishing or materializing it here.

2193bedaed6d.title: What an association is, and what it is not
2193bedaed6d.content: A harness has four ways to relate to another: . | relation | field | what it does | . | depends | needs | loads the other harness under this one (the overlay) | . | references | remoteGraphs | knows one graph held elsewhere | . | utilizes | dependencies (config) | resolves another folio’s skills and translations | . | associated | associatedHarnesses | knows another harness, and where it lives | . needs is required of every instance in this repository, and so is a harness IRI. check:instance-graph fails on: . | an instance with no needs (write [] for the floor; absent stays a legal runtime state and reports unknown, but a repository does not ship it); | a needs name that resolves to nothing, or a cycle; | an instance with no absolute harness IRI, or two sharing one. | . The IRI is derived, never written: kg-export’s exportIdentity mints <canonicalUrl>/<stub>.jsonld for an instance that declares its own base, and <host base>/<stub>/<stub>.jsonld for one published from the host. The gate calls that function rather than restating it, so the gate and the published @id cannot disagree, and the one place to change a base stays one place. An associated harness is not loaded, not built and not copied. This site does not publish it. The config panel lists it under “Associated ↗ remote”, and its links go to the harness’s own site and its own repository.

830b61b63328.title: Declare one
830b61b63328.content: Add an entry to associatedHarnesses in the declaring instance’s <name>.json: . "associatedHarnesses": [ { "name": "ihris", "title": "iHRIS Knowledge Base", "url": "https://litlfred.github.io/ihris/", "repository": "https://github.com/litlfred/ihris", "relation": "folio-of", "note": "A folio on this platform, published from its own repository." } ] . | name is the harness’s instance name as its declaration gives it. | url is required: where a reader goes. | repository is where the panel’s ✎ points. Leave it out if the harness has no public source, and the panel shows no ✎. It never falls back to this checkout’s origin. | relation is a few words; folio-of means “a folio built on this platform”. | .

7c4a1353bbed.title: What the schema refuses
7c4a1353bbed.content: AssociatedHarnessSchema is strict. It refuses: . | an unknown key (a misspelt repo would otherwise vanish and leave ✎ pointing nowhere); | the same name twice; | a name that is also in needs (then it would be both loaded and not loaded); | a name that is a harness in this checkout. That one is local, and belongs in needs or nowhere (associated-harness-config.test.ts). | .

48dc09f43356.title: Then

592abc5af67a.doc: Audio transcription: which recogniser, when, and how to check it
592abc5af67a.title: Audio transcription: which recogniser, when, and how to check it
592abc5af67a.content: The default independent recogniser is whisper.cpp. The worked example below is the smart-ra meeting: smart-ra/uploads/output.mp4, 17:09, H.264 1080p with AAC mono 16 kHz audio, English, two speakers, with two Microsoft Teams exports: a .vtt with 275 cues and the “Download as .docx” export, about 2,600 words.

d6c3fbfec24d.doc: Audio transcription: which recogniser, when, and how to check it
d6c3fbfec24d.title: 1. Always: extract the audio first
d6c3fbfec24d.content: ffmpeg -i <video> -vn -ac 1 -ar 16000 -c:a pcm_s16le <name>.wav . Every recogniser below expects 16 kHz mono PCM, or resamples to it. Extracting once means each tool sees the same audio, and the comparison measures the recogniser, not the decoder. Record the source file’s SHA-256 beside the WAV.

7a84b3855da2.doc: Audio transcription: which recogniser, when, and how to check it
7a84b3855da2.title: 2. Two exports of one recogniser are ONE opinion
7a84b3855da2.content: The smart-ra .vtt and .docx agree on 98.0% of words. That agreement is not confirmation: they share the same errors (“Carl Lightner” for Leitner, “philtres” for filters), because both are the same Teams recognition, saved twice. Score agreement only between independent recognisers, and treat none as ground truth. A human-corrected reference is the only ground truth. The cat-harness skill crdm-recorded-walkthrough makes the same rule for requirements walkthroughs. An independent Vosk transcript of the same recording agreed with Teams on 80.2% of words, and corrected both errors above. That is what a second opinion is for.

21e3b0c4152c.doc: Audio transcription: which recogniser, when, and how to check it
21e3b0c4152c.title: 3. Choose by constraint
21e3b0c4152c.content: Verify the licences, language coverage and sizes below against the project’s release page before pinning a version. | situation | use | why | . | Default. CPU only, offline once the model is present, any of the six UN languages | whisper.cpp (transcribe-whisper-cpp), base or small; large-v3-turbo quantized if time allows | MIT; C++, no Python; covers ar, zh, en, fr, ru, es; segment timestamps; -tr translates into English | . | The pipeline is already Python, and word timestamps are wanted | faster-whisper (transcribe-faster-whisper), int8 with VAD | MIT; CTranslate2, about 4x faster than reference Whisper on CPU; word-level timestamps | . | A quick, tiny second opinion in English or a European language | Vosk (transcribe-vosk), small model | Apache-2.0; 40–50 MB models, very light; but lower accuracy and no small Arabic model | . | Speaker labels, or word-precise alignment | WhisperX + pyannote | BSD-2 / MIT; forced alignment and diarization; wants a GPU, and pyannote’s models need a Hugging Face token | . | English only, best accuracy or throughput, GPU available | NVIDIA Parakeet-TDT v2 or Distil-Whisper | CC-BY-4.0 / MIT weights; English only; Parakeet v3 and Canary add fr, es, ru, but never ar or zh | . Not for this corpus: any recogniser without Arabic or Chinese, when the recording is in one of those languages. A tool that silently produces English from Arabic audio is worse than no transcript.

baa2d8ee49cd.doc: Audio transcription: which recogniser, when, and how to check it
baa2d8ee49cd.title: 4. Translation is a separate step
baa2d8ee49cd.content: Whisper’s translate task goes into English only. To make an English transcript into ar, zh, fr, ru or es, run a machine-translation tool, then the round-trip QA (the untainted-verification skill): a back-translator that sees only the target text, and an adjudicator that never sees it. The open-source MT options found were MADLAD-400 (Apache-2.0), Opus-MT (CC-BY-4.0) and Argos Translate (MIT). NLLB’s weights are non-commercial; check the licence against the folio’s use before choosing it.

f85348d7ddb5.doc: Audio transcription: which recogniser, when, and how to check it
f85348d7ddb5.title: 5. Check it, with a number
f85348d7ddb5.content: | measure | tool | when | . | WER (word error rate) | jiwer, after normalising case, punctuation and numbers | against a human-corrected reference | . | CER (character error rate) | jiwer | Chinese, and Arabic, where word boundaries are not spaces | . | DER (diarization error rate) | pyannote.metrics | only when speaker labels are claimed | . | name and term disagreements | cat-harness-tools/scripts/meeting-recording.py compare --keys | between independent recognisers, as a list for a reviewer | . meeting-recording.py compare today is a difflib word similarity, not WER. Report it as “agreement”, never as an error rate.

7f0d2acd8d84.doc: Audio transcription: which recogniser, when, and how to check it
7f0d2acd8d84.title: 6. What blocks a run, stated rather than worked around
7f0d2acd8d84.content: Every recogniser needs model weights, and the hosts are: . | huggingface.co for the Whisper family (ggml and CTranslate2), pyannote, NeMo and Distil-Whisper; | alphacephei.com for Vosk. | . In a cloud session whose network policy denies those hosts, the code installs but has nothing to run. The fix is to add the host to the environment’s allowed domains, or to supply the weights some other way. Do not substitute a different tool’s output, or a made-up transcript, for the one that was asked for. The transcribe-faster-whisper Tool node’s remedy for a huggingface.co refusal currently points at transcribe-whisper-cpp, whose ggml models are hosted on huggingface.co too, so that remedy fails in the same environment.

06882ef27ac6.doc: Audio transcription: which recogniser, when, and how to check it
06882ef27ac6.title: 7. File it in the library
06882ef27ac6.content: A recording becomes a library entry with one transcript per language: . library/<slug>/ recording.json folio-recording/v1: title, date, spoken language, speakers, source{} sha256 transcript/<lang>.json folio-transcript/v1: one per language, timed segments + review state blocks/transcript-<lang>.jsonld written by gen-library-jsonld, one per transcript manifest.jsonld contains the transcript blocks . | Write an identity file from the meeting record (title, YYYY-MM-DD date, BCP 47 language, speakers as they name themselves). Never guess a field. | python3 cat-harness-tools/scripts/recording-transcript.py record <media> -o library --identity id.json --slug <slug>. The media can stay in uploads/: source.sha256 identifies it. | Write a recogniser file from the run (tool, version, model, model_sha256, invocation), then recording-transcript.py transcript library/<slug> --whisper-json out.json --recogniser r.json --date <run day>. The transcript is the recogniser’s text unchanged, state draft, drafted by the recogniser as a script. Name and term corrections are a reviewer’s; confirming is a human’s. | A translation is transcript/<lang>.json with translated_from: {lang, segments_sha256} (recording-transcript.py segments-sha256 prints the source’s) and the source’s segment times one for one. Its translator is drafted_by (an agent names its model). Then the round-trip QA in §4. | bun run cat-harness-tools/pipeline/gen-library-jsonld.ts --entry library/<slug>, then check:l1-complete. Its audio-transcripts requirement checks the record, the source-language transcript, and that every translation is of the same bytes and the same segments. A translation whose source changed after it was made is reported stale, as advisory. | .

e453071e6b64.title: Where the pieces are
e453071e6b64.content: | piece | where | . | Tool nodes (declared, not installed) | cat-harness tools/index.ts: transcribe-whisper-cpp, transcribe-faster-whisper, transcribe-vosk | . | extract, parse VTT/DOCX, compare, frames, Vosk transcribe | cat-harness-tools/scripts/meeting-recording.py | . | library entry: record, transcript, segments digest | cat-harness-tools/scripts/recording-transcript.py; schemas in cat-harness schemas/library/recording.ts | . | walkthrough method (requirements from a recording) | cat-harness sdlc/skills/crdm/crdm-recorded-walkthrough.md | . | translation QA | the untainted-verification skill; translation-roundtrip-record Tool | .

d58603cc63bf.title: Audit coverage — measured, with denominators
d58603cc63bf.content: A sidecar count is a fine measurement of sidecars and says nothing about gates. That sentence is the whole skill. Run bun run cat audit:coverage before saying a corpus is unaudited, before writing a criterion for a kind, and before building any coverage report of your own.

befa99c5e207.title: A zero sidecar count is not “unaudited”
befa99c5e207.content: kg-qa sidecars measure kg-audit’s criteria exactly, and KG_SUBJECT_KINDS has no bean — so zero sidecars over the work item store is the right answer to “how many criteria reach this kind” and no answer at all to “is this kind audited”: the check:bean-* gates, check:ready-to-close, check:stale-paths and check:harness-dirs audit work items. This is covered-is-not-reachable one level out: coverage is a relation between an instrument and the question it was built for, and the signal in reach is rarely the signal you need. It is not a second answer to check:kind-validators. That asks whether a kind can be typed — does it have a validator that loads. This asks who judges it. A kind can be perfectly typed and audited by nothing, and a validator sweep reports it as covered.

61ac11965b7d.title: The gate half is DECLARED, never inferred
61ac11965b7d.content: A gate names the kinds it covers in its own module docblock: . * @covers bean-defs, beans * @covers none — .github/workflows/ is not a declared graph typology * @covers computed — it sweeps whichever kinds declare `nodeSchemas` . The tempting alternative is to infer it: grep each gate’s source for a kind’s name or its declared directory. It fails in both directions at once. A gate that mentions beans/defs/ in passing scores as auditing work items; a gate that resolves its directory through directoriesForGraph names no path and scores as auditing nothing. Both answers wrong, neither looking wrong: could-not-determine rendered as clean (directory-conventions). Five states, because three real gates cannot use a static list . | state | what it means | . | declared | names its kinds | . | none | has decided it audits no declared graph — check:workflows reads .github/workflows/ | . | computed | derives its set at run time — check:kind-validators sweeps whatever declares nodeSchemas, so a literal would go stale silently | . | no-script | bun test, eslint, tsc — nothing here to annotate | . | undeclared | has not said | . none and undeclared are different facts and collapsing them would leave a gate that genuinely audits no graph with silence as its only honest answer. computed exists because writing today’s answer as a literal is the snapshot BASE_GRAPH_TYPOLOGIES’ own doc refuses for counts in prose. An undeclared gate is counted and printed, never zero, and every “unaudited” verdict is stated as an upper bound while any remain. That is check:kind-validators’ state 2, for its reasons. All gates declare, so audit:coverage:require-all is wired in CI and the findings are verdicts rather than bounds. The flag is what keeps it closed: a new gate arriving undeclared turns them back into an upper bound, silently, unless something fails. The output still states the caveat whenever the count is non-zero, because the day it reopens is the day a reader needs to be told. When you cannot tell, do not annotate — and then go and read it . A fabricated @covers credits a kind with coverage nobody checked. Under-claiming is recoverable — the count says so out loud. Over-claiming looks like coverage. To resolve an undeclared gate, read its scan set, not its title: check:retired-front-matter is computed, because its set is kgRoots(instance) plus the undeclared .claude/skills/ convention; and check:agents-claims covers code, not docs, because it grades the symbols a prose claim names while AGENTS.md itself is a node of no declared graph.

73d2a4cb5c66.title: Four states per kind, and a single zero cannot tell them apart
73d2a4cb5c66.content: | state | what it means | the case that earns the name | . | no-directory | no instance declares one of this kind | bean-defs, declared inside beans/beans.json, reached through its parent — and carrying gates | . | empty | a directory exists and holds nothing | a determined empty | . | typed-only | a declared validator TYPES its nodes; nothing judges them | none here | . | unaudited | files, and nothing at all — not even a validator | none here | . bean-defs is why the first state is not a gap: it has coverage and no directory of its own. A report that printed 0 for its directory count and left the reader to infer would have manufactured a finding. So every row prints all four counts and names its state rather than leaving it to be read off a zero. typed-only is a finding, and that is the whole reason it exists . A kind whose validator check:kind-validators parses its nodes against looks unreached, because that gate declares @covers computed, which this report counts as neither coverage nor gap. Do not call it covered. --strict fails on typed-only as its own family, because typing is not judging — a kind can parse perfectly against its schema while nothing has an opinion about what it says. What the state buys is telling two different pieces of work apart: a schema parses these nodes and no criterion reads them is not nothing whatsoever reaches this kind. check:harness-state carries one family per kind, and --strict is green and wired in CI. The state stays, because the next kind to arrive will pass through it — and the flag is what stops it resting there. A validator must reach the nodes that are produced . | A kind’s schema must point at the module that holds its shape, not the one that holds its path. A pointer to where a fact is not written is worse than none: a reader who follows it concludes the shape is undeclared on purpose. | Every writer stamps $schema. Consumers route a node by its tag and skip a file that has none, so a writer that omits it leaves only hand-written files validated. A validator over the nodes nobody produces is not coverage. | An untyped node read by a shell script degrades rather than fails: a jq failure branch prints a line nobody acts on. That is why interaction and issue-marks declare validators. | .

7321f39f1498.title: Three rules for building any coverage report
7321f39f1498.content: A measurement must not be a term in itself . If the report’s own sidecar lives in a graph it counts, writing it changes the next run’s answer, and the gate is satisfied only by running the writer twice. Exclude your own output, derive the path from the constants that write it so a relocation cannot leave the exclusion pointing elsewhere, and test that one run converges. Store the RELATION, print the census . The record is stored on the qa-reports branch keyed by commit. Do not record files and sidecars in it: a writer in one graph would turn another graph’s coverage gate red, and a file count that moves whenever anybody adds a page makes the gate stale by default — one people learn to regenerate without reading. What belongs in the sidecar is what defines coverage: declared directories, criteria reaching the kind, gates declaring it, the state. Those move when coverage moves, which is when a reviewer needs the diff. One bit of the census — hasFiles — is all the states need. Recording a count would make the report depend on the signal it exists to replace. A docblock that documents a tag necessarily contains the tag . coversIn read audit-coverage.ts’ own worked examples of @covers as declarations, crediting the coverage report with auditing the work item store. Any parser over docblocks has to tell a use from a mention, and indentation is the distinction JSDoc already provides: ^ \* @covers , exactly one space either side of the star.

fd04785870e9.title: What --check fails on, and what it does not
fd04785870e9.content: --check computes and judges, and writes nothing. It fails on a finding that is NEW against a baseline — a kind that lost its audit, a gate that stopped declaring, in the commit under review — and not on its own sidecar being stale: derived QA results live on the qa-reports branch, so nothing committed is left to be stale. The baseline is read with --against <ref> (a qa-reports ref such as main). A baseline that is not there is UNKNOWN — printed, never a pass, never a failure, because an unwritten baseline is not this change’s defect. A checker that mutates its own subject cannot be falsified (red once, green on the rerun, the file still stale), which is the one property generalise-the-fix Move 3 asks a guard to have. A kind whose directory is declared but absent from the checkout reads unknown, not empty: an absent answer is never printed as a determined zero. A directory that declares storage reads stored instead: its files are on the branch, fetch them with bun run qa:fetch. The findings are reported and do not fail. --strict fails on an unaudited kind and --require-all on an undeclared gate, for the day each gap is meant to close. A gate that refused every push until somebody wrote criteria for interaction/ is a gate that gets switched off within a week.

aac39c37ac0f.title: Adding a kind, or a gate
aac39c37ac0f.content: . | A new gate: add @covers in the same change. If you cannot tell which kind its subject is, leave it off — the count is the honest answer. | A new graph typology: it appears in the report the moment it is registered, because the denominator is the registry. Expect it to read unaudited until it declares a validator and typed-only until something judges it — and say in the sidecar why it needs nothing if that is the answer, never by letting the row read clean. | A relocation: nothing to update. Directories resolve through directoriesForGraph. | .

9b001d8d163c.title: auto-docs — the index is generated, the meaning is authored
9b001d8d163c.content: <base>/<handler>/auto-docs/<auto-doc-type>/<sub-graph>/ is an index of what exists. It is not the documentation. The handler generates the index; the author of <harness>/docs summarises each business process it lists, reusing the index’s assets rather than restating them.

3d2964cb4d95.title: The obligation: reference the index, then say what it cannot
3d2964cb4d95.content: bun run cat auto:docs emits, per artefact, what that artefact declares about itself — a skill’s front-matter description, a process’s own <bpmn:documentation>, its lanes, the skills its activities name. That is a complete answer to what exists and no answer at all to: . | what this process is for, and when you would be in it; | what it is not, and which neighbouring process you actually want; | why it has the lanes it has, and what changes when you cross one; | which of them a newcomer should read first. | . An index with no authored prose around it reads as complete while explaining nothing. So when you author <harness>/docs, for each business process the index lists, write the paragraph the index cannot contain. Judgement, not a gate.

6a187cffc6d3.title: Reuse the assets; never restate them
6a187cffc6d3.content: The summary links to and embeds the derived entries — the rendered BPMN, the lane and activity names, the skill descriptions the activities point at. It does not paraphrase them into a second copy, because a second copy is free to drift and the copy a reader finds first is the one with no generator behind it. For example, a page whose requirements table is parsed out of the skill that states the requirements, rather than typed beside it, and which refuses rather than rendering an empty table when the source moves. Do that, not a transcription.

ce4294459af8.title: What the handler emits, and what it does not
ce4294459af8.content: Read the type list off TYPES in gen-auto-docs.ts, not off this table. |   |   | . | built | index/skills, index/docs, index/processes, glossary — each emitting under auto-docs/ | . | declared, not built | index, index/bpmn, index/dmn, index/tasks, index/roles | . | withdrawn | toc | . toc is out. A table of contents is a document-order notion, and a sub-graph has no single order to take one over. Unbuilt types are absent, not stubbed. A type that emits an empty page is indistinguishable from one whose sub-graphs happen to be empty, and the second is a fact while the first is an unfinished feature.

7dad3711b665.title: Two rules the generator keeps
7dad3711b665.content: A type names the GRAPH TYPOLOGY its artefacts live in. Walking every declared directory would count the generated markdown rendering of each skill under docs/ as a second skill. A rendering of an artefact is not the artefact. Ask the repository’s own function; do not re-derive its rule. Supporting pages inside a skill (skills/<package>/<skill>/<page>.md) carry the same front matter and are not skills; skillMdDirs() already encodes that, so the generator calls it: two answers to “what is a skill” is one answer too many.

6972f4fc02ad.title: The sub-graph segment is the declared id, not its path
6972f4fc02ad.content: The URL carries the declared entry’s id: it is what <name>.json declares and what an override matches on, so an id-derived URL survives the directory moving. It also stays one segment, which lets orphanSubjectPages() prune with an exact ownership test rather than a new pruner. Each page states its declared path, so the mapping lives on the artefact rather than only in the URL.

88d335aec9b1.title: An empty sub-graph gets no page
88d335aec9b1.content: A sub-graph contributing nothing to a type is not rendered: a page claiming to index an empty directory is a link that resolves to nothing while reading as a section. The corollary is that a page disappearing is normal, so the generator prunes its own orphans through the shared helper — ownership read off the page’s own var SCOPE line, never assumed from the directory.

8e502fdedc46.title: What else belongs to a harness’s docs
8e502fdedc46.content: . | the QA check check:docs-populated, run by code-quality-gates.yml; | a per-harness docs landing page and a navbar over harnesses with a populated docs/ — neither is built. <base>/cat-harness/ is served by the generated published-graphs.md, so the obligation above is unmet for that route. | .
