f9ce6630f4c4.doc: Blocking is a claim about the work, not a mood
f9ce6630f4c4.title: Blocking is a claim about the work, not a mood
f9ce6630f4c4.content: blocked is the most expensive status a work item can carry, because a blocked work item stops being work anyone can pick up — and unlike a failure, nothing ever tells you it went stale.

c076a2cf50ce.doc: Blocking is a claim about the work, not a mood
c076a2cf50ce.title: Default to non-blocking
c076a2cf50ce.content: Before setting blocked, ask whether the work is genuinely stopped or merely awkward. These are not blocking: . | Waiting on CI. End the turn; the result wakes you. | Waiting on review. The PR is the artefact; other work continues. | Waiting on a decision you have not yet asked for. Ask, then continue on the parts that do not depend on the answer. | Part of the task is unclear. Do everything that does not depend on the unclear part, and state the assumption for the rest. | You would rather do something else first. That is ordering, not blocking. | . The test: is there any remaining work on this work item that could proceed right now? If yes, it is not blocked — it is in progress with a question attached.

1c0c1278eee9.doc: Blocking is a claim about the work, not a mood
1c0c1278eee9.title: When it really is blocked, say four things
1c0c1278eee9.content: A bare blocked tells the next agent nothing except not to bother. Carry: . | field | why | . | what it waits on | so a reader can tell whether the thing has since happened | . | since | so staleness is visible | . | expires | a timeout, after which the block is presumed stale | . | handoff | what a different agent should do on picking it up | . Write it as a ## Blocked on section — NOT as a status . ## Blocked on - **waits on:** the Tools-schema carrier decision - **since:** 2026-09-18T17:20Z - **expires:** 2026-09-20T17:20Z - **handoff:** if no answer by then, proceed with the JSON-LD carrier as recommended and note the assumption in the PR body. The work item’s status stays in-progress. status: blocked does not exist: beans update --status accepts only in-progress, todo, draft, completed and scrapped (schemas/tools/tool-types.ts lists the same five). A prescribed form the tool refuses can never be followed, and a block written only in prose has no date that can expire. expires is an ABSOLUTE timestamp, not +48h. A relative offset has to be read against since by whoever finds it, which means a stale block stays arguable; a timestamp is either in the past or it is not. check:bean-blocks enforces the four fields on any work item carrying this heading. An external block’s expiry is a RE-ASK date, not a takeover date . A work item waiting on an external party (a standards body finalising a model, for example) has no honest date on which an agent should “take that over” — inventing one would fabricate someone else’s schedule. So an expiry answers “when should somebody look at this again”, and the handoff says which kind it is: . | a block on work inside this repository → on expiry, take it over; | a block on an external party, an owner ruling, or another work item → on expiry, re-raise and move the date out, saying so. | . Both are checkable, and neither lets a work item sit forever unexamined. What the gate refuses is an expiry that is absent, not one that gets extended with a reason. The expiry is the part that matters. A block with no expiry is indistinguishable from abandoned work. An expired block is a signal to act on its handoff — take it over, or re-raise it — rather than a work item quietly sitting forever.

b81383e4d520.doc: Blocking is a claim about the work, not a mood
b81383e4d520.title: Prefer sub-beans to blocking
b81383e4d520.content: Most blocks are really “one part of this is stuck”. Split it: the stuck part becomes a child work item carrying the block, and the parent stays in progress. That keeps the work pickup-able and makes the actual dependency legible instead of hiding it inside a status. Sub-beans are also what make parallel work possible without a swarm — see swarm-management.md before deciding you need one.

c4480a338462.doc: Blocking is a claim about the work, not a mood
c4480a338462.title: Never
c4480a338462.content: . | Never mark a work item blocked to end a turn tidily. If you are stopping for the day, the work item is still in progress; say so in the report. | Never leave a block without an expiry. If you cannot say when it goes stale, you have not established that it is a block. | Never block on something you have not actually asked for. Asking is the work; waiting to be asked is not a dependency. | .

8d7275e7564a.title: Bean Coordination
8d7275e7564a.content: The bean-based work-plan system — the beans CLI, a flat-file issue tracker storing issues as markdown under beans/ — is how every session tracks its work-plan and how agents hand off across sessions.

63978996bbc8.title: A bean is never deleted
63978996bbc8.content: beans delete exists in the CLI. Do not use it — not on a sibling’s work item, and not on your own. Work that turns out not to be wanted is scrapped: status: scrapped, with a section saying why. That is also what “disable” means here; the CLI’s status vocabulary is draft, todo, in-progress, completed, scrapped, and there is no disabled state. A scrapped work item records that something was considered and rejected, and on what grounds, which stops the next agent re-entering the same dead end. A deleted work item leaves a sibling session unable to tell abandonment from accident. Archiving is a VIEW, not a third way out . beans/defs/archive/ is not a terminal state. An archived work item keeps its status and is still part of the store, moved aside rather than closed. Archiving is a file move, not a status change, so it records no reason and is not a way to make unwanted work go quiet. bun run cat check:bean-archive holds the rule: the archive node must be declared in beans/beans.json — check:declared-dirs and check:harness-dirs compare declarations against disk, not the reverse, so they cannot see an undeclared directory — and every work item in it must be completed or scrapped. If you want a work item out of the way, scrap it with its reasons first, then archive if you like. readBeans reads the active store and readArchivedBeans the archive. They share the graph typology bean-defs, so anything resolving by KIND gets whichever is declared first; resolve the archive by its id. A work item count that reads only the active store does not fall when work is archived. Claiming and closing are separately scoped. Claim before you work, so two sessions do not pick the same item (§”Claims are global via the branch store”). Closing is governed by evidence, not by authorship: read §”Closing a bean whose work has already landed” before you close anything — it carries the three obligations, and the ready-to-close tag for the case where you cannot re-derive the measurement yourself. What stays off limits is a work item a sibling is mid-flight on: a claim naming a branch, a recent note, an open PR. Closing that loses work the sibling had not finished reporting. Full cycle, as a diagram: Work items and todos. Operational spec (read these): . | todo-manager.md — work item lifecycle: beans create / update / list, parent/child epics, status transitions. This is the authoritative local usage spec. | session-intent.md — session-start intent + session-end results protocol against the master ledger and the work item queue. | pending-show.md — read-only “what is this session working on?” display. | idle-backlog.md — pull right-scoped work items while idle. | . Install the CLI: cat-harness-tools/scripts/install-beans.sh (idempotent; go install github.com/hmans/beans@latest).

cd738caf9a87.title: Claims are global via the branch store
cd738caf9a87.content: Claims are pushed immediately to the branch store (cat/cat-harness/beans) by bun run cat beans:claim <id> (claimOnBranchStore). The claim and its holder note are written directly to the store, so: . | Immediate global visibility: sibling sessions see your claim as soon as beans:claim finishes. | Atomic push with collision detection: if two sessions race to claim the same work item, BranchStore detects the conflict via blob expectations and rejects the second claim (state: "conflict"). | . Always claim with bun run cat beans:claim <id>. Do not use beans update --status in-progress, which writes no holder note and does not push to the branch store. A claim’s push is not gated. The pre-push gate hook (prepare-merge step 6) judges only the checked-out commit, and the branch store pushes its own commit to refs/heads/cat/.... So beans:claim and state:push stay fast with the hook installed. If one is ever refused as a gate failure, that is a bug in the hook. Report it, and do not bypass the claim. When several agents drain at once, or the store has more than one copy, the claim is bean-drain step 2 instead: check recent commits and open PRs first, then a plain commit on every copy (the bean-claim-check Tool). beans:claim writes one copy and reads status only. Linking PRs to beans with Closes-bean: and recording closure evidence . Code changes on main and work-plan state on the state branch are separate git refs. To link them: . | In your PR body, include: Closes-bean: <bean-id> . | On closure, record the landed merge commit SHA from main, the branch, and verifiable evidence in the work item body before pushing to the branch store: bun cat-harness-tools/scripts/branch-store.ts push --id beans . | . A DECISION bean you will not land soon — put the question where a person reads . A decision work item exists to get a ruling, and its value is that somebody with the authority to rule sees it. A work item left on a branch merely gets duplicated; a decision left there sits unanswered while every branch downstream of it waits. If you open a decision work item on a branch you will not land soon: set status: draft in front matter (or beans create "<title>" --status draft), post the question where the owner already reads — the issue — and say ON THE WORK ITEM where you posted it. All three parts. The comment is what reaches a person; the line on the work item stops the next session re-asking and tells them where the answer will appear; and status: draft lets automated checks find an unanswered ruling request. draft is already in the status enum and otherwise unused, so it needs no new vocabulary. A decision work item stays status: draft until ruled on or landed. --- status: draft ... --- . Prose is not a signal. Recognisers over work item prose (Recommendation, Options, safe default, ruling, an unticked box) disagree by two orders of magnitude, and also match work items that record a ruling. So a check reads the STATUS, never the prose. bun run cat check:draft-beans (scripts/check-draft-beans.ts) finds any ruling request that never landed, reporting with a denominator. The trigger is STARTING WORK, not claiming . Run the open-PR check before you start work on a topic — not only before you claim a work item. A cause inside a work item you already hold, a fix an owner just asked for, a gate you are about to unbreak: each is a unit of work a sibling can already have a PR up for, and none of them involves claiming anything. Search the subject as well as the id: the file you are about to edit, the gate you are about to turn green, the symbol you are about to add. A search keyed on a work item id finds nothing when the sibling’s work has no work item of its own, or its work item is only on an unpushed branch. A duplicate-detecting test punishes whoever merges second, not whoever duplicated. Merging first does not mean you were first. Starting any new unit of work runs the collision review in coordinate §”Starting new work”, scaled to its blast radius and recorded in the workplan work item before the first edit. And ASK AGAIN before you open the PR — looking once is not enough . Re-run the open-PR search immediately before you open your PR, not only before you start. A search at the start finds nothing when the sibling’s PR does not exist yet, and no relation between work items can fix that: the second session to arrive cannot know it is second. Only asking again later finds it. These do not replace the second check: . | alternative | why it fails | . | a describes: edge between work items | the second session to arrive cannot know it is second, so nobody is in a position to write the edge | . | a label or line on the PR carrying work item ids | only helps once a PR exists, which is exactly the window these collisions open in | . Same commands, same widened search terms — the subject as well as the id. The cost is one call at a moment you are already stopping to write a PR body. Two independent implementations of one fix produce two sets of observations, and the weaker implementation’s observations look like findings about the subject — and you cannot tell which set you hold until the other lands. So the second check also stops a measurement taken against your own artefact from being reported as a property of the system. bun run cat beans:claim <id> — how it behaves . scripts/claim-bean.ts builds the status change as a commit of its OWN and pushes it, so a sibling sees the claim immediately instead of when your PR opens. bun run cat beans:claim <bean-id> # store defaults to the CURRENT directory's checkout bun run cat beans:claim <bean-id> --dry-run # say what would happen . Run it from the checkout doing the work. The command resolves the checkout’s top level, prints claiming from <tree> (branch <b>), and refuses with exit 5 when that checkout is on the default branch or detached — the signature of the wrong tree — naming the tree it was about to write to. Pass --repo <worktree> from elsewhere; --any-branch overrides for a claim that really is made from there. It is a claim only — never your work: a claim bundled with work cannot be pushed until the work is ready. It also writes the same status into your copy of the work item, so a branch still carrying todo does not revert the claim at merge time; it does not commit that. It builds the commit in a detached git worktree, so a session mid-edit is not asked to accept a checkout, and removes it on every path including failure. Read the outcome, because three of the seven are refusals: . | outcome | exit | what it means | . | pushed | 0 | claimed; every session sees it | . | already-claimed | 0 | a sibling holds it, and is named. Nothing written — pick another item | . | held-unknown | 4 | in-progress there, and nobody recorded a holder. Nothing written. It cannot tell a live sibling from a claim abandoned days ago, so it refuses and says so — read the work item and the open PR list before taking it | . | already-closed | 0 | it is completed or scrapped there. Not claimed, deliberately — reviving finished work, and especially a scrapped work item whose purpose is recording a rejected approach, is a decision rather than a side effect of asking to claim | . | new-on-branch | 0 | the work item is not in the shared store yet, so nobody can see it and there is nothing to race over. Claim locally and open the PR early | . | fell-back | 3 | the push was REJECTED. The work item is not claimed anywhere a sibling can see — claim on your branch and open the PR at your first commit | . | unknown | 2 | the store could not be read. Never “the bean is free” | . held-unknown is common: any work item set in-progress with beans update instead of beans:claim, or hand-edited, carries no holder. Its exit code is 4, distinct from 0 (which already-claimed uses to say pick another item) and from 2 (the store was read perfectly well). fell-back is to be expected. Whether a direct push is accepted cannot be determined from inside an agent session (GET /branches/main/protection answers 403, and git push --dry-run does not run receive hooks), so the tool attempts and handles the rejection, loudly. A non-fast-forward is retried — another claim landed first, and the retry may discover the work item is now theirs, which is the correct answer rather than a conflict to force past. Two sessions choosing the same work is a different failure from two concurrent PRs going green alone and red together; the latter is about merging concurrent work.

2499bdb435ee.title: Lifecycle of a coordinated work item
2499bdb435ee.content: Several agent sessions run in parallel against the same repo, each in its own claude/* branch and ephemeral container. Without discipline they duplicate work, clobber each other’s queues, or resolve items a sibling is mid-flight on. Work items are the shared substrate. | Prime — at session start read the current work-plan (beans prime + beans list, or the CLI-independent fallback that parses beans/ directly). Know what is open and what siblings are touching. | Declare intent + claim — before starting, claim the work item via bun run cat beans:claim <id>, which records your holder note and pushes immediately to the branch store so siblings see it globally. When the work item is for a process step (code-change-review, merge-train, crdm-requirements, etc.), start or resume its workflow instance with workflow_start (--bean <id>) so the work item is placed on its current BPMN step (process-state.md). | Work — keep the work item current; advance the workflow instance with workflow_complete as each step finishes; append status notes as you go to a work item only your branch is changing. When other open pull requests are adding to the same work item, write a note instead — §”Adding to a bean — a note, not an append” below. Do not fork it into a parallel todos/*.json queue — link to any bulk queue from the work item instead. | Hand off or finish — on landing, close the work item, complete its workflow instance (or run bun run cat workflow:instances --sweep to close stale instances on closed work items), and update any cross-repo ownership note. If you stop mid-flight, leave the work item in-progress with a note saying where you got to, so the next session resumes instead of re-deriving. A work item abandoned silently is indistinguishable from one nobody started. | . An unclaimed work item is fair game for any session; a claimed one is not. Respect sibling claims. Agents create and set in-progress; they do not take over the work another session is mid-flight on. Complete it in the PR’s own last commit . Mark the work item completed in the last commit of the PR that does its work. Do not wait for the merge: a completion committed after the merge, on a branch then re-created from the new main, is in no PR and is orphaned, so the work item still reads open and the next session is offered finished work. If the PR is abandoned, the work item reads done only on a branch that never lands. | The ## Done when items are ticked in that same commit, with the evidence, so the work item shows why it is complete, not just that it is. When the work item delivers requirement statements, those items ARE their success criteria, copied when the work item was made (todo-manager §”Working with Beans” 4), and the work item is in its requirement set’s workPlan — so ticking them is judging the criteria, and closing the last work item of a set is what moves the set toward delivered. | A work item whose Done-when is not yet all met stays open in that commit, with a note saying what is left; completing it to avoid an orphan would be the opposite error. | . bun run cat beans:landed reports what slipped through: open, non-epic work items named in a merged PR’s title on main, those with every Done-when item ticked listed first. It reports and never closes; closing is still on evidence, per the next section.

cb1c809ea802.title: Adding to a bean — a note, not an append
cb1c809ea802.content: When more than one open pull request has something to add to the same work item, each writes a NOTE, never an append to the work item. bun run cat beans:note <bean-id> --title "Finding 3: ruling and after state" --body "…" git add beans/notes/ # the note AND the regenerated index . That writes <bean-id>--<YYYY-MM-DD>--<branch>.md in the declared notes directory of beans/beans.json, and rewrites the generated index beside it (README.md). The work item itself is not touched. Appending from several PRs puts every other open PR in conflict on that one file, and the merge-main bot refuses a work item conflict on purpose: two sessions editing one work item is a coordination question, not a regeneration, so the shared write is what has to go. The branch is the key, and that is the rule that must not drift. Two open pull requests never share a branch, and the branch is known at the first commit, which a pull request number is not. A second note from the same branch is a new ## section in that branch’s own file — found by its front matter, not by today’s date — so only that branch ever writes it. A date-plus-finding name would collide when two sessions work the same finding on the same day. Reasoning in full: cat-harness/schemas/sdlc/bean-note.ts. What still conflicts, and why that is acceptable. The index is rewritten by every pull request that adds a note, so two of them conflict on it. Its rows all sit inside one <!-- bean-notes:begin --> region, so the declared readme-generated-regions pattern resolves it without a person and regen rewrites it from the merged notes. The notes themselves never conflict. cat-harness-tools/scripts/tests/bean-notes.test.ts merges two real branches to show both halves, and fails when the branch is dropped from the name. What beans:notes:check judges (in CI): every file in the directory is a folio-bean-note/v1 note naming a work item that exists, under exactly the name its own front matter derives (a hand-named note is the first step back to two pull requests writing one path), and the index is current. | The work item’s own body stays the owner’s. Re-scoping it, ticking its ## Done when, or closing it are still edits to the work item, made by whoever holds it. | A note does not move the work item’s updated_at, because bumping it from every pull request is the one-line conflict notes remove. A reader asking “is anyone working on this?” reads the index’s dates as well as the work item’s. | Sections appended before the convention stay where they are. Moving them would rewrite the region every still-open pull request is appending to. | .

b90410b64867.title: Closing a bean whose work has already landed (STRICT)
b90410b64867.content: A work item verified done and left open is as misleading as one abandoned silently: an agent that picks it up re-derives work already on main. A rule that says only who may not close a work item leaves nobody able to discharge it. So: a work item closes on EVIDENCE, not on authorship. You may close any work item — whoever opened it — when you have re-run the measurement yourself and it passes. You may not close one because a note in it says somebody else measured it. Three obligations come with that: . | Re-derive, never quote. The note claiming resolution is the thing under suspicion; reading it is not verification. Run the check, then record the command and its result in the work item, because notes claiming resolution do fail re-verification. Where a note gives a line number or a count, verify the fact — line numbers rot. | A Done-when only a person can satisfy is not yours to discharge — for example “the issue can be closed by its author”; an agent never closes an issue on its own say-so. | Mid-flight is still off limits. This governs work that has landed. A work item a sibling is actively working — a claim naming a branch, a recent note, an open PR — is theirs, finished or not. | . Verified-done and still not closable? Say why, with an expiry, in the shape bean-blocking.md requires of a block: an exception that carries no way to re-derive it is indistinguishable from an oversight. Stopping because you are blocked is a different state with its own requirements — what it waits on, since when, an expiry and a handoff: bean-blocking.md. Reconciling closes in bulk — and an owner’s reopen outranks your evidence . A sweep that closes many work items on evidence (patch-ids on main from branch-archaeology, a gate that now passes, commits naming the work item) is these same three obligations applied per row. It adds one of its own: the owner may have moved work items from completed back to todo or in-progress because the earlier close was not good enough, and those work items can still carry a close(<id>) commit on main. Before closing, read the work item’s own status history (git log -p --follow -- beans/defs/<file>, plus the archive). If it was closed and later reopened, it is not closable on any evidence that predates the reopen. Read the reopen note. Close it only with evidence that answers that note’s reason and is newer than it. If there is no such evidence, list it as “reopened by the owner — evidence does not answer the reopen” and leave it. The same holds in reverse: evidence that a completed work item did not land (its commits absent from main under every test in branch-archaeology §1) is a finding to report, not a licence to reopen it on the agent’s own say-so, unless the owner has asked for that sweep. Re-derive from the REMOTE, never from your checkout (STRICT) . Where you read the evidence from is part of the evidence. Getting it wrong produces a finding that is confident, specific and false — for example “this file has no such code” read from a checkout branched before the commit that added it. A branch older than the claim. Grepping the working tree answers “is this in MY base”, which is a different question from “does this exist”. Ask the remote: git show origin/main:<path>, git log origin/main -- <path>. Never grep over the checkout to prove an absence. A fetch in the same compound command is not a barrier. git fetch -q origin main && git cat-file -e origin/main:<path> looks airtight and is not: sibling sessions merge every few minutes, so the ref can be stale when read. Fetch, then read in a separate command, and re-read before publishing. A file that exists only on an open PR’s head. When the claim is “nobody has built this”, check the open branches too, with the open-work-lookup Tool: a path, a prefix or a work item id, against main and every open PR head (see also bean-drain). The cost is asymmetric, which is why this is STRICT. A missed finding is a work item that stays open one more day. A false one about a sibling’s work is a correction, a retraction, and a reader who now trusts the next finding less. When you cannot re-derive it yourself — ready-to-close . Re-derivation is not always available: the measurement may need a running deployment, a branch this container does not have, or a judgement the owner reserved. Without an exit, leave it open is what an agent picks every time, and the work item costs a session of confusion on every sweep. The third state: tag the work item ready-to-close, quote under a ## Evidence heading what you DID verify, and say in one line what you could not re-derive and why. The owner confirms the batch. It is a tag, not a status, because the status vocabulary belongs to the third-party CLI: . $ beans update <id> --status ready-to-close Error: invalid status: ready-to-close (must be in-progress, todo, draft, completed, scrapped) $ beans update <id> --tag ready-to-close Updated <id> . and BeanStatusSchema in schemas/tools/tool-types.ts is defined as “exactly what beans update --status accepts”, so a sixth status here would desync the schema from the tool it documents. bun run cat check:ready-to-close lists every tagged work item with its evidence, so the confirmation is one read. It reports and never acts — deletion-requires-confirmation.md — unless the owner has waived the bean-close gate for this session or process run, in which case the batch closes under that waiver and the turn report names it: confirmation-waiver.md. It is not a parking space. ready-to-close says re-derivation is beyond this session; it never says I would rather not. Where you can run the check, run it and close the work item.

c269f9ff7a80.title: Where a sibling session is visible from (STRICT)
c269f9ff7a80.content: Sibling sessions can be listed (list_sessions gives each one’s id, title, branch and a task summary), which is enough to see WHO overlaps you before you write anything. They cannot reliably be reached: each sibling is its own cloud container, and messaging one may be refused. Seeing a sibling is not reaching one; what you commit is the only thing that arrives. A session is an ephemeral container, and nothing about it survives the container except what it committed. The Claude-Session: trailer on a commit is therefore the ONLY durable session identity this repository has, and a branch tip is the only durable statement of where a session got to. A sibling’s state is INFERRED, and the inference has a boundary . | what the trailer and the branches DO tell you | what they do NOT | . | which commits a session authored | whether it is running now | . | when it started and stopped committing | whether it is blocked, thinking, or gone | . | which branches carry its work, and its latest subject | what it intends to do next | . “Stopped committing” is not “finished”, and it is not “abandoned”. Treat a recent tip as a live claim, treat silence as a question, and ask — never as licence. One command, not a procedure . bun run cat sessions --since 4h . The sibling-sessions Tool node (tools/sibling-sessions/) does this, so every session counts the same way. It reads all branches, because a sibling’s work is on ITS branch. A window with no commits exits non-zero rather than reporting “no siblings”: a sweep over nothing has not found anything. Before creating or claiming, look . | The checkout is a snapshot. A container fetched main when it started, and everything merged since is invisible until it fetches again. | beans create is not idempotent and dedupes on nothing. The existence check in todo-manager §”Check before you create” reads the LOCAL store, so it cannot catch a duplicate a sibling created since, and the cost of not looking is duplicates somebody scraps one at a time. | . So before creating a work item for a decision, or claiming one, do both: . git fetch origin main bun run cat sessions --since 4h . The second is the one that gets skipped, and it answers who else is on this right now.

8b386404965f.title: A quiet claim — what in-progress does NOT tell you
8b386404965f.content: blocked has an expiry (bean-blocking.md); in-progress has nothing, so it carries no information about activity, and a reader cannot tell a stalled agent from a claim nobody has thought about since a bulk edit. The signal is liveness, not elapsed time . A claim is LIVE when something outside the work item says so: an open PR naming it, an unmerged branch touching it, or a note since. A claim with none of those has announced nothing to anybody — and a claim that announces nothing does not reserve anything. Elapsed time is the fallback, not the rule, because it is what a tool can compute offline. bun run cat health reports bean-quiet-claims at 72 hours since updated_at, alongside bean-claimed as the denominator. Its count is an upper bound: a work item it lists may have an open PR the sweep cannot see. Read it as “check these”, never as “take these”. Who may act . | Any session may TAKE a quiet claim — check for a liveness signal first; if there is none, work it, and say in the work item that you took it and what you found. This is the unclaimed case, reached by a different route. | Nothing re-statuses it automatically. The check reports; a person or the session taking the work acts. A tool that flipped in-progress back to todo would destroy the one record of who was where. | Quiet is not evidence of completion. Closing is governed by §”Closing a bean whose work has already landed”, and staleness is not evidence. A quiet claim on unfinished work goes back to the pool; it does not get closed. | . A stale claim is reset to todo, and the reset keeps the record . A claim untouched for weeks is not one anybody is honouring, but it still tells every sibling “taken”. A claim with no liveness signal (§”The signal is liveness”) AND no commit naming the work item or touching its branch in 14 days may be reset to todo by a sweep, provided the sweep appends a note recording what it reset. beans update <id> --status todo --body-append - <<'NOTE' _<UTC timestamp>_ — claim reset by stale-claim sweep: was `in-progress` since <date>, held by <branch / session from the holder note, or "no holder recorded">; no open PR, no unmerged branch naming it, no commit in 14 d. Re-claim with `bun run cat beans:claim`. NOTE . This does not contradict “nothing re-statuses it automatically”: the note keeps the record. The sweep is run by a session or the owner who has checked the network half (bun run cat check:quiet-claims), never by an unattended job. 14 days is the bean-stale-in-progress threshold in bun run cat health, so the two never drift apart. The reset never moves a work item to completed or scrapped, never touches an epic whose children are moving, and runs as one batch with a summary, under work-plan-restructure when it is more than a handful.

d4acc4392446.title: The branch store is the one every sibling reads (STRICT)
d4acc4392446.content: Work items live on the dedicated branch store (cat/cat-harness/beans), not committed to main or held on unmerged feature branches, where a review of the store sees none of them. | Push work items directly to the branch store. Newly created work items, epics and Done-whens are pushed (bun cat-harness-tools/scripts/branch-store.ts push --id beans) as soon as the plan exists, so the work plan is immediately visible to all agents. | A sweep reads the branch store, and also sweeps open branches that still carry work item files from before the branch store, so no session is blind to current goals and claims. | .

0b2bf12aab87.title: Each bean has one home (STRICT)
0b2bf12aab87.content: Each work item lives in exactly one store, because copies of one work item written separately drift apart: . | Work item | Its one home | . | cat-tools-*, and the work items the tools layer took when it split off | beans/defs on main of https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools | . | folio-core-*, and the work items the core content layer took | beans/defs on main of https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant-core | . | every other work item | litlfred/folio-assistant, branch cat/cat-harness/beans | . litlfred/cat-harness’s own cat/cat-harness/beans branch keeps its notes, queue, surveys and workflows, but no work item files. Write a work item change once, to its home, and nowhere else. From a cat-harness checkout that means fetching the folio-assistant branch, not this repository’s. The tools hold the rule too: state:push refuses to write a work item file to the retired branch (deleting one is allowed), beans:claim there names the home instead of reporting the work item missing, and bun run cat check:bean-one-home fails when any work item id is in two stores or in the retired one. Run it after editing work items by hand. The table it reads is https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools/blob/main/scripts/lib/bean-homes.ts.

746dbd11cf3d.title: Which copy is canonical — work-plan/skills/work-plan/
746dbd11cf3d.content: This file. LOCAL_PACKAGES (built in scripts/skill-packages.ts) is the table skill_fetch serves from, so an agent asking for this skill by name receives this file. When this skill or the installer changes, work-plan/skills/work-plan/ is what a downstream repo syncs from, and the generated mirror under the docs site follows it automatically. On landing a coordination change that affects a downstream repo, update that repo’s ownership note and close the tracking work items.

ab42537c997e.title: Issues are a third todo source — queryable issue: link
ab42537c997e.content: beans/ (agent work plan) and todos/ (human items and feedback) are the two stores declared in the repository. GitHub issues are a third source, carrying external tracking, stakeholder adjudication, cross-repo visibility, and human decisions. A work item can link directly to its corresponding GitHub issue via the front-matter issue: field: . --- title: 'ISSUES ARE A THIRD TODO SOURCE: queryable bean-issue link' status: in-progress type: feature issue: 730 --- . The issue: field is typed as z.union([z.number().int().positive(), z.string().min(1)]).optional(), supporting numeric issue numbers (issue: 730), issue shorthand (issue: "#730"), or fully-qualified issue URLs (issue: "https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/730"). When an issue is owed . Work items representing substantive roadmap scope or human adjudication owe an issue: . | Features (type: feature): features deliver user-facing capabilities or major roadmap changes, so they require an external tracking issue for stakeholder visibility and acceptance. | Stakeholder adjudication: any work item requiring human adjudication, policy rulings, or cross-team consensus (flagged via issue-required or needs-issue tags, or explicit adjudication requirements in the body) owes an issue link so the discussion and ruling remain discoverable. | . The check bun run cat check:bean-issues audits the work item store to verify that work items owing an issue provide either an issue: front-matter link or an issue reference in the work item body (#<number>, issue #<number>, or issue URL). It reports compliant work items alongside findings for unlinked items under 3-state reporting (0 = pass, 1 = finding, 2 = could not determine).

2aa8cc55db56.title: Disambiguation (do not conflate)
2aa8cc55db56.content: . | work items = the agent’s session work-plan (beans/, this skill). | todos = the human work-plan items (todos/). | issues = the third todo source (issue: front-matter field), carrying human/stakeholder adjudication and external tracking. | sidecars (*.qa.json, *.witness.json) = content state tracking. Work items ≠ sidecars. Do not convert QA / witness queue items into individual work items (see todo-manager.md disambiguation block). | A sibling session sharing this store (this skill) ≠ an agent in another environment you hand ONE task to, which you cannot see and which a person may relay to: agent-handoff. That covers who writes which work item, where the receiver reports, the one line the person pastes, and why the receiver’s own measurement is evidence rather than the close. | .

A stub of the same name lives at .claude/skills/local and is published as bean-coordination (local stub); it only points here. Edit this page’s source, never the stub.

99de8fe9930d.title: Bean drain
99de8fe9930d.content: A drain is the delivery loop run over a queue instead of over one item. Each work item in it still goes through the ordinary lifecycle (bean-coordination, todo-manager, continual-progress). What this skill adds is what goes wrong only when several agents drain the same store at once: two of them starting the same work item. The drain is drawn as a process: Process_BeanDrain (sdlc/processes/bean-drain.bpmn). It builds the queue (the drain-queue Tool), then for each work item calls OPEN (Process_BeanOpen, whose check is the bean-claim-check Tool), works it, calls CLOSE (Process_BeanClose), and refills. The steps below are the same loop in prose.

6ba51b5b4a71.title: Roles
6ba51b5b4a71.content: | role | does | holds | . | queue keeper | builds the queue, assigns work items to drainers, refills a drainer that runs dry | the queue file | . | drainer | takes the next work item from its own list, checks, claims, works, closes | the work items it claimed | . One agent can be both. Drainers are cloud threads and agents on the owner’s own machine, side by side. Each one is told apart by its commit author on the work item branch, never by its own say-so: . | agent | commit author on the work item branch | . | cloud threads | Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>, or litlfred <litlfred@users.noreply.github.com> | . | agy, the owner’s local Antigravity agent | Carl Leitner <litlfred@fenugreek.home> | . | the state bot | folio-state-bot | . A new kind of agent joins this table when it starts committing. An author not in the table is treated as “another agent”.

2d0fc10ae732.title: Spawning drainers
2d0fc10ae732.content: A queue keeper that starts drain threads seeds each one as coordinate §”A spawned helper is reachable, and the owner’s authority is not relayed” says: the owner’s words verbatim, no relayed rulings (a merge window included), and a finishable list. Give each drainer this skill and its list, not a copy of the rules. Three further rules: work leaves up (a parent closes when its last child does), one PR per work item or tight cluster, and scrap obsolete work items with reasons.

a79c002ff049.title: 1. Build the queue — the drain-queue Tool
a79c002ff049.content: Read every work item store, not the one this checkout mounts. Each work item has one home (bean-coordination §”Each bean has one home”): the cat/cat-harness/beans branch on folio-assistant, plus the tools and core layers’ work items on their main. The cat-harness copy of that branch keeps no work items. If two stores ever hold the same id again, bun run cat check:bean-one-home names it; the newest updated_at wins here and the disagreement is listed, so somebody can fix it. Leave out, each with its reason in the output so nothing vanishes silently: . | goals and epics (milestone, epic): they close when their children do; | blocked: a work item in blocked_by that is still open (bean-blocking); | closed or not ready: completed, scrapped, draft; | owner-held or parked: the last note says it waits on the owner, a date or a ruling; | not drainable here: it needs something the drainers lack (a network host, a person’s account). Route it to an agent that has it instead, and say which. | . Group the rest by owner (the thread or agent that already holds work in the same area), in priority order, and write the result to one shared file. Mark the work items other agents hold as skip. Refill a drainer from the deepest queue when it finishes, and refresh the file each time. The queue is advisory. It says who should take a work item; only a claim says who did. So a drainer still runs step 2 on every work item it takes from the queue.

ee6308d3a5df.title: 2. Before each bean: check, then claim — the bean-claim-check Tool
ee6308d3a5df.content: Run this before any work on the work item, including reading code for it. The trigger is starting work, not claiming (bean-coordination §”The trigger is STARTING WORK”). | Fetch every copy, in its own command: git fetch origin cat/cat-harness/beans. A fetch in the same compound command as the read is not a barrier (bean-coordination §”Re-derive from the REMOTE”). | Read the last commits on the work item’s file, per copy: git log -3 --format='%an %cI %s' FETCH_HEAD -- 'beans/defs/*<id>--*'. Skip the work item if another agent committed to it in the past 24 hours, or its last note says it is claimed. | Look for open work naming the work item: an open PR whose title, body or branch names the id, in every repository the drain touches — the open-work-lookup Tool. Skip if one exists and is not yours. This catches a duplicate that exists only on an open PR’s head, which step 2 cannot see. | Claim: set status: in-progress, append a dated note naming you and your session, and make a plain commit on every copy. Push it before any other commit of yours, so the next agent’s step 2 sees it. | A rejected push means somebody wrote first: fetch, rebase, re-read the work item, and go back to step 2. Never force-push a work item branch. | . status: in-progress alone is not a claim you can trust. It goes stale (§”A quiet claim” in bean-coordination), so steps 2 and 3 read activity, not status. Why plain commits, and why on every copy. bun run cat state:push and bun run cat beans:claim write the one copy the checkout points at. With more than one copy, the others go on saying todo. So while there is more than one copy, a drainer edits work items with plain git commits on each, and never with state:push. Where a work item has one copy, beans:claim is the claim.

ba59323bb8a3.title: 3. Work it
ba59323bb8a3.content: . | Open the PR at the first commit, with Closes-bean: <id> in the body (continual-progress, pr-description). An open PR is the claim every other agent can see without the work item branch. | Add the PR’s link to the work item with a dated note, on every copy. | Work only the work item you claimed. A cause you find inside it that is a separate piece of work becomes a new work item, and is checked and claimed in its own right. | .

c1314a3b03f3.title: 4. When the bean waits on the owner
c1314a3b03f3.content: Ask through ask-the-person: the full question and every option in the chat first, then the card. Record the question’s link in the work item. Keep the claim while the question is open, and take the next work item meanwhile. A work item that will wait long goes back to todo with the question recorded, so that it does not hold the queue. When the question is about changed pages, it carries the staging preview: one deep link per changed page, with the same page on main, in the output contract’s stagingLinks field (staging-review §”The deep-link rule”).

cf5624f3ecff.title: 5. Close it, and refill
cf5624f3ecff.content: Close on evidence (bean-coordination §”Closing a bean whose work has already landed”), on every copy. Then tell the queue keeper, or take the next work item on your list. A drainer whose list is empty asks for a refill instead of picking from another owner’s list.

b5fe832156d7.title: Tools
b5fe832156d7.content: | Tool | answers | contract | . | drain-queue | which open work items, grouped by owner, with what was left out and why | definitions.queue in the output schema | . | bean-claim-check | may I take this work item; if so, claim it on every copy | definitions.claimCheck | . | open-work-lookup | does a path, a path prefix or a work item id appear on main or any open PR head, and where | definitions.lookup | . Run from an index checkout, with one --copy per work item copy checkout: . bun run cat beans:drain-queue --copy folio-assistant --copy cat-harness --holdings holdings.json bun run cat beans:claim-check <id> --copy folio-assistant --copy cat-harness \ --repo litlfred/cat-harness --repo <tools-layer-repo> --session <your session link> bun run cat lookup:open-work --bean <id> --repo litlfred/cat-harness # or --path / --prefix . Pass one --repo per repository the work item’s work can land in — for example the harness and its tools layer. --dry-run on the claim check says what it would do and writes nothing. --json on any of them emits the contract below. The claim check exits 0 when claimed, 1 on a skip and 2 when it could not tell; 2 is never “free”. The Tools satisfy bean-coordination rather than this skill: this skill’s contract is the whole drain, and each Tool takes one step of it.

b86183a104da.title: Input and output
b86183a104da.content: The contract is input.schema.json and output.schema.json. | In: the work item copies to read, the agents and how each is recognised, the owners’ current holdings, the windowHours (24) and the queueFile. | Out: the queue (by owner, excluded with reasons, copies that disagree), one claimCheck per work item taken, and what each drainer closed or asked. | .

73029f482eb0.title: /before-after-preview — show the reviewer the change, not a description of it
73029f482eb0.content: Skill id: before-after-preview · Package: sdlc-core · Worked example: the Folio tab . continual-progress holds that a human cannot assess a rendered artefact from a description of it. rendered-verification adds that the agent that wrote the change cannot either. This skill is about what goes to the reviewer: a before/after preview that is a fair comparison, carries a number, and can be read without opening anything else. It covers every content type this platform renders.

cfd4f9d5e7af.title: How this sits beside its neighbours
cfd4f9d5e7af.content: This skill does not replace any of these. It tells you which one to use. | skill | what it answers | use it for | . | rendered-verification | does it work? — the agent checks in a browser | the tools: computed style, hit tests, pageerror, and asserting that the page actually loaded its styles | . | visual-diff | how much of this figure changed? | automatic pixel pictures of changed blocks on a folio’s review page | . | staging-review | where do I look? | the before (main) and after (staging) URL pairs, and what to review at each | . | this skill | is the reviewer’s comparison fair, measured and findable? | the preview itself, for any content type, and where it fits in the processes | . If the change is a folio block and the staging job already made its pictures, link to those. Use this skill for everything the job cannot make: page chrome, behaviour on scroll, a PDF page, an IG page, a slide. A staging “after” is not permanent. gh-pages keeps at most ten branches/<slug>/ previews and rotates the least recently updated off, so a link in a preview can 404 days later while the PR is still open. The next push to the branch re-stages it. Where the comparison must outlive that, publish the captures themselves (§6) rather than only the staging URL. Detail: staging-review §”The cap”. Which pages to picture. For a Change Set, the pages come from its rendered list (skill rendered-impact), so the “k of n pages changed” count is the list’s count, not one made by hand. Its unconfirmed content pages (bytes unchanged, content loaded in the browser) are exactly the ones a screenshot settles.

0b64c1acee38.title: The rule
0b64c1acee38.content: A reviewer is shown a rendered change as a before/after pair. Each pair comes from ONE build with ONE variable, is captured stably, is paired with a measured count and its method, and has a status line saying what it is and what was not checked. Each pair is introduced by a narrative: a sentence or two, in plain words, on what a reader will now see or do differently and why. The narrative comes first, above the pictures. A pair without it makes the reviewer play spot-the-difference, and the difference they find first is not always the one that changed: a re-render shifts anti-aliasing, a merge brings in somebody else’s edit. Name the change so the reviewer looks for it, then let the pair confirm it. If any part is missing, say so in the preview. Never drop a missing part silently. Build only the cone. For any rendered kind, the “after” build need only cover what the change can reach: its own files, its generator’s import closure, and what is derived from those. That is the general rule, written once in feature-staging §7. Anything the cone leaves out is identical to the “before” by construction, so leaving it out loses no comparison.

c530eb6cbbbe.title: 1. One build, one variable
c530eb6cbbbe.content: The only difference between the two pictures should be the change under review. In order of preference: . | The same build, with the change toggled. Render once and make “before” by switching the change off in place. The usual way is injected CSS that hides the new element, reverts a rule, or removes a class. Everything else stays identical, including the build, the theme, the fonts, the data and the viewport. | Two builds made with identical tooling, one of the base commit and one of the head commit. Use this when the change cannot be toggled, for example generated markup, a different PDF, or a new IG page. Use git worktree add <dir> origin/main --detach and symlink the installed dependencies (see rendered-verification §”A before/after pair beats an after”). Say in the preview that there are two builds, with both SHAs. | A local build against a published one. Only if nothing else is possible, and the preview must say so in its first line. The published side used different tooling. On the docs site, for example, the pinned remote_theme differs from the local theme gem. Any difference in the pictures may come from that and not from the change. | . Record which of the three you used. It is the first line of the status line in section 5.

cfbec3092d8f.title: 2. Stable capture — load everything, then check the two shots line up
cfbec3092d8f.content: A pair captured while the page is still settling compares two moments, not two versions. Do all of these before either shot: . | Force lazy media to eager: document.querySelectorAll('img[loading=lazy],iframe[loading=lazy]').forEach(e => e.loading = 'eager'). | Scroll the whole page once, top to bottom and back, so anything that loads on intersection has loaded. | Wait for network idle (page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')) and for document.fonts.ready. | Turn smooth scrolling off: document.documentElement.style.scrollBehavior = 'auto'. Otherwise a scrollTo returns before the page has moved. | Assert the shots line up: scrollY must be equal in both, and so must the getBoundingClientRect().top of a reference element outside the change, such as a heading. If either differs, the shots are invalid. Retake them. Do not caption around the mismatch. | . Lazy images that load between the before and after shots move the text, so the two pictures show different content at the same scroll offset and still look plausible. The reference-element check catches this; looking at the pictures does not.

c51cc15489a1.title: 3. Measure, don’t just show
c51cc15489a1.content: A picture shows one position. A count shows all of them. Send both, and name the method so the reviewer can repeat it or dispute it. | Choose a question that has a yes/no answer at one position. For example: “is body text visible beside the handle?”, “does the caption overflow the slide?”, “is this IG table wider than the viewport?”. | Ask it at many positions: scroll steps, pages, slides, or viewports. Report the result as k of n, before and after. | Measure from the rendered geometry. For text overlap, collect Range client rects of the text nodes, intersect them with the element’s getBoundingClientRect(), and confirm each hit with document.elementFromPoint at the overlap. A rect intersection alone counts text that is painted underneath. | State the step size and the viewport with the numbers. | . Folio tab, platform.html, 19 scroll positions at 1280×900: text visible beside the handle at 16 of 19 positions before, 0 of 19 after. At 390×844: 18 of 20 before, 0 of 20 after. A second table used 97 px steps across four page and viewport pairs: platform 1280 9/21 → 0, platform 390 32/39 → 0, index 1280 25/50 → 0, cat-harness/index 390 36/60 → 0. Treat a count the same way as any other measurement. Validate the method on a known positive and a known negative before trusting it (rendered-verification §”A COUNT over the built site needs its instrument validated first”).

666850962bd8.title: 4. Several viewports, and both schemes when colour is involved
666850962bd8.content: At least: . | viewport | size | why | . | desktop | 1280×900 | the layout most authors write in | . | phone | 390×844 | fixed and sticky elements, narrow columns, overflow | . Add light and dark whenever the change touches colour, contrast, a border or an image with transparency. Switch the scheme with the real control (on the docs site that is jtd.setTheme, not an attribute set by hand) and check that the switch took effect before shooting. Show a pair for each combination that matters. Give the count for every combination you measured.

43f7621da34d.title: 5. Honest status — one line, at the top
43f7621da34d.content: Status: <committed | pushed | in PR #N | merged> at <sha> · Build: <one build, toggled | base <sha> vs head <sha>, same tooling | local vs published> · Not checked: <what, and why> . “Not checked” is required and is never empty without a reason. Typical entries: . | local theme gem vs the pinned remote theme; | dark mode; | a browser other than Chromium; | print CSS; | the IG Publisher’s full build (only sushi ran); | the PPTX was not rendered, only its geometry was reconstructed. | . A preview that looks complete but hides an unchecked axis is a false green.

3b49140f0549.title: 6. Publishing — a private page, updated in place
3b49140f0549.content: . | Where: a private web page. Use the Artifact tool when it is available. It holds the pairs, the counts, the method, the status line and links to the PR and the issue. Update the same page as the work moves on, so the link in the PR body stays current. Do not post a new page for each round. Where no page can be published, attach the images to the turn and to the PR comment instead. | Alt text on every image, saying what the reader should see. For example: “Before, phone, scrolled 1200 px: the Folio tab covers the first three words of each line”. Do not write “before screenshot”. A preview without alt text cannot be used by a reviewer with a screen reader. | Label each pair in words, not only with position or colour: “Before” and “After”, then viewport and scheme. | Committed evidence: do not commit screenshots to the repository. The page and the PR are the record. visual-diff’s pictures are built by CI and are not committed either. | . The Folio tab preview was published this way as a private artifact page, with the before/after pairs, the counts above, the method and the PR link.

8a873081dbf5.title: 7. By content type
8a873081dbf5.content: The discipline above is the same for every type. What changes is how you build it, what one “position” is, and what you toggle. Docs site (Jekyll, just-the-docs) . | Build: bun run cat preview:site. Its header explains how its output differs from CI’s: the local theme gem, not the pinned remote_theme. | Serve under the baseurl. Symlink <serve>/folio-assistant -> <build> and serve the parent directory. Served at /, every stylesheet returns 404 and the page still renders, unstyled. | For theme chrome, take the real CI build from gh-pages (rendered-verification §”The REAL build is reachable”). | Toggle: inject CSS into the one build. | Position: a scroll step (for example 97 px) or a page. | . The worked example is the Folio tab. The fixed “Folio” handle covered body text as the page scrolled. The capture used one preview:site build of commit 438268976. “Before” was made by injecting .fa-glass-band{visibility:hidden!important}, so the new strip was the only difference. The capture forced lazy images to eager, scrolled the page once, turned smooth scrolling off, and checked that scrollY was equal in both shots. The counts are in section 3. Papers (LaTeX → PDF) . | Build: the paper render path. See build-pdf (the science layer) and the paper_render_pdf tool, or document_render_pdf for a document folio with no TeX. Build base and head with the same TeX Live and the same class files. A PDF cannot be toggled in place, so this is always case 2 of section 1. | Page images: rasterise with pdftoppm -r 110 -png or mutool draw when present (check with command -v). Otherwise render the pages with pdf.js in Chromium. paper_preview opens a rendered PDF or HTML for a person to look at. It is for a human looking, not for capture. | Position: a page. Align pages by anchor, not by page number. An added paragraph shifts every later page. Pair the page that holds the changed label in each build. | Measure: changed pages k of n, overfull boxes and warnings from the log before and after, and page count. | A changed block’s own picture comes from visual-diff on the HTML render. Link it rather than taking it again. | . FHIR IGs (sushi, IG Publisher) . | Order: sushi must pass first. A red sushi run has no IG to preview. Then run the IG Publisher, and compare the rendered output/ pages (ig-publication (the FHIR IG layer), fhir-validation (the FHIR IG layer)). | Build: two builds with identical tooling. The Publisher jar floats to the latest release on every run, so record its version for both sides. If the versions differ, some differences in the pictures may come from the tool and not from the change. ig-incremental-build.bpmn’s restored-state assembly is fine for an authoring preview but is not the full build. Say which one you used. | Position: an output/ page such as StructureDefinition-*.html, a pagecontent page or artifacts.html. Pick the pages from the changed resources, not by browsing. | Measure: pages changed k of n. Also compare qa.json errors and warnings before and after. A preview that looks right with more QA errors is not an improvement. | . Slide decks (PPTX, ODP) . On a slide, layout carries meaning. What overlaps, what is cut off and what sits next to what is part of the message. | Render if you can. soffice --headless --convert-to pdf, then use the paper route for page images. Check with command -v soffice. The session that worked out this route had no LibreOffice in its container. | If you cannot render, reconstruct the geometry from the package XML. A .pptx is a zip file. | ppt/presentation.xml <p:sldSz cx cy> gives the slide size. | Each ppt/slides/slideN.xml shape has <a:off x y> and <a:ext cx cy>, in EMU (914400 per inch). | A shape with no <a:xfrm> inherits its geometry from its placeholder in slideLayoutN.xml, then from slideMasterN.xml. Follow the chain or the shape is missing. | For .odp, read content.xml svg:x/svg:y/svg:width/svg:height, which use units such as cm. | Draw the boxes as SVG with their text, before and after. Measure overlaps and boxes past the slide edge as k of n slides. | . | Status must say “geometry reconstructed, not rendered”. Fonts, autofit and text wrapping are not modelled, so text overflow inside a box is unchecked. | . Websites in general . | The docs-site method, without the Jekyll parts. Build base and head with the site’s own build, or toggle with injected CSS or JS in one build. Serve under the same path prefix the site is deployed at. | Everything in rendered-verification applies: styles actually loaded, pageerror count zero, and hit tests at the centre of controls. | Position: scroll steps, routes, or interaction states such as a menu open or a form in error. List the states you covered. | .

6d6782956c76.title: 8. In the review and feedback processes
6d6782956c76.content: When it is required. A preview is required before a rendered change is handed to anyone to judge: . | when the PR is opened for review; | at each round of author feedback; | at the HCI validation gate’s review. | . A non-rendered change needs none. Say so in one line, rather than attaching an empty preview. Who makes it. The agent that made the change, in its own lane. The reviewer’s lane reads the preview and does not build it. A reviewer who must build their own before/after has been handed a chore, not a review. Only the producing activities carry the skill ref, because a skill ref says the lane PERFORMS the skill and the lane’s role must carry it (role-carries-activity-skill). The reading activities name the preview in their documentation and carry no ref. | process (cat-harness/processes/) | activity | role | . | content-change-review.bpmn | Task_CommitPush | agent produces it with the first push (skill ref) | . | content-change-review.bpmn | Task_Iterate | agent refreshes it with each revision push, which bypasses Task_CommitPush (skill ref) | . | content-change-review.bpmn | Task_ReviewStaging | author reads it beside the staging URLs | . | content-change-review.bpmn | Task_CompareBeforeAfter | review committee reads it beside visual-diff | . | code-change-review.bpmn | Task_CommitAndOpenPR | agent produces it for a change to a rendered surface (skill ref) | . | code-change-review.bpmn | Task_Review | reviewer reads it | . | editing-hci-validation.bpmn | Task_DraftEdit, Task_ReviseEdit | agent produces it with the proposal, before Gateway_ValidationFork, so it exists when review starts (skill ref) | . | editing-hci-validation.bpmn | Task_SmeReview | human or SME reads it as an input to judgement | . Where it is linked. | PR body: the preview link and the status line, near the top. Also any count that settles the question. | Issue comment: each round’s summary on the issue carries the same link (issue-working). | Update the page in place, so both links stay current. | . Asking the reviewer. The question follows interaction-modality: context first, then options, then the recommendation, then the question. The choices are structured and easy to select, because some reviewers find typing hard. Put the preview link and the counts in the context, so the reviewer can answer without opening anything else. Recommended first: . | Looks right. Approve this preview. (recommended when the counts went to zero and nothing is unchecked) | Something is wrong at a position. Pick the pair by its label, for example “After, phone, 1200 px”. Adding a note is optional. | Check something not covered. Pick from the “Not checked” list. | Not now. | . Say what happens if they give no answer: the PR stays open and nothing merges. Merging still needs the explicit confirmation the processes require. How feedback becomes work. | A choice of 2 or 3, or a comment on the preview, becomes a work item with the pair’s label, the status line’s SHA and the position (todo-manager; check before you create). | On a folio, a comment tagged block: <label> on the PR becomes a review-comment/1.0.0 todo (review-comments). | Feedback on published content goes through content-feedback. | The next round’s preview answers each item. Take the same pair again and update the count. | .

6d59b4150235.title: What this does NOT do
6d59b4150235.content: . | It does not decide whether the change is right. It makes that decision possible to take at a glance. | It does not replace the gates, rendered-verification’s checks, or visual-diff’s pixel job. It uses them. | It is not a merge approval. A reviewer choosing option 1 has approved the preview, and the merge still needs its own confirmation. | .

355f57140b66.title: Processes that run this skill
355f57140b66.content: | process | step(s) that name it | . | Code change and review | Commit, push, open the PR | . | Make the content change | Commit, push, update PR | . | Content Change and Review | Iterate on author feedback | . | Editing and HCI validation | Draft the block edit; Revise the proposed change | . | L2 component edit and review | Render, stage, before/after | .

ebd888ffabd7.title: Benchmarking mode — reports across models, deliberately excluded from the KG
ebd888ffabd7.content: Skill id: benchmarking-mode · Package: sdlc-core . Benchmarking output is a report about model performance across configurations, not an assertion about the subject folio. Every other verdict this platform produces goes into a declared graph (test/results/ for the qa graph, test/attestations/ for attestations, test/health/results/ for health). Benchmarking output is a deliberate exception: it does not enter any declared graph, has no graph typology, and must never be committed to graph directories.

a5c98111abf0.title: The rule, and why it is not obvious
a5c98111abf0.content: Every QA review sidecar, witness file, and kg-qa verdict this project produces goes into a declared graph (test/results/, qa graph) precisely so that findings are addressable nodes in the repository’s knowledge graph. Do not declare a benchmark-results or benchmarks graph typology in cat-harness.json. The distinction is an ontological one: . |   | QA review mode | Benchmarking mode | . | What it asserts | Facts about the subject folio (e.g., voice compliance, translation fidelity, schema validity, structural correctness) | Facts about the model and runner configuration (e.g. prompt template, inference engine, context window, temperature, seed) at one point in time | . | Reproducibility across clones | Invariant across checkouts: the subject folio either passes or fails | Dependent on model availability, vendor versions, non-deterministic weights, and compute access | . | Graph status | Declared graph content (test/results/, qa graph, attestations graph) | Deliberately NOT graph content — excluded from all declared graphs | . | Output destination | test/results/**, test/attestations/** | build/benchmarks/ (default, gitignored) or reports/ (synthesized CRDM reports) | . | Audience & lifetime | Platform gates, CI verification, and release attestations | Model evaluation, verifiability studies, and CRDM requirements synthesis | . If benchmark metrics were admitted as KG nodes, the repository’s graph contents would depend on which model happened to execute the run. Two checkouts of the exact same commit running on different machines with different model backends would instantiate conflicting graphs.

ae2849059b5c.title: Where benchmark reports land
ae2849059b5c.content: Benchmark outputs land in locations that are never declared as graphTypologies entries: . | build/benchmarks/ (default for raw outputs and runs): All runner scripts (such as scripts/toc-benchmark.py and scripts/page-label-benchmark.py) default their file output to build/benchmarks/<tool>.json. Because build/ is gitignored across all folio and harness layouts, automated runs never dirty git status or pollute repository state. | reports/ (synthesized human-readable reports): When benchmark runs across multiple models or prompt strategies are synthesized into a publication or requirements analysis, the resulting document lives under reports/ (or CRDM analysis folders) as a standalone report document, not as a KG database node. The shape and contents of synthesized reports answer user needs defined by the CRDM process. | .

4de524752222.title: Enforcement: path guards against graph pollution
4de524752222.content: The isolation between benchmark execution and declared graphs is enforced by code, not left to good intentions: . | Runner defaults: Benchmark scripts default output paths into build/benchmarks/, never relative roots or graph roots. | Path guards: Both TypeScript (scripts/benchmark-guard.ts) and Python (scripts/_benchmark_guard.py) implement path verification against cat-harness.json. Any benchmark execution attempting to direct output into beans/, todos/, test/results/, library/, schemas/, skills/, or any other declared graph directory is rejected with an explicit refusal. | Path audit gates: scripts/tests/audit-output-paths.test.ts scans benchmark runners and pipeline scripts to ensure they never default into beans/, todos/, or declared graph roots. | .

21122d112b92.title: Sibling contrast: translation QA vs benchmarking
21122d112b92.content: The contrast with translation QA clarifies the boundary: . | Translation QA evaluates whether a translated document accurately renders the source. It is an assertion about the folio’s fidelity, and therefore joins the audited review record under test/results/. | Model benchmarking tests how well candidate models perform when inferring structures (e.g. table-of-contents extraction or page labeling) across a test bank. It is an evaluation of the models, not of the documents being processed, and therefore produces isolated reports in build/benchmarks/. | .

2b981cebbf60.title: What this skill does
2b981cebbf60.content: Every entry in content/schema/references.ts must be human-reviewed against its source. This skill manages that status and drives unreviewed references to validated.

ba968d82235e.title: 1. Audit — find unreviewed references
ba968d82235e.content: . | Read references.review.json. Any references.ts id whose effective status is not validated is flagged (absent ⇒ unreviewed by default). | An entry is stale when its entryHash (12-char SHA-256 prefix of the canonical-JSON-serialized references.ts entry) drifts — treat as unreviewed. | Automated check: cd content && bun run pipeline/validate-references-human-review.ts (content/ is its own Bun package) computes each entryHash, reads the sidecar, and flags every non-validated ref. Flags: --strict (exit 1 — CI gate, warn → strict), --json (machine output), --seed (list refs that would get a physical-review issue). Issue template: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bib-physical-review.md. | .

b60a6f7706b0.title: 2. Acquisition ladder (per flagged reference)
b60a6f7706b0.content: . | Source in uploads/ → identify the cited page/passage (agent-sourced; no human photo) → mark source-in-repo; hand to ingestion (§4). | Not in repo → acquire legally for uploads/ (open-access / arXiv / author copy), with author assistance if needed. | Paywalled / not digital → open a physical-review issue (§3); the author photographs the page(s) at a library. | .

0caa87f98f22.title: 3. GitHub issue (one per ref needing physical review)
0caa87f98f22.content: Create with template .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bib-physical-review.md. Assign the repo owner. Include, consistently readable: . | Bibliographic block: title, authors, year, journal/volume/pages, DOI, ISBN, library call number, holding library. | Project context: the citing block(s) (.md + label), formal-proof -- Ref: sites, the \cite{}/uses[] sites — with blob links. | What to verify: the specific theorem/section/equation relied on. | Labels: bib-physical-review, needs-photo, + chapter/domain tag. | Ask: author uploads a photo of the relevant page(s). | . Set the ref’s status to issue-open (source = issue#NNN).

ccafde556d86.title: 4. Hand-off to ingestion
ccafde556d86.content: When a photo is uploaded (or an in-repo passage is identified), the bib-photo-ingestion watcher (companion integration-watcher skill) runs: OCR → formalise the cited result (if the project has a formal-proof pipeline) → confirm the project’s usage matches the source → machine + agent bib validation → set status validated, record { by, date, source, page, entryHash }, refresh the sidecar, post back on the issue.

fcc863b8b367.title: Guardrails
fcc863b8b367.content: . | Never set validated without a human reviewer recorded in by. | The acquisition must be legal (open-access / library / author copy). | One reference per issue; keep GitHub noise low (only genuinely-unvalidated refs needing physical access get an issue). | .

e0412127ae49.title: bib-human-review

486d520b549b.title: bib-photo-ingestion-watcher
486d520b549b.content: The automation half of the bib-human-review workflow. Companion to the status sidecar content/schema/references.review.json.

beffe997d053.title: Trigger
beffe997d053.content: . | A photo is attached to a bib-physical-review GitHub issue (subscribe via mcp__github__subscribe_pr_activity / issue events), or | the bib-human-review skill has marked a reference source-in-repo (agent identifies the cited passage in uploads/ — no human photo needed). | .

c3a1d4720ce0.title: Pipeline (on a photo / identified passage)
c3a1d4720ce0.content: . | Read the source. OCR the photo (or read the uploads/ passage); extract the specific cited theorem/section/equation. | Source-match. Confirm the project’s usage matches the source statement — the .md claim, the \cite{}/uses[] sites, any formal-proof -- Ref:. Flag any mismatch back on the issue (do not auto-validate). | Formalise (if applicable). If the project has a formal-proof pipeline, place the formalised result in a per-paper package / namespace; if the project overlaps the paper’s result, wrap it (thin specialisation) rather than re-prove; where the paper is unformalised, state an axiom/class with a -- Ref: comment. Build against the restored proof cache (do not iterate blind; establish editor/LSP feedback first). | Bib-validate. DOI/metadata cross-check, validate-references, -- Ref: resolution, entryHash recompute. | Set status. On success set the ref validated, record { by, date, source, page, entryHash } in references.review.json, refresh the sidecar, and post the outcome on the issue. On failure, post the specific blocker (mismatch / unresolved DOI / formalisation gap) and leave status issue-open. | .

dc83c9632c1e.title: Guardrails
dc83c9632c1e.content: . | Never validated without a recorded human reviewer (by) — the photo upload is the human act; record the uploader. | Acquisition must be legal; never fetch paywalled PDFs by scraping. | One reference per issue; reply only with the outcome or a blocker (keep noise low). | .
