94f3f0f03a27.doc: Graph rendering: one set of rules for every drawn graph
94f3f0f03a27.title: Graph rendering: one set of rules for every drawn graph
94f3f0f03a27.content: Skill id: graph-rendering · Package: graph-management . One set of rules applies to every drawn graph, so that each drawing does not follow conventions of its own. This skill is the general part. It says what any drawing of a graph owes its reader. The per-graph skills say how one generator meets it: uml-overview for schemas, bpmn-authoring for processes, and content-graph for a folio’s blocks. A drawing is how a person READS a graph. graph-detanglement is how the graph is RESTRUCTURED, and it needs the drawing: a partition you cannot see is a partition you argue about from numbers alone.

a7d3866c1657.doc: Graph rendering: one set of rules for every drawn graph
a7d3866c1657.title: The ten rules
a7d3866c1657.content: The failure each rule prevents is stated beside it. | Draw from a declared graph, never by hand. Every node and edge in the picture is read from a source: a schema, a declaration, a BPMN file, a uses[] list, a dependency cache. A wrong picture is fixed at its source. A hand-edited diagram is overwritten on the next run, and a check fails while it is stale. | Groups are declared sub-graphs. A box around nodes is a named sub-graph (a directories[] entry, a chapter, a package), never a grouping the renderer invented. | No empty box without a reason. A node drawn with nothing in it reads as a rendering fault. A node with no fields to show carries one line saying why. A node whose shape could not be determined is drawn dashed, as a finding, never as a quiet empty shape. | Edge kinds are drawn distinctly and never merged. A graph has more than one kind of edge (edge-kinds-and-blast-radius). Editorial uses[] and a content type’s formal edges, enforced and prose-only references, and a field-carried link versus one declared elsewhere (the UML’s dashed bootstrap.processes:skill edge) each get their own line style and a legend. Merging two kinds into one line destroys the signal every metric on that graph is computed from. | Pick the layout engine by what the graph is, and write down why. See §”Layout engines” below. The choice is a claim with a measurement behind it, not a taste. | Offer two orientations from one source. A tall graph on a wide screen and a wide graph on a phone are both unreadable. Derive the second view from the first (landscapeOf in scripts/plantuml-render.ts) rather than keeping two sources that can drift apart. | Declare colour once. Colour a node by its family (for the UML: schema, scenario, process, state, test) in one stylesheet, and have every renderer read that stylesheet (uml-palette.ts). A second palette is a second answer free to disagree with the first. | Stamp the output with its source’s hash. A rendering whose staleness check needs the renderer is a check CI cannot run: Java, a browser, or a font set that measures text a pixel differently. Write the sha256 of the exact source text into the output and compare stamps. The UML and block-graph SVGs do this through scripts/plantuml-render.ts, which every PlantUML generator shares, with its pinned jar and one JVM for all diagrams. | Show it in a zoomable figure. On the site, use the bpmn-figure markup so docs-ui.js adds zoom, reset and full-width controls, and the export ones: download the SVG, download a 2× PNG, or copy it (as an image where the browser allows, else as SVG text, and it says which). A pages template missing layout: default renders with no site script and so no controls, and nothing reports it. There is ONE viewer, and every diagram on a folio or IG page gets it. It is mountFigure in docs-ui.js; mountFigures decides what is a figure. Do not write a second one for a new kind of page. Extend what mountFigures and inlineDiagrams recognise instead. It takes each way a page embeds a drawing: . | embedded as | taken by | where it appears | . | .bpmn-figure markup | always | the process pages | . | an inline <svg> | always (an icon-sized one, or one inside a link or nav, is not a figure) | Mermaid, an IG’s {% include x.svg %} (PlantUML) | . | <img src="x.svg"> | always; inlined first | UML overviews, workflow figures | . | <object data="x.svg"> | always; inlined first, and its fallback text becomes the name | the IG Publisher’s convention for a pre-rendered diagram | . | a raster <img> | only on a page that opts in with data-fa-figure-images, and only when the column has shrunk it | an IG’s .drawio.png architecture drawings | . The raster row is an opt-in because a raster image on the platform’s own pages is as often a card face or a photo. A site build that knows its images are drawings stamps the attribute on the page. The IG site build does this on every IG page, and its own skill (ig-site-links) says where. This skill names no instance, because the viewer belongs to the platform. At 100% a plain figure is shown at its own width, capped at the column. It is not stretched to fill the column. A figure that is wider than its column scrolls inside its card and never runs past the page’s edge. The viewer is keyboard-operable, because the profile is low-dexterity. Drag-to-pan is an accelerator, never the only way to pan (board-windows §”The floor”). The figure takes focus (Tab from its toolbar). While it has focus, the arrow keys pan it, + and - zoom, and 0 resets. An arrow key is taken only when the figure can scroll in that direction. Otherwise the page scrolls as usual. The tools layer’s test/ig-diagram-viewer.e2e.ts checks all of this on a fixture page. | Put the measurement on the drawing. When a graph is being partitioned, show each group’s detangle numbers (size, cohesion, links in and out) beside the group, so the picture and the metric are read together. The UML overview pages do this through detangleResultsDir (schemas/kg/detangle-sidecar.ts), the same function the detangler writes through. A number shown without its picture invites arguing about the number. | .

6c341f4b3993.doc: Graph rendering: one set of rules for every drawn graph
6c341f4b3993.title: Layout engines
6c341f4b3993.content: Measured on the UML overview. Re-measure before relying on it for a different graph. | engine | use it for | what it gets wrong | . | stored layout (BPMN DI) | a graph whose author placed the nodes | nothing to choose: never re-lay a graph that carries its own layout | . | ELK (!pragma layout elk in PlantUML) | the compact, portrait default; it routes edges around boxes | it lays everything top to bottom and ignores left to right direction and arrow hints (output byte-identical). Unconnected groups end up in one wide row. | . | ELK + hidden links | a grid of unconnected groups (an overview) | nothing, if the column count suits the orientation: ceil(√(n/2)) for portrait, ceil(√(2n)) for landscape | . | Graphviz dot, left to right, polyline edges | the landscape view of a connected graph | it can route a long edge across a box, which is why ELK stays the portrait default. Use nodesep 70, ranksep 160. | . | Graphviz with orthogonal edges | avoid | it places edge labels away from their edges and runs lines through boxes. | . | Mermaid (dagre) | a secondary view where CSS classes on nodes matter | the same model came out three times taller than ELK’s | . | Graphviz dot in the browser (WASM, unflatten then dot) | the interactive view a reader rearranges by dragging nodes (kg-subgraph-layout) | like ELK it sets unconnected clusters, and unconnected nodes in one cluster, on one rank: fold both into grids with invisible, marked anchors | .

9a6cb733b03e.doc: Graph rendering: one set of rules for every drawn graph
9a6cb733b03e.title: Applying it
9a6cb733b03e.content: | graph | source | groups | edge kinds | renderer today | owes | . | schemas | graph-typology registry, Zod schemas | <instance>/<sub-graph> | composition; field-carried vs declared elsewhere | gen-uml-overview.ts (PlantUML, Mermaid and the DOT of the Interactive view), gen-object-model-uml.ts | meets all ten | . | processes | .bpmn files | pools and lanes | sequence, message, call | render-bpmn.ts (stored layout) | rule 6 (orientation) does not apply: the author placed it | . | folio blocks and any formal relation the content type adds | buildContentGraph in pipeline/content-graph.ts; status from the content type’s status source | chapters | editorial (uses[], interprets), solid, vs formal (the content type’s own edges), dashed purple | gen-content-graph-uml.ts (Tool content-graph-uml), run from a folio | meets rules 1 to 8. Rule 9 waits on a folio page to show it; rule 10 on detangle scanning a folio | . | detangle partition | the sidecars under detangleResultsDir | detangle groups | enforced / recorded / prose | numbers only; the UML pages show them (rule 10) | a drawing of the cross-group edges themselves | . A folio is content, and content lives in a folio repository, not here. Apply the rules there through the platform’s generator, and ask the owner before a PR in a content repository the owner has said to ask about. The editorial and formal relations are one drawing, not two. buildContentGraph holds both over the same blocks, so gen-content-graph-uml.ts draws them together and keeps them apart by line style. Status fills come from the same stylesheet as the family colours (--fa-uml-status-* in uml.css). A human review outranks an agentic one, which outranks a machine-derived status. For a paper folio, where the formal relation is Lean’s, the science layer’s lean-formal-graph (skill_fetch lean-formal-graph) says what that edge and status source are, and which older drawings this one supersedes. Never populate uses[] from a formal graph to make a drawing look connected. The editorial relation is authored; see AGENTS.md and uses-editorial-review. Rule 4 is how the drawing keeps them apart.

f7f32f9e0315.title: Role
f7f32f9e0315.content: Compute Gröbner bases and normal forms for the project’s algebraic structures (commutative or non-commutative), and apply the reduction to the project’s words/elements to extract the invariants the project needs. The deliverable is always a reproducible witness: the reduced normal form plus a step-by-step log of which relation fired at each step.

6fc402a6854f.title: When to Use
6fc402a6854f.content: . | “reduce word” / “Gröbner reduce” / “normal form” | “compute element” / “trace / invariant from reduction” | “Gröbner basis for …” / “division algorithm” | “CAS computation” / “letterplace” | .

29f721ba31d5.title: Tools
29f721ba31d5.content: CAS (exact, symbolic) . For exact symbolic computation over the base ring. Fastest for large inputs. For a non-commutative algebra, a letterplace CAS encodes positioned generators and provides the core operations: build the letterplace ring with a degree bound; multiply with position shifting; compute the two-sided Gröbner basis of the defining ideal; reduce an element to normal form modulo that basis. Record the ring, the relations of the ideal, and the monomial ordering used. Instrumented project routine (step-logged) . A project routine performs the same reduction with step-by-step logging — which relation fired, and any cost/weight change it incurred. Use it when you need the reduction trace, not just the answer. It exposes: build-and-reduce of the input element, the reduction itself (with logging), the invariant extraction, and a full-computation entry point that emits a witness.

02ff73d08e9b.title: The Gröbner basis
02ff73d08e9b.content: For the project’s algebra, the Gröbner basis G consists of the defining relations of the ideal, expressed in the project’s monomial ordering. Classify each relation by whether it changes the project’s tracked cost/weight (the “energy-changing” relations) or preserves it (reordering / topological-invariance relations). The admissible system (B, <) uses the project’s chosen monomials and ordering.

89cca3822708.title: Proven results to track
89cca3822708.content: Record the structural results the project relies on (each with a witness and/or formal cross-reference), e.g.: a factorization of the extracted invariant; path-independence of the cost under reduction (a diamond -lemma / confluence statement); which relations change cost; and the complexity of the decomposition.

9232b62210a0.title: Witness files
9232b62210a0.content: All computations produce witness JSON next to the script, named per the project’s witness convention (<computation>.witness.json), including a CAS-backed variant when a CAS is available.

7178a109faee.title: Cross-references
7178a109faee.content: Link each result to its formal/blueprint counterpart: the admissible system and division algorithm; the unique-normal-form proposition; the cost-as-invariant theorem; the factorization theorem; and the complexity proposition. Keep these cross-references in the project’s content tree.

b7c5b0c41b4e.title: Hand back to the discussion
b7c5b0c41b4e.content: The procedure behind Process_HandBackToDiscussion. It joins two rules that already bind: ask-the-person (how a question is put) and the relay paragraph of interaction-modality §4.1 (a relayed question says where the answer goes). This skill is the missing step between them: who puts the question, and how the answer gets back.

ac184c0663d7.title: Why
ac184c0663d7.content: A card posted only in a sibling’s own thread is not seen by the person, who is talking with the discussion agent elsewhere; the decision stalls, or reaches the person only by reconstruction. A feedback channel in play (a review sheet, an issue) is used as well.

c5939dd8433c.title: The two roles
c5939dd8433c.content: | role | who | does | . | Discussion agent (session-coordinator) | the agent the person is talking with right now: a project coordinator, the parent of a subagent, the session that spawned a swarm | shows the hand-back to the person, asks with ask-the-person, marks every copy answered, routes the answer back | . | Sibling (sibling-session) | any agent the discussion agent spawned, or one working beside it on the same goal: a project thread, a subagent, a workflow agent, a cloud session | composes the hand-back once, with the analysis it alone has, and acts on the answer | . You are a sibling when your brief names a discussion agent, or when you were started by another agent while a person was talking with it. A sibling that is not sure hands back anyway: one extra copy costs a line, and a missed card costs a stalled decision.

ab8456ccc7d8.title: The brief names the discussion (spawning agent)
ab8456ccc7d8.content: An agent that spawns a sibling during a live discussion puts the discussion link in the brief (definitions.discussion of the input schema): who the discussion agent is, how to reach it, the standing card rules, and any feedback channel in play (a review sheet’s id and tab, an issue). See process-state §”A coordinator that briefs a thread”. A sibling has nothing else that tells it.

088808bcc343.title: Input and output
088808bcc343.content: The contract is input.schema.json and output.schema.json. | In (the hand-back): from (title, link, process), to (the discussion link), kind (decision, question, context, result, blocker), a one-sentence summary, ask (the ask-the-person input, unchanged, for a decision or question), context (for the others), links, channels (always discussion, plus any of own-thread, project-chat, review-sheet, github-issue, github-pr), answerRoute, blocking, and supersedes when it replaces an earlier one. | Out (the record): shown (every copy, discussion first), state (open, answered, withdrawn, superseded, informed), the ask-the-person output, chosen, quote, answeredIn, marked (the strike-through edit per copy) and deliveredBack (proof the answer reached the sibling, with citesPerson). | .

4455e6516f6a.title: Steps — sibling
4455e6516f6a.content: . | Compose once. A question is the full ask-the-person input: what will differ, context, every option lettered with a one-line trade-off, the recommendation and why, what happens with no answer. The discussion agent must be able to show it without opening your thread. Context, a result or a blocker gets the same test. | Show it where you are. Post it in your own thread too (chat text, then the card), so the tappable card sits beside the work. Your own thread is never the only copy. | Mirror it to the feedback channel in play. When a review sheet governs the work, write the “Decision needed” block into the row’s agent column and set Agentic status to Needs you (the document layer’s review-sheet-script skill, §”A question to people goes in the sheet”). An issue or PR in play gets a comment. These are extra copies, never instead of the discussion. | Hand back to the discussion agent with the host’s route: . | host | route | . | Claude projects thread | message_coordinator (or message_thread to the discussion thread), the hand-back as plain prose in the schema’s order: summary, question, lettered options with trade-offs, recommendation, if silent, link to your thread | . | subagent (Agent tool, workflow agent) | your final report: the hand-back as a fenced json block that validates against the input schema, then a one-line summary. You cannot reach the person; the parent asks | . | sibling session | SendMessage to the discussion session | . | none of these | a comment on the issue or PR the discussion is about, and say so in your own thread | . | Keep working on the recommended option where it can be undone; stop where it cannot (blocking: true). | Act on the answer when it comes back. Only an answer that carries the person’s own words (a cited message, a card tap, a Blue-column cell) is their approval. A paraphrase from another agent is not. | .

b71514aaf873.title: Steps — discussion agent
b71514aaf873.content: . | Show it in the discussion, saying it comes from the sibling (title and link) and that you will pass the answer on. A question goes through Process_AskThePerson unchanged: the chat text in full first, then the card with the same letters. Never “see the card in thread X”. | Context, a result or a blocker that needs no answer: post it, state informed, done. | Take the answer from any copy. A tap on your card, a tap on the sibling’s card, or a Blue-column answer in the sheet all count. Take the first, and treat a later disagreeing answer as a new question. | Route it back on answerRoute, attaching the person’s own message by id where the host allows (citesPerson: true). | Mark every copy answered. A chat copy keeps its text: strike the question through and add [Edit: <letter> chosen by <who>, <time>]. A card you posted is closed with the chosen option. A sheet’s “Decision needed” block is replaced by the decision and who made it, and Agentic status moves on. A withdrawn or superseded hand-back is marked the same way with the reason. | A rule-level answer goes into the governing skill in the same turn (symbiotic-interaction §2). | .

dec329731c47.title: Anti-patterns
dec329731c47.content: . | A card only in the sibling’s thread. | A hand-back that says “see my thread”. A pointer is not the question. | The discussion agent rewriting the options. The sibling did the analysis; reword for the person if needed, but keep the letters and the recommendation, and say so if you change one. | The sheet as the only copy. People on the committee see the sheet; the owner in the discussion may not be looking at it. | An answer that never reaches the sibling. The person answered once; the sibling must not ask again. | .

be38a5d04c7f.title: Input
be38a5d04c7f.content: One hand-back from a sibling agent (spawned, or working beside the discussion) to the discussion agent: the agent that is talking with the person right now. It carries a card, a question, context, a result or a blocker, complete enough that the discussion agent can put it in front of the person without opening the sibling’s thread. A question or decision carries the ask-the-person input unchanged, so the card the person sees is composed once, by the agent that did the analysis. | Field | Type | Required | Description | . | from | object | yes | The sibling that hands back. | . | to | any | yes |   | . | kind | "decision" | "question" | "context" | "result" | "blocker" | yes | decision and question need the person’s answer and carry ask. context, result and blocker inform; a blocker that needs the person to act is a decision, not a blocker. | . | summary | string | yes | One sentence that stands alone: what the person needs to know or choose. (minLength: 1, maxLength: 300) | . | ask | any | no | The composed question, exactly as ask-the-person takes it. Required for decision and question. | . | context | string | no | For context, result and blocker: what happened, what it touches and what happens next, every id glossed. | . | links | array | no | PRs, issues, staging pages and files the hand-back is about, each with a title. | . | channels | array | yes | Every place the hand-back is shown. The discussion is always one of them; a review sheet or an issue is an extra copy, never the only one. | . | answerRoute | object | yes | How the answer reaches the sibling again. An answer typed at the discussion does not reach the sibling by itself. | . | blocking | boolean | yes | true when the sibling has stopped and waits on the answer; false when it keeps working on the recommended option. | . | supersedes | string | no | The id of an earlier hand-back this one replaces; the discussion agent withdraws that card. | . from . | Field | Type | Required | Description | . | title | string | yes | The sibling’s thread or task title, as the person would recognise it. (minLength: 1) | . | link | string | yes | A link to the sibling’s thread, session or PR, so the person can open it for more. Never the only place the content is. (minLength: 1) | . | process | string | no | The process and step the sibling is in (process-state), or “none”. | . links[] . | Field | Type | Required | Description | . | title | string | yes |   | . | url | string | yes |   | . answerRoute . | Field | Type | Required | Description | . | how | "thread-message" | "send-message" | "return-value" | "issue-comment" | "sheet" | yes | thread-message: the host’s message-to-thread tool, with the person’s message attached by id. send-message: a sibling session’s inbox. return-value: the sibling is a subagent and the answer goes into its next prompt. issue-comment and sheet: the sibling reads it there. | . | target | string | yes | The thread id, session id, issue or sheet row the answer goes to. (minLength: 1) | . Raw schema · ✎ Edit .

ef155a30156f.title: Output
ef155a30156f.content: The record of one hand-back: where it was shown, its state, the person’s answer quoted, how every copy was marked answered, and proof the answer reached the sibling. A dismissed card is not an answer. | Field | Type | Required | Description | . | shown | array | yes | One entry per copy, the discussion’s first. | . | state | "open" | "answered" | "withdrawn" | "superseded" | "informed" | yes | open: waiting. answered: the person chose, in any channel. withdrawn: the question no longer needs an answer. superseded: a later hand-back replaced it. informed: a context, result or blocker that needed no answer was shown. | . | ask | any | no | The ask-the-person output, when the hand-back carried a question. | . | chosen | string | null | no | The letter chosen; null unless answered. (pattern: ^[A-D]$) | . | quote | string | null | no | The person’s answer verbatim, with who, when and the message id or sheet cell it came from. | . | answeredIn | "discussion" | "own-thread" | "project-chat" | "review-sheet" | "github-issue" | "github-pr" | null | no | Which copy the answer came from. | . | marked | array | no | How each copy was closed once answered or withdrawn. A chat copy keeps its text: the question is struck through and “[Edit: chosen by , ]" added, so the record still says what was asked. A sheet copy's "Decision needed" block is replaced by the decision and who made it. | . | deliveredBack | object | null | yes | Proof the answer reached the sibling; null only while open or for state informed. | . | stagingLinks | any | no | When the question asks the person to look at changed pages: the staging preview, one deep link per changed page with the same page on main, shown in the chat copy. When there is no preview, say so in missing. Rule: cat-harness sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/staging-review.md §”The deep-link rule”. | . shown[] . | Field | Type | Required | Description | . | channel | "discussion" | "own-thread" | "project-chat" | "review-sheet" | "github-issue" | "github-pr" | yes |   | . | ref | string | yes | Message id, card id, sheet cell (tab!header/row key) or comment URL. (minLength: 1) | . | card | string | null | no | The card’s id when this copy offered one. | . marked[] . | Field | Type | Required | Description | . | ref | string | yes |   | . | edit | string | yes | The text applied, e.g. “Which layout? [Edit: A chosen by litlfred, 2026-10-31 15:50Z]”. (minLength: 1) | . Raw schema · ✎ Edit .

4faf500377b6.title: Handover report
4faf500377b6.content: An agent’s state lives in three places that do not survive it: the chat, its scratchpad, and uncommitted work in its worktree. A handover report moves the parts that matter into the repository, as a committed work item note, so the next agent starts from fact rather than from guesswork. To produce one under time pressure, follow prepare-for-handover: it commits and pushes first, then writes this report citing the pushed SHAs. This skill is not agent-handoff, which hands one task to a named agent in another environment. A handover report is a snapshot of everything one agent is holding, written for whoever turns up next, which may be no one in particular.

eb667ec131aa.title: When to write one
eb667ec131aa.content: . | When told a stall is likely. Write it first, before continuing any work. A report written after the stall is never written. | Before a long or risky step: a 30-minute regenerate, a big merge, a disk-heavy run. | At the end of an arc, even a successful one, if anything stays open. | When a steward or the owner asks. | . Write it short and early, then update it. A 20-line report pushed now is worth more than a complete one that never lands.

2cd310854414.title: Where it goes
2cd310854414.content: A work item note on the work item you are working, or on its epic if you hold several: . bun run cat beans:note <bean-id> --title "handover: <role> <date>" \ --body-file <file> --branch <your-branch> bun run cat beans:notes # rewrites the index; commit both files git add -A && git commit && git push . One file per branch per work item, so two agents writing handovers never conflict (bean-coordination §”Adding to a bean — a note, not an append”). Write it in your own worktree. Some tools write into the main checkout instead; if you are a subagent, check git status there afterwards. Push it, even onto a draft PR or a red branch. An unpushed report does not exist.

e847ceb57cc0.title: The template
e847ceb57cc0.content: Mix narrative with formal content. The tables are what a triage agent parses; the prose is what a person reads. ## Handover report: <role> (<session or agent>) - **Session:** <session URL, or the parent session plus agent id> - **Written:** <UTC time>, <why: stall expected / end of arc / asked> - **Role and mandate:** <one line; the owner rulings that bound you> ### Where I'm going (current arc) <2–4 sentences: the goal, the epic it serves, and what "done" looks like.> ### Done so far - <outcome, with PR, commit or bean> ### Next in queue 1. <next concrete step: command, file, PR> 2. … ### In flight | item | kind (PR / branch / bean / process run) | state | next action | owner |---|---|---|---|---| ### Blockers and dependencies | blocker | waits on | since | expires / re-check |---|---|---|---| ### Decisions pending (owner) - <question, with options and your recommendation, so it can be asked cold> ### Unpushed or at-risk state - <scratchpad files, local commits, running jobs, and whether each is reproducible> ### Dispatch lines (copy-paste, one per unstarted item) Do bean folio-assistant-<id> on branch <branch-to-create> of repo <owner>/<repo>. Do bean folio-assistant-<id> on branch <branch-to-create> of repo <owner>/<repo>. ### How to resume <the first three things the next agent should do, in order> .

c087722b1d2b.title: Rules
c087722b1d2b.content: . | Facts with provenance. Write “CI red on abc123 (check X)”, not “CI is flaky”. Give SHAs, PR numbers and work item ids, never “the branch”. | Say what is NOT pushed. Unpushed commits, scratchpad plans and running background jobs are exactly what a stall destroys. Name each one, and say whether it can be rebuilt. | Owner rulings verbatim, with the date. A ruling paraphrased in a handover becomes a different ruling by the second handover. | Never put secrets in it. Name secrets, never give their values. | Blocks follow bean-blocking: what it waits on, since when, and when to re-check, so a stale block can be told from a live one. | Update in place. Re-run beans:note on the same branch and work item, which gives the same file. Do not append a second report. | Every unstarted item gets a DISPATCH LINE, in one fixed sentence. Do bean folio-assistant-<id> on branch <branch-to-create> of repo <owner>/<repo>. It is a format, not a suggestion: write it verbatim with the three slots filled. Why one sentence, and why these three slots. A dispatch is read by somebody with no context — the owner pasting it into a new session, or a steward handing out work. The three slots are the minimum that makes it actionable alone: the WORK ITEM says what and carries its own Done-when, the BRANCH stops two agents landing on one ref, and the REPO is required because an agent’s session may be scoped to a different one. Drop any slot and the recipient has to come back and ask. Three rules: . | Name a branch that does not exist yet, and say so. A line naming a finished branch sends an agent to a dead ref. | One work item per line. Not a theme, not “the three remaining X”. The work item is what carries the Done-when, and a line that names a theme hands over a judgement instead of a task. | Order them, and say what is ordered. If a line must follow another, write that above the block — not inside the sentence, which stays fixed. A hidden prerequisite makes a list of dispatchable work items worse than a list of the one that is ready. | . dispatch-agent governs what happens AFTER the line is sent — the progress contract and the heartbeat. This rule is only about writing the line so the work can be handed on at all. | .

e6a7742d7024.content: | process | step(s) that name it | . | Stalled-agent triage: collect handovers, consolidate themes, recommend, re-route | Collect or reconstruct a handover report per agent | .

a101e1624ef4.doc: Harness projections: CI writes them, the owner consents to every hand edit
a101e1624ef4.title: Harness projections: CI writes them, the owner consents to every hand edit
a101e1624ef4.content: .claude/ is what the Claude Code harness reads before any skill is loaded: the slash commands a person can type, the memory injected into a subagent, and the hooks and permissions every session runs under. An edit there changes how every later session behaves, including sessions that never see the commit.claude/ is one instance of a general rule. Every coding-agent Tool has config files, and some of them are projections of the graph: CI writes the projections, and a person consents to each hand edit.claude/ is named here because it is the agent-host directory the generators write. Which files a Tool reads, and which of them are generated, belongs to that Tool’s adapter. Securing what the agent may do at all is agent-permissions.

61bf39b05e5e.doc: Harness projections: CI writes them, the owner consents to every hand edit
61bf39b05e5e.title: Two kinds of file, two writers
61bf39b05e5e.content: | kind | examples | source of truth | who writes the .claude/ file | . | projection (generated) | .claude/commands/<name>.md carrying a generated: key (skill:commands); the marked region of .claude/agent-memory/<agent>/MEMORY.md (agent-memory); .claude/agents/* where the memory assembler writes them; .claude/skills/ synced from packages | the skill’s front matter, the memory nodes under memory/, the package | CI only. A workflow step runs the generator and commits the result to the PR branch. | . | hand-edited | .claude/settings.json and its hooks, a hand-written command (no generated: key), an agent definition’s hand-written body, a memory file’s ## Session log | the file itself | an agent, only with the owner’s consent to that exact change | . The rule for a projection: edit the source, not the projection. To change a slash command, change the skill’s user_invocable or description. To change what a subagent remembers, add or edit a node under memory/ (agent-memory). Push the source change and let CI write the projection. You may run a generator locally in its --check form, or into a scratch tree, to see what it would write. Do not stage or commit anything it writes under .claude/. This applies inside skill-registration too. skill:register runs skill:commands, which writes .claude/commands/ in a composed checkout. Commit what it writes everywhere else, and leave .claude/ to CI. Why CI and not the agent. A projection is correct only if it was generated from the tree that lands. An agent’s local run reflects the tree it had, and a hand-merged projection drifts from its source; the CI step runs on the PR head, so the projection on the branch is the one the merge will carry, from one writer.

40aa69cb5510.doc: Harness projections: CI writes them, the owner consents to every hand edit
40aa69cb5510.title: Hand-edited files: consent per change
40aa69cb5510.content: Before you write a hand-edited .claude/ file: . | Show the exact diff. Paste the unified diff itself, not a description of it. | Give the reason: what breaks or is missing without the change, and what the change does to every later session (a hook that runs on every tool call; a permission that stops a prompt). | Ask, and wait. The order is context, diff, recommendation, question (interaction-modality §4.1). “Go ahead” discharges this question, for this diff only. | Record the consent in the commit that makes the change, and as a comment on the PR: . claude-config-consent: by: <owner's login> on: <ISO-8601 date-time> file: .claude/settings.json diff: <sha256 of the diff shown> evidence: "<the owner's words, verbatim>" (<session link or comment permalink>) . | . A standing waiver does not reach this. Consent is per change, so there is no gate class for it in confirmation-waiver’s table, and a waiver that claims one is not a waiver. A broad instruction such as “fix the hooks” or “make the session start work” authorises the investigation. It does not authorise the edit. Bring the diff back. When a hook or setting gets in your way, report it; do not edit it. This is the same rule as prepare-merge §Guardrails (“fix the tool” rather than delete the branch), with one extra step: here, fixing the tool is itself a change that needs consent.

06927a16765f.doc: Harness projections: CI writes them, the owner consents to every hand edit
06927a16765f.title: Where it sits in the process
06927a16765f.content: merge-to-main.bpmn runs Task_RegenProjections in its build-pipeline lane before it reads any evidence. CI regenerates the projections on the head and commits them to the PR branch, and the evidence is then read on that new head. A PR whose projections are stale therefore cannot reach the merge gate looking green (merge-to-main).

624b0bbb4613.doc: Harness projections: CI writes them, the owner consents to every hand edit
624b0bbb4613.title: What this does not do yet
624b0bbb4613.content: . | The CI step is declared here, not built. In the platform repository, merge-main.yml runs regen (which includes skill:commands and agent-memory) and pushes to the PR branch, but only for PRs labelled merge-main when main moves. code-quality-gates.yml runs skill:commands:check and agent-memory:check and fails, but commits nothing. A step that regenerates the projections on every PR head and commits them is a workflow change in the repositories that carry .github/. That change is not made here. | No check refuses an agent-authored commit under .claude/. Telling a CI-written commit from an agent’s needs a committer convention (the bot identity the workflow pushes as), and a gate that reads it. | skill:register still writes .claude/commands/. Restricting it to --check for that one step would be a change to skill-register.ts. | .

5fb9cfb1590b.title: Harness requirements — what an instance owes for what it declares
5fb9cfb1590b.content: Declaring a directory is a promise that this instance holds a graph of that kind and a consumer may scan it. The obligations below make the promise keepable. bun run cat check:subgraph-coverage measures them.

a7aa8c6ba3c0.title: The five obligations
a7aa8c6ba3c0.content: | obligation | declared as | the question it answers | . | visualiser | by the HARNESS: an entry in its <instance>.json visualisers — covers (its directory ids) or coversKinds, renderedBy a Tool whose renders lists the kind — published at <base>/<harness>/<id>/; the directory keeps only its tile: look | can a person LOOK at this? | . | docs | by the PAGE: documents: in its front matter (or its manifest, or <meta name="documents"> in generated HTML) names the kind or <instance>/<id> | can a person READ ABOUT this? | . | skill | by the SKILL: graph-typologies: names the kind, or governs: [<instance>/<id>] the one directory | is an agent handed something that GOVERNS this? | . | serialisations | coverage.serialisations | is each node ADDRESSABLE as json, jsonld and schema.json? | . | README | an instance-readme asset, inside the instance | can a reader ENTER this instance at all? | . The first four are per declared directory. The fifth is per instance and is ranked harder: an instance with no starting README of its own cannot be entered.

ef293baa8a34.title: Severities
ef293baa8a34.content: . | major — an obligation this kind OWES and the instance has not met, or a target declared and not resolving. | minor — nobody has said yet, for a kind that never owed one. | . They are ranked apart because an axis that cannot tell a broken promise from an open question has a count that means nothing. Which kinds owe a visualiser . Every kind that is not part of the static knowledge graph — active material about the work, such as beans/, todos/ and fsh-guts/. Authored subject matter can be read as itself; a record of where something got to needs something that renders it. The rule is holds !== "content" (owesVisualiser() in schemas/kg/cat-harness.ts). content is “authored nodes a reader or a tool consumes as the subject matter… It stands on its own”, so it needs no viewer. Do not key the rule on holds === "state": fsh-guts is context (no running step writes it) and still owes a visualiser, and a kind moving between state and context must not change what it owes. Any rule over this axis must pass that test. Exemptions . | renderable kinds are exempt by construction. docs and folio render to pages, so the pages ARE the view and a separate viewer would be a second rendering of the same thing. | Bootstrap is exempt by INSTANCE, not by kind. bootstrap has no visualiser, but it must have its json/jsonld. The exemption is keyed on the instance name, so every other instance declaring the same kind keeps the obligation, and an exemption by kind would stop checking the one thing bootstrap must have. | An unknown kind owes one. A kind nobody has classified must not escape an obligation by being unmentioned. (This is the opposite of graphLayer(), whose undefined callers must not read as content; both fail safe.) | .

372d30fc919a.title: Where a visualiser is published
372d30fc919a.content: | # | URL | what it is | . | 1 | <base>/ | the ROOT’s rendering — its docs/ is installed by cat-harness, so no segment | . | 2 | <base>/<instance>/ | the instance presented as itself, on its own theme | . | 3 | <base>/<harness>/<visualiser>/<sub-graph>/ | a visualiser the harness DECLARES, over the full KG it covers (<base>/<harness>/<visualiser>/) or one sub-graph of it, with assets beneath (…/<sub-graph>/<path to asset>) | . The case-3 segments come from the harness’s visualisers declaration and are computed by visualiserRoute (schemas/kg/visualiser-route.ts) — never composed by a generator, never claimed by a page. Two declarations on one route are a declaration error, refused by check:visualiser-routes; see harness-tiles §”Where a tile goes”. So docs/ has two roles at once: a directory cat-harness instantiates AND a namespace under which the docs-kind assets of another subgraph are rendered, e.g. <base>/cat-harness/docs/<iris-replica>/. Case 3 is the canonical address; a bare <base>/<visualizer>/ is an opt-in alias (alias on the declaration, composed as a redirect) — see schema-management §”Where a viewer publishes”. The site owner’s state dashboards are at <base>/cat-harness/<id>/, with the bare URL (/beans/, /todos/, …) as their declared alias. “Which directory holds it” and “which URL serves it” are different questions; a visualiser’s declaration answers the first. Never compose the second by hand. The root’s own documentation pages are the exception to case 1. Pages authored in cat-harness’s docs/ folder publish under <base>/docs/cat-harness/ — concepts/architecture.md → <base>/docs/cat-harness/concepts/architecture.html, its locale copy at <base>/docs/cat-harness/concepts/fr/architecture.html. Everything else keeps its URL: the landing page <base>/ and each locale landing <base>/fr/, the instance sites (case 2), the viewers (case 3), the kind directories the same tree publishes (<base>/processes/, <base>/proposals/ …) and every root export. This is done with permalink defaults in that _config.yml, beside each chapter’s parent, so baseurl stays the site’s and Jekyll’s page.url is the one answer. A generator that links to a docs page by its source path asks publishedPagePath / publishedHref (scripts/lib/jekyll-permalink.ts) rather than swapping .md for .html; an authored link in a docs page to something outside docs/cat-harness/ is written {{ '/x' | relative_url }} (in a table row, {{ site.baseurl }}/x, whose missing | cannot split the cell), because a relative one would resolve under docs/cat-harness/.

88e6b9c4cfe1.title: Serialisations — the obligation that cannot be waived
88e6b9c4cfe1.content: A declared directory owes two levels of addressability: . | level | URL | what it asserts | . | the directory | <base>/beans.json, .jsonld, .schema.json | this graph exists and here is its shape | . | every node in it | <base>/beans/<node-id>.json, .jsonld, .schema.json | each node is individually in the graph | . Whatever form a node HAS is reachable; a missing form is not invented. A .schema.json that 404s where no schema exists is honest. A .jsonld that 404s where the node exists is the defect. Why this one takes no exempt . Rendering, documenting and governing are choices about effort, so they are waivable with a reason. Addressability is the existence claim: harnesses cannot override a node being in the KG. A harness that could waive it could declare a directory into the graph and make its contents unreachable — a consumer scanning nothing and reporting a clean run. Even bootstrap, exempt from a visualiser, keeps this obligation. SubgraphCoverageSchema.exempt therefore carries three keys, not four, and tsc enforces it, so a waiver for serialisations is a type error rather than a silent undefined that reads as “not exempted”. How it fits the render pipeline . Each graph’s render pipeline is reader → projection → viewer → gate. The serialisation obligation is a constraint on the projection, not a fifth part: the projection must be reachable as the three content types at the directory’s URL and per node beneath it, so a graph that has done the pipeline work has mostly done this. Do not compose these URLs by hand: the directory’s declaration answers which directory holds the nodes; the published-URL resolver answers where they are served.

ce5f9a9554eb.title: Before you declare a directory
ce5f9a9554eb.content: . | Say what renders it, documents it and governs it, or say why it needs none — coverage.exempt.<criterion> takes a reason, and a waiver with no reason is a silence list. | Say what serialises it. There is no waiver: a directory whose nodes are not addressable has not entered the graph. | Declare only what exists. A declared-but-absent directory makes a consumer scan nothing and report a clean run. | Check the kind’s layer. If it is not content, you are promising a visualiser, so know who is building it before the declaration lands. | .

e5638b835f89.title: Before you add a graph typology
e5638b835f89.content: GraphTypologyDef requires renderable and holds, so a kind cannot go unclassified, and tsc enforces it. It does not carry the visualiser obligation, which is derived from holds. Set holds on what a running process DOES with the graph, never on what you would like the obligation to be.

fcbf9aff138e.title: Reading the axis
fcbf9aff138e.content: It is advisory — it reports, ranks and exits 0, because a hard gate over a large backlog is a wall somebody switches off. It becomes fatal once the count of unmet obligations is low enough to mean something. | undetermined is never a clean run. An unreadable declaration is reported as such; a sweep blind on one instance has not cleared the others. | Never quote a count from prose. Run it. | A finding is not a task list. The obligations belong to whoever declared the directory, and deletion-requires-confirmation applies to every remedy that removes something. | .

423f6da1bc72.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
423f6da1bc72.title: A tile is the harness’s, not the node’s
423f6da1bc72.content: A tile is a function of a harness watching a directory, not of nodes. If a harness declares visualisers, each one gets a tile; a tile defaults to the theme, and a harness can declare one or more visualisations, each with a title. The tile set is not a new registry — it is the visualiser obligation made reachable. A harness declares its visualisers in its <instance>.json visualisers (HarnessVisualiserSchema), and kg:audit reports which directories owe one. A graph that owes a visualiser owes a tile, so the audit needs no second list free to disagree with it.

284daea90d8c.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
284daea90d8c.title: Where a tile goes — the declared route, and nothing else
284daea90d8c.content: Each visualiser is ONE declaration in the harness that owns it: . "visualisers": [ { "id": "library", "renderedBy": "library-viewer", "coversKinds": ["library"], "subgraphs": "instance" }, { "id": "todos", "renderedBy": "state-viewer", "covers": ["todos"], "alias": "todos" }, { "id": "fsh-guts", "renderedBy": "staging-graph-viewer", "covers": ["fsh-guts"], "publish": "staging-only", "writer": ["scripts/gen-fsh-guts-viz.ts"] } ] . | id is the URL segment; renderedBy names a Tool node (the implementation may live anywhere); covers names this harness’s own directory ids, coversKinds graph typologies, over every declared directory of them in the checkout. A harness never names another instance’s directory — that would be a lower layer naming a higher one. | The URL is computed, never chosen. visualiserRoute in schemas/kg/visualiser-route.ts is the ONE function every generator and reader uses: <harness>/<id>/ for the full KG, <harness>/<id>/<sub-graph>/ for one sub-graph (subgraphs: "instance" — one per covered instance — or "directory", nested under subgraphUnder[kind] where the visualiser declares one), and an asset path below either. Every page is written to that route under the site’s docs layer, so the file and the URL cannot disagree. A tile opens the sub-graph view when it exists, else the full one. | A page claims nothing. A page carries only rendered-by: <Tool>, as provenance; it carries no renders: or <meta name="renders">. A directory’s coverage.visualiser is filled IN MEMORY by withViewers from the declarations, never from disk. | Collisions are declaration errors. bun run cat check:visualiser-routes refuses two declarations resolving to one route (or one inside another’s subtree), a page drawn by a Tool outside every route that Tool is declared to render, a page under a route that names a different Tool, a visualiser covering a kind its Tool does not renders, and any renders: or coverage.visualiser on disk. | The short URL is an opt-in alias. alias: "todos" makes <base>/todos/ a redirect to <base>/cat-harness/todos/, composed by compose-docs.ts for every page under the route. An alias that names another alias, a harness, or anything the site already carries at its top level is refused by the gate before a build and by the composer during one. A tile always links the canonical route. | publish: "staging-only": compose-docs withholds the route (and its alias) from a canonical deploy. | .

70e188e2c18c.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
70e188e2c18c.title: Instantiated is a different fact from declared
70e188e2c18c.content: Only the harnesses instantiated in the folio get tiles, not every dependency. Which instances are instantiated here is answered by the root index.config.json (instances[]), or without an index by each root <name>.config.json. That rule is index-config’s; the tiles only consume it, because the navbar cannot be derived from the declarations alone and a directory listing is not the question a reader is asking. Dependencies keep a group of their own rather than disappearing, so a reader looking for one is not answered with silence. A harness a KG subscription chose is instantiated by the same file, with no local declaration: its declaration is the substrate snapshot kg:subscribe cached at the pin. bun run cat kg:instantiate <subscription> <harness> writes the config and the harness’s state directories (and, under an index, the harness’s instances[] entry), and refuses a harness that was not chosen, not declared at the pin, or whose needs nothing here holds. The tile is drawn from the snapshot (scripts/subscribed-harnesses.ts): it links nowhere, because nothing of it is published here, and a snapshot that cannot be read is a finding on the tile rather than an empty one.

85b133537be4.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
85b133537be4.title: Which harness / is — the landing is index-config’s rule
85b133537be4.content: The site’s landing page is one of the instantiated harnesses. It is never the instance the generator happens to live in, and never the repository’s name. Which one it is — site.landing in the root index.config.json (an instance name or "hub"), or the per-config site.landing flag without an index — is index-config’s rule. resolveLandingInstance in schemas/kg/harness-config.ts reads both, and check:landing-instance is the gate. When the landing is the neutral hub, / is the harness listing (harness_details.html, these tiles) and the todo panel — the landing sticky panel, not a second board.

312f09395f95.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
312f09395f95.title: “Harness” carries TWO senses, and only one of them is this rule
312f09395f95.content: | sense | what it means | how you tell | . | 1 — instantiated here | this checkout runs it | an entry in the root index.config.json instances[] — or, in a folio with no index, a root <name>.config.json (index-config). Read the file, not a number quoted here | . | 2 — a layer others instantiate | a base a downstream repo stands up | nothing in this checkout. It is a statement about the layer’s role in the stack | . The rules on this page are about sense 1. Sense 2 is correct usage too: a layer can be declared, not instantiated, and declare no visualiser — so it owes no tile — while being exactly what a downstream repository instantiates. No count is given for either sense, because a count in prose is a claim nothing checks; ask the filesystem. Do not write a checker for this. A predicate on the word cannot separate its two senses, so it is an adjudication, not a check (adjudication). When the word is load-bearing, say which sense — “instantiated here” or “a layer downstream repos instantiate”.

96cb0ad553a8.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
96cb0ad553a8.title: A tile opens the INSTANCE, not a kind handler’s view of it
96cb0ad553a8.content: A viewer page is a RENDERING with its own IRI, separate from the asset it shows; see kg-viewer §”The asset and its rendering are two resources with two IRIs”. scripts/mount-instance-docs.ts carries the two routes: . | route | handler | what it is | . | /<kind>/<instance>/ | the kind’s, cat-harness’s | the default rendering any instance declaring that kind gets | . | /<instance>/ | the instance itself | its own themed root | . The tile’s target is the instance’s own themed root when it has one, and a handler’s viewer only when it does not. The viewers stay reachable, listed beneath. An instance has that root when it has its own site directory, read from its own declaration — never by probing the BUILT site, where an instance whose pages are generated at build time has none until its generator runs.

8187b4446f1f.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
8187b4446f1f.title: Order is the declared dependency stack, reversed
8187b4446f1f.content: Bottom to top, computed from the declared needs, never written out as names: a name list is a rule true only for the instances somebody remembered. The spine’s head keeps the top and its floor keeps the bottom. An instance whose layer nobody declared is undetermined — placed below the head, alphabetically, carrying a finding that says its place is not derived. Absent is not []: one is nobody having said, the other is an instance asserting it sits on nothing. A broken graph does not blank the navbar. flattenDependencies returns an empty order on a cycle, which is right for a pipeline and wrong for a sidebar, where showing nothing hides every instance over one typo. The problems are reported and the list falls back to alphabetical.

83f386d3e5f8.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
83f386d3e5f8.title: Two gaps, reported rather than hidden
83f386d3e5f8.content: Both are the third state, and they are DIFFERENT findings: . | declared and not rendered — a graph the instance declares with no published page. Not linked (a dead link reads as “this site is broken”), and reported. | rendered and not declared — a page published under a kind the instance does not declare. Also not linked, because the declaration decides what a tile may claim to show — and reported, because staying silent would hide a working viewer behind a rule, and the remedy is one line in a declaration. | .

14829bcc212a.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
14829bcc212a.title: An inert row SAYS why, and “no viewer” is four answers
14829bcc212a.content: A declared graph with no published viewer appears in the navbar as a row that does not open. Drawing it grey is not saying it: . | A title on a non-focusable element is a label for a pointer and for nothing else — no keyboard path, and not reliably announced. | Dimming alone is state carried by contrast, and can pass the contrast ratio while saying nothing. | . The reason is content: real text in the row. It is in the accessibility tree, survives a stylesheet that does not load, and cannot disagree with a second signal. Do not use aria-disabled — nothing is a control, and marking a <span> disabled announces a widget that does not exist. “No viewer” is four states, told apart by inertNote (harness-tiles.ts): . | state | the row says | is it a gap? | . | declared publish: "staging-only" | staging only | no — withheld on purpose | . | instance declares renderExemption.of: ["visualiser"] | no viewer by design | no | . | a viewer exists off the conventional path | viewer not published | yes, and a different one | . | nothing declares a viewer | no viewer yet | yes | . One wording for all four would label an intended state a gap, which is as wrong as hiding a real gap. Neither navbar picks the words. They render what the generator gave them, which keeps them one navbar rather than two that agree by maintenance. A kind the generator said nothing about renders with no claim about why.

abd3ed5c9efc.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
abd3ed5c9efc.title: A tile, or an avatar? WHO DECLARED IT
abd3ed5c9efc.content: A tile is what the HARNESS declares. An avatar is what the FOLIO holds. | the thing | renders as | because | . | a declared visualiser (the harness’s visualisers) — over a directory or sub-graph | tile, functional | the harness declares it; §”A tile is the harness’s” above | . | a set of schema instances — todos | tile, content | the harness declares the set; the instances are the folio’s | . | a note, a document, a materialised asset in the folio’s reproduce directories (library/, uploads/) | avatar | the folio holds it; it is the reader’s, not the harness’s | . A TILE IS ONE OF TWO KINDS, and they bind to different things . |   | functional tile | content tile | . | subject | a directory or sub-graph | a set of schema instances | . | bound to | a SKILL | a SCHEMA | . | resolved when opened | a tool that implements the skill | the instances | . | what empty means | a gap to report — a skill nothing implements is unreachable | a real state — “nothing outstanding” is not “broken” | . A functional tile names the SKILL, never the tool. schemas/tools/tool-types.ts makes tools that satisfy one skill interchangeable, so a tile bound to a tool breaks the moment another tool is chosen. Likewise VisualiserDeclarationSchema takes “one path, or several visualisations”: a sub-graph may be rendered more than one way. Empty is asymmetric. A content tile opening on zero instances is CORRECT and must not be hidden — an empty board and a person with nothing outstanding are opposite facts. A functional tile whose skill has no tool is a gap to report. THEME IS NOT A THIRD KIND. A theme is a palette and its art; a tile takes the avatar’s declared hue. Theme is how either one looks, never an alternative to being a tile. Size does not decide it . A whole materialised knowledge graph (such as cat-bootstrap or cat-harness) on the glass renders as an avatar. So these two tempting rules are wrong: . | “Many behind it → tile, one → avatar” — a materialised graph is many things and is an avatar. | “Opens a viewer over a set → tile” — opening that avatar opens a viewer over a set, and it is still an avatar. | . Declaration ownership decides: a materialised asset is in the reader’s folio however big it is. The same subject can be both. todos is a content tile in the strip and an individual todo is an avatar on the glass: the tile is bound to the SCHEMA and the avatar is one INSTANCE of it. What is checkable here, and what is not . Tile-vs-avatar is not. Nothing classifies a folio item; the rule governs authoring, and the renderer reads the graph an item came from, so a gate would be a declared property whose check cannot answer its own claim. “A functional tile names the skill, never the tool” IS: a declared visualisation naming a tool id where a skill name belongs is decidable against knownSkills() and the Tool graph. No such tile exists yet, so nothing is gated today.

504509cbac53.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
504509cbac53.title: The navbar icon row is DECLARED, and three states is not two
504509cbac53.content: navbarIcons on the instance declaration. A closed set — close, todos, beans, processes, kg, fsh-guts, qr, launcher — because a free string lets an instance name an icon nothing draws. Seven is the cap and it is refused, never truncated: silently dropping an eighth entry would overrule the instance’s decision. fsh-guts is a control, like launcher: a button that opens the discarded-items list and carries its live count, not a link. It is also the way back the discard confirmation names, so that dialog says “the fish in the icon row” only when this icon is on the page, and points at Page settings otherwise (board-windows §”Send to fsh-guts asks first”). | declared | means | . | absent | inherit — walk needs, site owner as the floor | . | [] | show none | . | a list | this instance’s own answer | . Absent and [] must not collapse. The guard is !== undefined, never a truthiness test: a truthiness test turns “nobody has said” into “nothing to show”, and makes an instance that has not declared the field indistinguishable from one that wants a bare navbar. The distinction is kept at every layer: resolveNavbarIcons returns undefined for undetermined, harness-tiles.ts omits the field rather than writing [], sync-docs-harness.ts emits null, and the client draws no row and says so once. The walk is needs, not a second traversal. Nearest declaration wins, breadth-first toward the foundation — the direction resolveSkillDirs already composes. A new walk would be a second answer to “what is this instance built on”, free to disagree with the first. Destinations are looked up, never written down. They come from the instance’s own declared visualisations plus siteLinks, so an icon whose graph this instance does not publish gets no href and renders as a non-link. close and launcher carry no href on purpose: they drive controls on the page, and an href would make them look like navigation.

d04901f64f10.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
d04901f64f10.title: The theme avatar: the assignment is theme-mediated
d04901f64f10.content: The navbar’s mark is the instance’s theme card art, clipped — not its icon. The chain: . instance → its sticky contribution → the sticky’s theme → the theme’s imageRole → the instance’s images carrying that role → the card layout → its avatarRegion . resolveThemeBackdrop is the join and returns the DeclaredImage, so the crop comes with it. An indirection is not an absence: look through the theme before concluding no assignment exists. Take the card layout, not laptop or mobile. KgImageSchema refuses a non-square avatarRegion in pixels, and only the square crop can satisfy that: equal fractions on a landscape image give a box wider than tall, and the clip scales width and height separately. A card with no declared crop is a finding, not an avatar: the whole composition squeezed into a small frame is unreadable. Report it and fall back to the mark.

fe3ed5a0a42b.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
fe3ed5a0a42b.title: Where a tile lives, and what it must not eat
fe3ed5a0a42b.content: Tiles render in the navbar and on the glass: one declaration, per-surface visibility, never two registries. The sticky board carries NO tiles. | Removing a surface loses nothing only if the others still carry it. Every tile this repository declares names navbar and glass, so each stays reachable. A tile that named ONLY a surface that is not mounted would vanish silently — report it, do not re-route it on the author’s behalf. | board stays a legal value in TILE_SURFACES, and nothing mounts it, so existing declarations that name it stay valid (the “every field but ref is optional” rule in schemas/kg/cat-harness.ts). A declaration saying ["board"] alone is valid and renders no tile; the graph-tiles e2e asserts both halves. | . They are collapsible, with the count on the summary so a collapsed list still says how much is behind it — a fixed-height sidebar of tiles must not push the page nav off the top. Theming comes from the avatar’s declared hue: one hue, both schemes derived, so no tile can be legible in one mode and invisible in the other. A per-instance palette would be a second colour vocabulary beside theme.ts.

b92d8335c074.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
b92d8335c074.title: On a folio’s own site, a tile describes the FOLIO
b92d8335c074.content: A page’s tiles describe the instance whose site the page is on. A folio’s own Pages site (an IG repository’s folio-site.yml, a document folio’s folio-staging.yml) wears the platform’s chrome, and the platform’s _data/harness.json comes with it: tiles, counts, icon row, rail scopes and title, every path root-relative to the platform’s site. Unscoped, the folio’s badges show the platform’s counts and its links 404. cat-harness-tools/scripts/lib/foreign-site-scope.ts applies the rule to the data, once, for both passes (compose-docs --shell --instance, and rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site): . | the link points at | on a folio’s site it | count | . | the folio’s own root (/<instance>/…) | resolves inside the folio’s baseurl | kept | . | a page the folio’s declaration publishes at its site’s root (/beans/), when the folio IS the checkout’s root (rootOwnPages) | stays root-relative, on the folio’s own site | kept | . | another instance’s state graph (work items, todos, QA, health, uploads …) | is not linked; the icon says why in words | none | . | a platform content, context or derived graph (skills, processes, tools, schemas, docs …) | is re-based, absolute, onto DOCS_SITE_BASE, with its qualifier shown | none | . | a kind nothing classifies | is treated as state | none | . The state row is unlinked rather than shown at zero or re-based. Per schemas/ui/tile-count.ts, absent is a third state, never 0: a folio that declares no beans graph has said nothing about work items. Showing 0 would be a claim, and showing the platform’s number answers the folio’s question with somebody else’s. The icon keeps its place and its accessible name says, for example, *“ declares no beans graph"* (§"An inert row SAYS why"). Ownership is decided by where the link points, never by a kind of the same name. A folio that declares a qa directory does not borrow the platform’s QA tile and its count; borrowing it because the word matched would put the platform’s number back on the folio’s page. A count beside a borrowed link is dropped too: the link is accurate, but the number would still sit on the folio’s page next to the folio’s own. The qualifier is shown instead, so the tile reads as the platform’s. The host’s count projections are not chrome. compose-docs --shell leaves out every assets/**.json that declares a headline tile count, as it does _includes/generated/. A badge whose file 404s renders as ABSENT, with no number. A figure that is not a tile follows the same rule: . | figure | it came from | on a folio’s site it | count | . | the translation sweep badge | _data/translation-qa.json, the platform’s | the shell leaves the file out; the badge stays, inert, reading “QA: not published”, and says why: *“ publishes no translation QA sweep on this site"* | none, and not “not run”, which would be a claim about the folio | . | the navbar’s locale swap | _data/translations.json, the platform’s index of its own pages | the shell leaves the file out; the index reads as null, “could not determine”, and the navbar stays as built | n/a | . | the fsh-guts fish | a button whose count is fetched from this site’s /fsh-guts.json | the button is drawn only when the folio links its OWN fsh-guts; otherwise the fish is the row’s re-based link, named *“the platform’s: declares no fsh-guts graph"*, or an inert icon with the note | none, never ”?”: ? means the read failed | . A folio that publishes its own sweep or fsh-guts document gets its own figure back with no further change: foreignSite.absent (written by scopeHarnessData) only supplies the words for when the site carries nothing. The two _data/ files are named in HOST_DATA_PROJECTIONS, since neither declares what it describes. foreign-site-scope.test.ts fails on a shell that carries a _data/ file nobody has classified as chrome or projection. A folio that IS the root of its own site (for example one whose site is generated rather than a Jekyll tree) needs four more things: . | Its declared pages are its own. Its visualisers under its own site directory publish at the site root, by the same ownsSite || isRepoRoot rule siteDirMount gives its icon (harness-tiles.ts), and the scope keeps them (ForeignScope.ownPages). | The icon row’s own paths and counts resolve on the folio’s site. After scoping, every root-relative href left in the row is the folio’s, and so is the count.json its badge fetches. rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site writes the row’s data-fa-root as the page’s own site root (rowRoot), while its script and style still load from the platform (assetRoot). | Its mark loads from its own site (ownsCheckout). | An image mark can sit on the rail itself. The rail draws the instance’s tone square behind every avatar; a declared image with ground: "none" (KgImageSchema) is drawn with no tone. | . The pinned rail reserves its width. Hover and focus open the bar over the page, as a peek; pinning keeps it open, so .main moves over (docs-ui.css). The gate is foreign-site-scope.test.ts. It runs both foreign-site passes over a folio and asserts (a) no tile carries another instance’s count or links its state graph, (b) no href is left root-relative unless it is the folio’s own path, (c) the platform’s translation sweep and index are not shipped and the rendered head_custom.html hands the badge its words, and (d) the fish fetches no count from a site that has no fsh-guts. The client halves are in translation-badges.e2e.ts and navbar-row.e2e.ts. A check of a page’s chrome has to run on a site that is not the platform’s, because on the platform’s own site the platform’s tiles are right by construction.

a76e238774e5.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
a76e238774e5.title: The glass strip — pinned first, and “+N more” counts the rest
a76e238774e5.content: No tile may be silently off-screen: a reader cannot tell a tile scrolled out of view from a tile that does not exist. | The pinned set is DECLARED, never written into a surface. glassStrip on the instance’s declaration lists the pins in order: { "chrome": … } for the glass’s own controls (todos, filter, settings) and { "kind": … } for a graph typology. It is inherited along needs like navbarIcons, so absent inherits and [] pins nothing. sync-docs-harness.ts resolves each kind to ONE tile (resolveGlassStrip): the directory named for the kind, else the first glass tile that holds it. A kind several harnesses publish gets one slot, and the others wait in More, where their qualifiers tell them apart. A pinned kind that no tile holds is reported in glassStrip.unmatched and never skipped silently. | Fit, not scroll. The strip shows as many pins as fit at the current width, in declared order, and refits whenever its box changes. It never scrolls sideways (scrollWidth <= clientWidth is asserted at 1280×800 and 390×844). | The last tile says “+N more”, and N is exact. N counts every tile not on screen: pins with no room at this width, plus everything the reader keeps in More. Shown + N is always the total. The tile is a button named “N more tiles”; it opens More and moves focus into it. Pins that did not fit come first in More, marked as pinned. | The reader may still arrange. A strip the reader has arranged, by dragging or with the Strip and More buttons, overrides the declared default in that browser. The fit and the count apply to their arrangement too. | It starts HIDDEN. With no stored choice, the folio opens with the strip slid away. Only its tab shows, reading “Show tiles (N)”. The tab is the one control both ways (board-windows) and carries aria-expanded. The reader’s choice is remembered in this browser as 1 or 0, and storage that cannot be read counts as no choice: hidden. | . glass-strip-fit.e2e.ts holds the four fit assertions and glass-strip-default-hidden.e2e.ts the default.

2605c72dee00.doc: A tile is the harness's, not the node's
2605c72dee00.title: summary and alsoWritten — what a reader sees, kept apart from why it was named
2605c72dee00.content: A harness section on the landing page shows the declaration’s summary, a one-line gloss, and lists alsoWritten, the other spellings of the name. A description made to carry them shows the reader a naming rationale or spellings that render as one line. Authoring notes belong in description or a _comment. The reader-facing line goes in summary, and alternative spellings go in alsoWritten as a list, never inline. A harness’s sticky shows the same text as the landing page. A sticky contribution declares bodyFrom: "summary", and the card’s words are readerText in schemas/content/sticky-contribution.ts: the summary (else the description), then the alsoWritten spellings after “Also written:”. That is the rule docs/_includes/harness_details.html applies, read from the same two declaration fields, so there is no copy of the text to keep in step. bodyFrom: "description" still parses, because the pinned bootstrap/bootstrap.json declares it. bun run cat landing:sticky:check fails when a card built from its declaration does not open with that text. A bodyAppend may follow the reader’s text, and a card with a literal body is not compared.
