1bf70334b4e4.title: ig-publisher-fork
1bf70334b4e4.content: Skill id: ig-publisher-fork · Package: fhir-ig-base · Instance: fhir-harness . The brief for an agent taking a local, experimental fork of the FHIR IG Publisher, so that an AST can be emitted and cached.

b90acddfb069.title: Which repositories, and why only one
b90acddfb069.content: | repository | holds | needed for | . | HL7/fhir-ig-publisher | orchestration, the loaded resources, DependencyAnalyser, CqlSubSystem, the metadata exports | the dump, the toolchain record, the logic-layer dependency edges | . | hapifhir/org.hl7.fhir.core | the renderer, the validator, dependency loading | page-fragment provenance only | . The logic-layer edges are a publisher-side gap, not a core one: . | DependencyAnalyser is in the publisher (org.hl7.fhir.publisher.core/.../igtools/publisher/). Its analysePD and analyseAD are empty stubs, and Library and Measure are not dispatched. That is the whole criterion-2 gap. | CqlSubSystem already attaches CQL depends-on to each Library (AdjunctFileLoader), so Library→Library edges exist in memory; nothing exports them. | . Only page-fragment provenance needs core. Read upstream before re-quoting either claim.

0901e8fdd493.title: The shape taken: a library ON TOP, not a fork IN it
0901e8fdd493.content: Do not change existing Publisher code unless there is no other way: remarshal, reuse, subclass. The work is ast-export/, a separate Maven project on branch claude/ast-export of litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher. It depends on the released org.hl7.fhir.publisher.core from Maven Central, is not a module of the root pom, and changes no Publisher file. | AstPublisher extends Publisher and overrides nothing. It reads getFileList() after execute(). | AstFieldsAccess is a read-only view of package-private PublisherFields, declared in the Publisher’s package inside the library. A rename upstream fails to compile rather than failing at run time. | Upstream’s DependencyAnalyser is reused unchanged; LogicEdges sits beside it. | . That makes “behind a flag, default byte-identical” true by construction for the Publisher itself: a stock build never loads the library. What still needs measuring is that AstExportCli’s own build writes the same output/ as a stock one.

8cac4108af2f.title: The tools an agent runs
8cac4108af2f.content: In the fork, under ast-export/: . | tool | what | network | . | scripts/run-real-igs.sh [work] [--byte-identical] | W1/W2 on the WHO SMART Trust IG and the WHO SMART Immunizations IG, W2 per resource type | packages.fhir.org, tx.fhir.org | . | scripts/w7-round.sh <work> | one incremental round on a one-CQL-file change | same | . | AstExportCli, AstPlanCli, IncrementalBuildCli | export, plan a delta, rebuild the cone | export and rebuild: yes; plan: no | . Here, ig-ast-delta lists, checks, diffs and renders what those produce. The one CI path is .github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml: it runs AstExportCli on a runner, at the pinned commit, to refresh an IG’s AST cache, calling the same exporter and ig-cache.sh. ig-build-pipeline §”The AST cache lifecycle” owns it. Any other CI calls these same scripts.

359ff148acfc.title: Without packages.fhir.org: seeding the cache from trusted sources
359ff148acfc.content: Some environments reach GitHub and registry.npmjs.org but not packages.fhir.org. The seeder fills the FHIR package cache from sources that are each a trust anchor: named by the owner, or the package’s own publisher. Nothing else is consulted. There are two copies: ast-export/scripts/seed-fhir-cache-from-npm.py in the fork, which ig-ast-refresh.yml runs, and scripts/fhir-cache-seed-npm.ts here, which the Tool fhir-cache-seed-npm invokes. | source | trust | what it holds | . | npm, account grahamegrieve | owner: trusted. Grahame Grieve founded HL7 FHIR | mostly the latest version of each HL7 package; core packages under @hl7/ | . | a publisher’s own published-site repository on GitHub | the publisher’s own published site | every released version that publisher hosts there | . | a template’s own repo at HEAD | FHIR/ig-registry/templates.json names it; owner: fhir.base.template is trusted | templates, #current included | . | --mirror | whoever ran mirror-fhir-packages.sh (Tool fhir-package-mirror) | what the others lack | . Rules: . | Exact versions only. A pin is never satisfied by another version; there is no “approximate” build with substituted versions. The one exception is the Publisher’s own rule: a patch wildcard (1.1.x) resolves to the highest 1.1.N a source lists, and the resolution is recorded. | Verified. npm tarballs against npm’s sha512. Every other source must carry a package/package.json naming exactly the requested package and version. npm’s 0.0.1-security malicious-package placeholder is refused. | Nothing computed once and kept. Load from the repositories every run; do not compute once and assume it fixed. The template registry, the IHE folder listing and any mirror clone are fetched fresh every run into a scratch directory deleted at exit. There is no table of package locations that could go stale behind the registry. | Provenance in ast-export-npm-provenance.json: the source, URL or commit, and hash of every package. | . Where it stands, measured over the WHO SMART Trust and Immunizations IGs: 20 packages install, including both templates. Missing are the pinned HL7 versions (IPS, terminology, extensions, CQL, CRMI, SDC, IPA), fhir.cqf.common and us.nlm.vsac. To close the gap: . | Run the seeder with --missing-out missing.txt. | Run mirror-fhir-packages.sh <repo> missing.txt on a machine that reaches packages.fhir.org. | Run the seeder again with --mirror <repo>. | . What the declared dependencies miss. Seeding from sushi-config.yaml alone leaves the build short (Publisher 3.0.0 / core 7.0.1): . | The template. It is named in ig.ini, not in sushi-config.yaml, so pass it to the seeder as a positional name#version. | A template seeded from its repo keeps the repo’s layout. The template’s own files go at the top of the cache entry, and only package.json goes under package/. The Publisher reads a cached template with NpmPackage.fromFolder, which files a top-level file under package/$root and unpacks it into template/. A file under package/ lands in template/package/, and the build fails with template/config.json not found. | Packages the Publisher loads by itself: . | hl7.fhir.pubpack at CommonPackages.VER_PUBPACK; | hl7.fhir.xver-extensions at CommonPackages.VER_XVER; | hl7.fhir.uv.tools.r<N> at Publisher.TOOLING_IG_CURRENT_RELEASE, for the IG’s FHIR release; | the latest milestone of hl7.terminology.r<N> and hl7.fhir.uv.extensions.r<N>, when the IG does not declare them. Read the versions from the release you build against. Never copy them from here, because they move with each release. | . | “Latest” offline is not exact. When it cannot reach the registry, getLatestVersion falls back to the highest version in the local cache. That silently breaks the exact-versions rule. Mirror the version the registry lists today, and record which version it was. | . An offline validator crash that is not ours. In core 7.0.1, InstanceValidator.checkTypeValue fetches the approved additional resources from fhir.github.io. When that fetch fails it dereferences a null set, so the build fails with an NPE on additionalResourceNames. Only an environment that cannot reach fhir.github.io meets it. It is upstream’s bug (org.hl7.fhir.core), and it is not patched here, because the library does not change Publisher code. Build with a terminology server. A -tx n/a build, which is run-real-igs.sh --no-tx, is only for finding faults before the real run. Its numbers are never recorded as measurements. A template the registry does not list is named by the caller with --template-repo <name>=<owner/repo>, on the command line, never stored. Publishers’ site repositories. The fork’s seeder keeps one fixed table mapping a package-name prefix to the publisher’s own GitHub repo. It can drift, which is tolerated only because every package fetched through it must name itself exactly in its own package.json, so a stale entry fails as “missing”, never as a wrong package. The copy here holds no such table: the caller maps each prefix with --site-repo <prefix>=<owner/repo>[@branch], none by default, because which publishers exist is not something fhir-harness may know.

b2bf912f16a5.title: The measurement that justifies the work
b2bf912f16a5.content: Using the Publisher’s current metadata exports as an AST proxy across two real IGs: . | export | the WHO SMART Trust IG | the WHO SMART Immunizations IG | . | valueset-ref-list.json ValueSet→CodeSystem edges | 17 over 14 | 431 over 252 | . | codesystem-ref-list.json uses populated | 0 of 15 | 0 of 14 | . | usage-stats.json extension→path | 6 | 35 (+5 profiles) | . Two findings: . | uses is declared and never populated — in both IGs. | Nothing exports Library / PlanDefinition / Measure dependencies — 458 artefacts, 61 % of the WHO SMART Immunizations IG, the decision-logic core, with zero edges. | . Re-derive both before quoting them. If a later Publisher release closes either, the fork’s scope shrinks accordingly.

e52e69cd2cd5.title: Acceptance criteria
e52e69cd2cd5.content: The AST must carry: . | one structured record per resource, keyed by canonical URL and version — an id alone collides across versions | dependency edges among Library, PlanDefinition and Measure — the gap above. Built as LogicEdges; not yet measured on the WHO SMART Immunizations IG. Measured as: every logic resource has at least one logic-to-logic edge in either direction. In graph terms, no vertex is isolated. Outgoing edges alone cannot be the test, because a finite acyclic dependency graph always has a sink: a library that others depend on and that depends on no logic itself. run-real-igs.sh prints both counts. | uses actually populated, or an explicit statement that it cannot be — a declared-and-empty field is worse than an absent one, because a consumer cannot tell “no dependencies” from “not computed” | page-fragment provenance — which source produced which output fragment, so a rendered page can be traced without re-running | the resolved dependency closure with pinned versions | terminology expansion provenance — which server, which version, and whether expansion actually happened; a build against a dead tx must be distinguishable from an IG with thin ValueSets | a toolchain object — publisher version, core version, SUSHI version. publisher.jar is re-downloaded from the latest release on every WHO build, so without this an AST cannot say what produced it | . And the fork itself must satisfy: . | emitted behind a flag, with default behaviour byte-identical when the flag is absent | upstreamable shape — a flag and an additional writer, not a rewrite; a fork that cannot be offered back has no exit | no change to validation or rendering semantics. If a fork build’s qa.json differs from an upstream build’s on the same input, that is a defect in the fork, and it is the first thing to check | .

7a4eac37d371.title: What the agent must not do
7a4eac37d371.content: . | Do not treat the AST as an authority. It is a cache: its indices, dependency edges and versions are unverified until a full run. Anything written to consume it says so — see ig-publisher-reduction §P3. | Do not vendor either repository into this one. The fork lives at its own remote; exactly one repository runs a thing. | Do not add WHO, DAK or SMART concepts to the fork. The AST is a property of a FHIR IG. A DAK-shaped field in it makes the fork unofferable upstream and breaks the layering fhir-harness exists to keep. | Do not fix uses by inferring it. If the information is not there, report that it is not there. An inferred edge in a dependency graph is indistinguishable from a real one downstream, and every ordering metric computed from it becomes unfalsifiable. | .

8edb10127bb2.title: Reporting
8edb10127bb2.content: A fork round reports: which repositories at which commits, which criteria are met, which are not, and what was measured rather than what was implemented. A criterion is met when an AST from a real IG is shown to carry the thing. The WHO SMART Immunizations IG is the right subject: it carries the 61 % gap.

9e1f21ba0ba5.title: ig-publisher-reduction
9e1f21ba0ba5.content: Skill id: ig-publisher-reduction · Package: fhir-ig-base · Instance: fhir-harness . Get to the point where the IG Publisher is needed only to produce an AST and a QA record, with rendering owned by the just-the-docs pipeline. During iteration and staging, an IG is rendered from its cached AST; its generated /html is not mounted. Two changes are separable: stop mounting generated HTML (a rendering change) and cache an AST (a build change). The phases do the first before the second, because the first is verifiable without a fork and the second is not.

a48b6763b34f.title: What the Publisher does that a cache cannot fake
a48b6763b34f.content: . | Profile validation against the declared FHIR version. | Dependency-closure resolution with version pinning — hl7.terminology, hl7.fhir.uv.cql, hl7.fhir.uv.cpg, hl7.fhir.uv.crmi, hl7.fhir.uv.sdc for the WHO SMART Base IG. | Terminology expansion against a tx server. | . None is reproducible from its own output. The end state is the Publisher invoked for these, not the Publisher gone.

3354d644931c.title: The phases
3354d644931c.content: |   | does | exit criterion — MEASURED | . | P0 | re-point the metadata→variables bridge; render one IG’s input/pages/ through just-the-docs | the WHO SMART Trust IG’s pages render with Publisher metadata populating the Jekyll variables, and every page the Publisher renders for that IG is accounted for as exactly one of: matched (this site renders it), refused under P2 (an XML/Turtle view, in P2’s refusal record), or on the fork’s ask (rendered from data the Publisher does not export, listed with the data it needs). A page in none is a gap; P0 passes with zero gaps, and nothing is silently excepted | . | P1 | derive navigation from sushi-config.yaml’s pages: and menu: | the derived navigation is diffed against the Publisher’s, one diff per IG, and each difference is empty or explained entry by entry; the per-IG diffs are also reported together, answering “what are the differences in IG1, IG2, … IGN?” (scripts/ig-nav-diff.ts) | . | P2 | JSON-only representations; XML/TTL dropped from the render path, and not linked | every dropped representation is recorded as a refusal, per IG with the same combined view as P1, so “publishes no Turtle” and “we ignored its Turtle” stay distinguishable (scripts/p2-refusals.ts, p2:refusals:check) | . | P3 | AST dump behind a flag on the fork; staging renders from cached AST | a staging page built from cache carries a visible stale-until-full-run mark, and a reader can tell which facts are provisional — the AST comes from the fork, which is a prerequisite | . | P4 | Publisher invoked for AST + QA only | a release is still cut from a full build, and the artefact says which it came from | . P4 in practice: the refresh rebuilds a stale cache incrementally; a release step refuses an incremental AST (ig-ast.ts build-kind --require-full), and the site’s folio-build.json records which kind of build it came from (ast.kind). See ig-build-pipeline, “The AST cache lifecycle”. fsh-cone’s source edges (below) are useful for rebuild cones, but they do not replace the fork for P3: the AST is the Publisher’s. P0 is a re-point, not a build . The metadata half: the ig-site-data tool writes site.data.fhir (ig.* from the ImplementationGuide resource, packageId, canonical) for one IG — from the FHIR AST first (the ImplementationGuide resource in output-ast/), then sushi-config.yaml or a published IG’s fhir-artifact-index for what the AST lacks. It reports a field the AST and sushi-config state differently, lists every field it cannot source instead of writing an empty string, and refuses a source describing another package. fhir-harness declares site.data as a pass-through Liquid prefix, so the platform’s value resolver leaves {{ site.data.fhir.… }} for Jekyll and the Publisher alike. The per-artefact half: build-ig-site.ts (artifactVariables) writes site.data.fhir.artifacts.<Type>__<id> with the families and keys of generate_smart_liquid.py’s variables — url (canonical, page, json), text.display, link.html and elements.<key> — lifted, not redesigned. They carry no smart__ prefix (that prefix is WHO’s) and are computed in the same Jekyll run that consumes them, so the surface converges in one build. There is no url.xml or url.ttl (P2). P1’s exit criterion is a diff . “Navigation looks right” is not a criterion. sushi-config.yaml’s pages: is an ordered map and menu: carries the grouping, so the derived navigation is computable and so is the Publisher’s — compare them. An entry that differs is either a bug or a deliberate improvement, and saying which is the work. P3 is where the honesty lives . A staging build from cached AST is provisional: its indices and dependencies may not be valid until a full IG Publisher run. The contract: . An AST is a CACHE, never an authority. Anything rendered from one declares, in the artefact a reader sees, that its indices, dependency edges and versions are unverified until a full run. A stale mark that exists only in a log does not satisfy it: a page that silently serves stale dependencies looks exactly like one that does not. P3 is BLOCKED on more than a fork . Nothing in the Publisher’s current exports carries dependencies among Libraries, PlanDefinitions or Measures — 458 artefacts, 61 % of the WHO SMART Immunizations IG (Library 279 + PlanDefinition 138 + Measure 41 of 748), the CQL and decision-logic core. The index’s field set is canonical, category, dak, description, id, key, materialization, name, published, resourceType, title, version — there is no edge field, so the exit criterion is unsatisfiable against this export, not merely hard. An AST that stops at terminology cannot support iterative deltas over the part of an IG that actually changes. Re-derive that 61 % before quoting it. A second route to the edges, with no fork . scripts/fsh-cone.ts builds the same IG’s graph from source — .fsh + .cql — where the index is the Publisher’s output. scripts/measure-logic-layer-edges.ts compares the two on the WHO SMART Immunizations IG: . | The 458 map onto FSH source 1:1, zero unmatched ids. | After FSH RuleSet parameter substitution — what SUSHI does before the Publisher sees a resource — 458 of 458 logic artefacts carry an edge to another logic artefact, verified per resource type. | . So P3 does not depend on a fork for the existence of logic-layer edges; those are in the IG source at full per-artefact resolution. What the fork uniquely delivers is resolved, version-pinned, cross-package edges. Two things in fsh-cone make that true: . | The Library→CQL edge matches on node.id ?? node.name: Library instances usually omit Id: and rely on SUSHI’s name→id default. | A library canonical inside a parameterised RuleSet (* library = Canonical({library}Logic) in PlanDefMain(library, version), or a string URL in MeasureProportionBasic reached through a second level) is found by buildFshGraph substituting the RuleSet’s positional arguments into its body before scanning. Such edges are tagged insert (parameter expanded). | . Current figures on the WHO SMART Immunizations IG: 3,329 internal edges, 469 distinct targets across the 458, 354 nodes with no dependent, backward-cone median 11, largest forward cone 856. Break any coverage number down by resource type. An aggregate can read 99.8 % while every artefact points at the same shared RuleSet, so the graph cannot tell one Library from another. Rebuild fraction . Replaying 257 commits on the corrected graph, the mean rebuild per commit is 23.5 %; each graph with missing edges gave a lower figure (8.2–16.0 %). Do not quote a rebuild fraction without saying which graph produced it — an incremental build sized from an under-connected graph under-rebuilds, which is the failure fsh-cone’s header calls dangerous. Whether ~24 % of an IG per commit pays for the machinery is an open question, separate from whether the edges exist. What a source edge cannot carry . The source graph answers which artefact is stale, not what a reader must be told. It cannot carry: . | Version pinning. resolveRef strips |version, and PlanDefMain takes library and version as separate parameters that are never associated. The graph cannot tell a dependency on X|1.0.0 from one on X|2.0.0. | Cross-package references. Dropped by design — InstanceOf contributes 3 edges across the whole IG, because 179 of the 458 are InstanceOf: a cpg/cqfmeasures profile URL that resolves into a dependency package. | Rendering-time coupling. Invisible to it; a cone is a lower bound. | Compiled truth. RuleSet substitution is a partial reimplementation of SUSHI: it handles positional {param} substitution, nested inserts and multi-line argument lists, but not soft indexing, a RuleSet’s defaults, or SUSHI’s context-sensitive rules. An edge it derives is a claim about the source, not the compiled resource; the insert (parameter expanded) tag says which claims rest on that substitution. | . So the source route supplies the dependency-edge third of P3’s visible mark and the rebuild set behind it, the index third only as a lower bound, and the version third not at all. ig-publisher-fork closes P3 for versions and package closure.

4d4e3144047e.title: What is NOT settled, and must not be decided by drift
4d4e3144047e.content: . | transform_dmn.py emits HTML, which the JSON-only contract does not take as a representation. Structured output, or embedded asset? Open. | “Parity-ish” needs a stated checklist of asset types and page kinds before MVP is declared. The ceiling is a data limit: a page kind whose source the Publisher does not emit cannot be rendered at any effort, and belongs on the fork’s ask rather than on the parity list. | Whether P4 keeps a tx dependency in staging. Expansion is the slowest step and the one most likely to be unavailable offline. | .

62214868414c.title: Do not
62214868414c.content: . | Declare a phase done on an impression. Each criterion above is a measurement or a diff; if you cannot run it, the phase is not done. | Collapse P2 into P0. Dropping representations while the renderer is also changing makes a missing page and a refused representation indistinguishable. | Treat a green gate set as a rendered page. Look at the rendered site (preview:site): generator output can look right while kramdown gives many headings one anchor. | .

ece61549d888.title: IG publisher + validator — the role’s contract
ece61549d888.content: ig-publisher-service in scenarios/roles.json is played by a mechanical actor (actorKinds: ["system"]; scenarios/actors/ig-publisher-service.json, which runs in the folio-assistant-smart-guidelines image). A role played by a machine is still a role, and its skills are its contract: the responsibilities it must perform, which a test can hold it to. Each line below cites the declaration it comes from.

fd6ac07e0a44.title: What it must do
fd6ac07e0a44.content: . | Build a FHIR Implementation Guide and report its QA — the actor’s description (“FHIR IG Publisher build and QA reporting”), and the qa-reporting action ODRL grants it in policies/ig-publisher-service.jsonld. | Complete the IG Publisher build with no errors in qa.html, after SUSHI has compiled the FSH — req:fhir-validation#ig-publisher-qa, which depends on #sushi-compile and which the ig-publisher capability (scenarios/capabilities/ig-publisher.json) declares it satisfies. | Validate individual resources and profiles against a package between builds — the fhir-validator capability, distinct from a whole-IG build. | Be detectable: each capability’s detection command answers --version / -version on a machine with a Java runtime (requires: ["java-runtime"]). | .

71cc3b02b783.title: What it is not asked
71cc3b02b783.content: . | To judge. The role is “external in behaviour, internal in configuration” (its description): it reports what the publisher found; whether a warning matters is the QC reviewer’s or the FHIR modeller’s call. | . No test in this repository runs the services — they run in a folio’s build, not here. The test in tested-by: holds lines 1–4 to what this repository declares: the actor and its ODRL grant, the two capabilities and their detection, and the requirement statement the publisher satisfies.

e9011accf96f.title: ig-render-jekyll
e9011accf96f.content: Skill id: ig-render-jekyll · Package: fhir-ig-base · Instance: fhir-harness . Render an IG’s pages as folio pages — markdown with front matter, through Jekyll and just-the-docs — from the Publisher’s structured output, never its finished HTML. Publisher HTML has no front matter, so the navbar, language bar, QA badges and translation surface cannot reach it; a folio page gets them all. Whether an IG repository gets this rendering is asked when it is adopted (default yes); see ig-build-pipeline §”Who starts a build”.

279855844bb1.title: The three contracts
279855844bb1.content: 1. JSON only . The Publisher emits JSON, XML and Turtle; only JSON is taken, wrapped in JSON-LD / JSON Schema. RDF, where needed, is projected from the JSON-LD. A representation that arrives and is not taken is recorded as a refusal. Not linked either. The site does not link a resource’s .xml or .ttl copy: JSON-LD nodes carry only JSON encodings, and the site.data artefact variables only url.json. The refusal record still counts what each IG published in those forms. 2. Navigation is derived, never authored . sushi-config.yaml already carries both maps the site needs: . | pages: — an ordered map of source file to title. That is the page order. | menu: — the grouping, including nested subsections. | . Derive the navigation from them. Do not hand-author a nav file or write entries back into sushi-config.yaml. When the config names a page that does not exist, that is a finding, not a reason to create a placeholder. 3. LHS rail, and the theme is captured rather than replaced . Navigation goes in the left-hand rail, not the FHIR IG’s top bar. The rest of the IG theme — CSS, typography, resource-page furniture — is captured into the theme layer rather than discarded. Nav position is a layout setting; nav contents are derived per build.

d33381f22d66.title: What the render reads in the IG repository
d33381f22d66.content: Only what the repository declares. Every reader on this path (build-ig-site, ig-site-data, ingest-ig-menu, ingest-ig-chrome, ig-repo-site) goes through scripts/ig-read-scope.ts, which honours contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json; anything outside it is not rendered. A repository with no section is read whole, with a warning. See ig-build-pipeline §”What this layer reads”.

df1893b2f743.title: Where the variables come from
df1893b2f743.content: artifactVariables (build-ig-site.ts) writes the per-artefact Liquid variables from the artefact index to _data/, read by the same Jekyll run: site.data.fhir.artifacts.<ResourceType>__<id> with url (canonical, page, json), text, link.html and elements.<key>, plus artifact_categories, artifacts_listed and artifact_lists. An element key the index does not hold is reported as not sourced, never written empty. The families and keys follow WHO’s generate_smart_liquid.py, a build script outside this layer, without its smart__ prefix: that prefix is WHO’s, and this layer does not know about WHO.

edac27f48893.title: What parity means, and what it does not
edac27f48893.content: Parity is a checklist of asset types and page kinds. A page kind the Publisher emits no data for cannot be rendered.

b36fc9541740.title: Thin pages, the default (--full-pages to opt out)
b36fc9541740.content: Every IG page is a thin HTML shell that loads its content from the JSON-LD graph, unless a build passes --full-pages. The shell is cat-harness-tools’ thinPageHtml. Artefact pages (gen-ig-pages.ts) . | Page address: artifact/<Type>-<id>.html, self-canonical. | The asset is a JSON-LD node, artifact/<Type>-<id>.jsonld with a .json twin, written by ig-artifact-jsonld.ts from the index (kind ig-artifact-jsonld; QA ig-artifact-jsonld.ts check over the built site). It uses the FHIR RDF class, dcterms, schema.org and PROV, and mints nothing. The page names the node as alternate. | One shared renderer. assets/ig-artifact.js fetches the node, then the resource’s local copy, draws the description, facts, identity table and elements, concepts or includes, and hands the narrative and JSON to ast-resource.js. The page carries only its title, key and a <noscript> link to the node and resource. | The rail is linked: folio-navbar: linked, and the rail pass (rail-standalone-pages.ts) links its style and scripts rather than inlining them. | The tab views are thin pages too, written beside the page wherever the site serves the artefact’s JSON: a compiled copy (--compiled-data) or, failing that, the Publisher’s own <Type>-<id>.json carried as data (--publisher-data <dir>, from the docs root). An IG repository’s site (ig-site:compose) passes only --compiled-data ast-data, the AST’s copy. Each view keeps the Publisher’s file name: . | -definitions: the snapshot’s element table, differential marked; | -mappings: each mapping declaration with the elements mapped to it; | the JSON view (.profile.json for a StructureDefinition, else .json), drawn by ast-resource.js; | -examples, for every StructureDefinition: the instances claiming it in meta.profile, or a note that there are none. | . Each uses the same shell (thinArtifactView) and renderer; the artefact’s page links them in a tab bar, and the narrative’s links to them are relinked. The change history, testing, XML and Turtle views are neither rendered nor published. The IG API view pages stay full pages. | Nothing under comparison-v*/ is published. ig-site:publisher-pages serves the AST’s data and reads no Publisher output. | In an IG site the docs root is the site root, so --compiled-data is ast-data; ../ast-data would point every resource link above the site. | . The artefact list and the table of contents (build-ig-site.ts) . | One index node, artifact/index.jsonld (family folio-ig-artifact-index-jsonld/v1, same kind), lists every artefact once, in the Publisher’s order, each entry naming its node and carrying only what a list row shows; check holds it to the artefact index and each node. | artifacts.html is a thin shell over that node: a jump list of categories, a filter, then every category open (nothing collapsed), anchored #artifacts-<slug>. | What a list draws: . | The IG’s own ImplementationGuide is “This guide”, drawn first (#artifacts-this-guide), never as a “Not categorised” row; the toc lists it first too. | A category that mixes resource types is sub-headed by type (#artifacts-<category>-<type>; the Publisher’s “Other”: Basic, Questionnaire, DocumentReference…), and the jump list counts each type. | A table draws only the columns its rows fill. An instance (an artefact with no canonical URL) has no description, so the index copies what the resource states: its meta.profile (dcterms:conformsTo, drawn as the last path segment, linked when it is in the same IG) and its code (dcterms:subject). A definition’s core profile (shareablevalueset) is not shown. | . | toc.html is a thin shell. The IG’s own pages (sushi-config.yaml pages:, landing page first) stay in its HTML; the artefacts under each category are drawn from the index node. | Both are written by stageIgSite when StageOptions.artifacts.index is given, which stage-ig-sites.ts does unless --full-pages. Staging thin a site whose artefact pages were generated with --full-pages (no index node) is refused. | . The narrative pages (composeIgSite) . | The IG’s prose stays in the HTML, rendered by Jekyll; composed into a host site, the page wears thinIgLayout (_layouts/ig-thin-<instance>.html) instead of the host’s layout, so none of the host’s chrome (harness bar, SVG sprite, sidebar nav, inline scripts) is written into it. | Everything around the prose is linked: assets/ig-artifact.css, assets/ig-topbar.css, assets/ig-source-links.js and the rail (folio-navbar: linked). The IG’s top bar, edit links, footer and TOC declaration stay. | The thin page has no host search box or QA badges; it has its own search box and language picker block (below). | . Search and the language picker . The folio rail replaces the theme’s side menu (#site-nav is dropped; IG_DROPPED in stage-local-ig.ts), and the IG’s top bar carries a search box over the IG’s pages and artefacts (ig-search.ts): . | ig-repo-site.ts compose writes the index, assets/ig-search.json (each IG page’s title and full text; each artefact’s title, id, name, key, canonical and description), and the client, assets/ig-search.js. The index is fetched on the box’s first focus, never on page load. | The box (form.ig-search, input #search-input) is in the composed pages’ .ig-topbar and the thin pages’ header.iga-top. It is not .search, so docs-ui leaves it in the top bar. A build that does not write the files (gen-ig-pages without --search, StageOptions.search unset) writes no box. | Any other built page lacking a box (for example an IG API hub page or openapi/index.html) gets one: publisher-pages puts a bar at the top of its body (header.ig-search-top: the IG’s name, the box, the picker’s slot; stampSearchBox, withSearchBar). The pass skips assets/ and runs only when the site serves a search index. | The language picker sits beside the box, in the empty <span data-fa-slot="locale"> that follows it, which docs-ui fills. A site with no IG bar keeps the picker in docs-ui’s band. | docs-ui draws the picker from a page’s fa-translation-meta block, which publisher-pages writes (cat-harness-tools lib/translation-meta.ts) into every built page lacking one, from the IG checkout’s translation declaration; set-html-lang.ts reads it afterwards. | . The root parity guard (cat-harness-tools site-parity.ts) refuses to publish a build lacking the search box or language block over a root that had them. The opt-out . gen-ig-pages.ts --full-pages and stage-ig-sites.ts --full-pages build full pages (composeIgSite(…, { fullPages: true })). Pass both or neither. --thin is a no-op; --thin --full-pages is refused.

376882aec8f6.title: What this does not replace
376882aec8f6.content: Which AST the pages are drawn from. An IG repository’s site is drawn from the AST on its cache branch, cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id>, which a Publisher run on a runner refreshes; the publish refuses an AST not valid for the commit. See ig-build-pipeline §”The AST cache lifecycle”. The Publisher still runs: validation, dependency resolution and terminology expansion are its job and are not reproducible from cached output.

e58b75c0412c.title: Processes that run this skill
e58b75c0412c.content: | process | step(s) that name it | . | An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch | Build and publish the site from the AST | . | Each IG, composed into a host docs site and rendered with just-the-docs | Clone each IG at its recorded commit and stage it; Compose each staged IG into the host source | .

06d44c764004.title: ig-site-links
06d44c764004.content: Skill id: ig-site-links · Package: fhir-ig-base · Instance: fhir-harness . An IG’s pages are written for the IG Publisher’s output directory: a flat folder of the IG’s pages, every artefact page, its QA report, its download archives, and whatever its template copies. Our site renders the same pages inside just-the-docs and holds only some of that. Every link a page makes therefore resolves somewhere specific, or is said to resolve nowhere.

04c291c76103.title: Where each link goes
04c291c76103.content: | a link to | goes to | by | . | an artefact page (StructureDefinition-X.html) | artifact/… on our site | relinkArtifacts | . | …differing only in CASE (-hcert for -HCert) | the one page it can mean; two candidates leave it alone | relinkArtifacts | . | a Publisher download (package.tgz, *.zip) | the IG’s published site (sushi canonical) | relinkPublisherOutputs | . | a Publisher-only page (qa.html, toc.html, …) | the published site | relinkOffSite, PUBLISHER_PAGES | . | a FILE of the IG’s repository (.github/…, bpmn/x.bpmn from input/bpmn/) | that file on GitHub, at the edit branch | relinkOffSite | . | openapi/index.html (Swagger’s deep links too) | the OpenAPI graph’s own index, which forwards #/<tag>/<operationId> — on an IG repository’s own site too, where publish-served puts the graph at openapi/ | gen-openapi-pages, publish-served | . | a .html page nothing serves | left as written and reported — DEAD in the IG's own source in the stage log | relinkOffSite | . The last row is deliberate. A page that is in no source anywhere is dead on the IG’s own published site too; pointing it there would trade our visible dead link for an invisible one. Report it to the IG instead.

fc0236ffa567.title: Liquid the Publisher accepts and Jekyll does not
fc0236ffa567.content: The Publisher’s Liquid (Java) reads "<a href=\"x.html\">X</a>" with escaped quotes; Ruby Liquid has no escapes and ends the string at the first \". rubyLiquidStrings writes such an {% assign %} single-quoted with plain quotes — the same string in both engines — and leaves one holding an apostrophe as written, since it has no faithful Ruby form. Without this, a page shows <a href=\ for every such link variable.

7f68dbce32af.title: The gate: a generator never links what it does not write
7f68dbce32af.content: gen-ig-pages refuses (exit 1) when a page it generates links, within its own directory, a page that run does not write. The rule for any generator here: write a link and the page it points to under ONE condition, and check it. A link and its page decided by two conditions (for example a view written only when the index is served) dangle whenever the conditions disagree.

dc32e8a1768c.title: Verify on the built site, not on the source
dc32e8a1768c.content: These are found by link-checking the BUILT pages, not by reading the generator: a full site build, and a check over every relative link in the IG sections. The stage log’s DEAD line is the start, not the whole — it cannot see what a later step (the mount pass) serves.

b1c8241db077.title: An IG’s diagrams get the platform’s figure viewer
b1c8241db077.content: An IG page embeds a diagram in three ways: inline ({% include x.svg %}), as <object data="x.svg">, or as an <img>, often a .drawio.png. All three get the same pan, zoom, full-width and export viewer as the platform’s BPMN figures. Every IG page carries the data-fa-figure-images stamp (IG_FIGURE_IMAGES_STAMP in build-ig-site.ts, written by the standalone layout and by the composed pages’ top include), so a raster drawing that the column has shrunk also gets the viewer. Which embed is taken, the opt-in, and the keyboard controls are covered in graph-rendering rule 9. Do not give IG pages a viewer of their own.

9e511290ff9e.title: The chrome’s links are not the IG’s, and are scoped to the IG’s site
9e511290ff9e.content: The harness rail, the tiles, the navbar icon row and the folders around an IG page are the PLATFORM’s chrome, so none of the rows above covers them. On an IG repository’s own site they come from the platform’s _data/harness.json, which compose-docs --shell --instance <ig> scopes to that IG: its own paths resolve under its baseurl, the platform’s graphs link to the platform’s site, and no other instance’s state graph or count is shown: a tile counts the IG repository’s own graphs, not the platform’s. The rule, and why an undeclared graph shows no number rather than zero, is in harness-tiles §”On a folio’s own site, a tile describes the FOLIO”.

c0518fda6c9a.title: ig-site-theme
c0518fda6c9a.content: Skill id: ig-site-theme · Package: fhir-ig-base · Instance: fhir-harness . An IG staged as its own just-the-docs site (/<instance>/ig/) wears the palette of the one webpage theme its instance declares, or inherits along its needs. Nothing new is authored for the IG: the theme already exists as data, and this is how it reaches the site.

e42495d0dace.title: The path, end to end
e42495d0dace.content: . | Declared — the instance’s themes/themes.ts exports INSTANCE_THEMES, one of which has kind: "webpage" and a palette of four roles (surface, ink, edge, accent). Declaring a theme is theme-declaration’s subject, not this skill’s. | Resolved — stage-ig-sites.ts webpagePalette(repoRoot, instance) reads it through instanceThemes (cat-harness/schemas/theme-by-ref.ts), keyed on the instance’s declared name. An instance that declares no webpage theme inherits the nearest one along its needs chain, breadth-first, and the stage log says which instance it came from. | Rendered — build-ig-site.ts colourScheme(palette) writes _sass/color_schemes/ig.scss and sets color_scheme: ig. just-the-docs’ own colour-scheme mechanism does the rest, so the IG keeps the theme’s machinery unchanged and only its colours move. The sidebar takes accent; its text colour is chosen by contrast, and a pairing under WCAG AA is reported (CONTRAST: in the stage log), never hidden. | .

39b1810b962f.title: What is refused, and what is said
39b1810b962f.content: | case | outcome | . | no webpage theme, own or along needs | built on just-the-docs’ default light scheme, and the stage log says colour scheme: NONE, with each instance’s reason (declares themes, none of kind webpage) | . | two or more webpage themes in one instance, or at the same distance along needs | refused — nothing says which one dresses the IG | . | a palette pairing below AA | built, and reported under CONTRAST: | .

866687e10a1a.title: Three theme paths — do not conflate them
866687e10a1a.content: | path | surface | data | code | . | IG site palette (this skill) | the standalone IG site, /<instance>/ig/ | the webpage theme’s palette | stage-ig-sites.ts → build-ig-site.ts colourScheme | . | docs-page theme | the instance’s composed docs pages, /<instance>/… | the same theme, as CSS variables | gen-themes-css.ts → _data/instance-themes.json → head_custom.html | . | IG chrome | “fixture” pages that mirror the Publisher’s template | the template chain’s tokens and rules (chrome.json) | schemas/ig-chrome.ts, ingest-ig-chrome.ts | . The first two read one declaration, so an IG’s site and its docs pages cannot disagree on colour. The chrome is a different model — the Publisher template’s own CSS, ingested with its conflicts — and is not a palette.

cbba39d30f68.title: Verify on the built CSS, not on a log line
cbba39d30f68.content: A staged site’s theme is checked by finding the palette’s hex values (here an accent of <hex>) in the built stylesheet: . git show <gh-pages>:branches/<slug>/<ig>/ig/assets/css/just-the-docs-default.css \ | grep -c '<hex>' . Calling stageIgSite directly with no palette option prints colour scheme: NONE — true for that call, not for the instance. Do not read it as a missing theme. Stage through stage-ig-sites.ts (or pass webpagePalette(...).palette), and judge the result by the built CSS.

3a92e516762b.title: Do not
3a92e516762b.content: . | Author a second palette for the IG. One declaration, read by both paths above; a copy would be a second answer free to drift. | Touch the theme’s machinery. just-the-docs’ layout, nav and components stay as they are; only the colour scheme is the instance’s. | Put a logo on it. Colour carries identity; the wordmark is set in type. | .

79877f85406d.title: Incremental render — the cache is easy, the cascade is the work
79877f85406d.content: Three steps. Only the third is hard, and it is the one that fails quietly: . | Seed — start from a previous render rather than from nothing. | Re-render what changed — the steps whose inputs moved. | Re-render what DEPENDS on them. | . A page that was not re-rendered looks exactly like a page that was, so an incremental render that gets the dependency graph wrong ships wrong pages and reports a clean build.

c56b0e1ba2d3.title: The two edges, one mechanism
c56b0e1ba2d3.content: | edge | example | one change means | . | projection | <page>.html ← <source>.md | one source file → one page | . | index | community-list.html ← every catalogue node | one member → the whole index | . The index edge is the one people forget: an index is derived from a SET, so it goes stale when a member changes even though the index file itself did not. The runner treats both alike: if any declared input changed, the step re-runs, and the step’s own --check decides which outputs actually differ. The downstream half uses needs, which already orders the pipeline: a step whose dependency re-ran re-runs too.

61a6e72add99.title: A step declares GRAPH TYPOLOGIES, not paths
61a6e72add99.content: RenderStep carries two ways to say what it reads, and the second is the one to use: . | field | what it names | when | . | inputs | repository-relative files or directories | a path that is not a declared graph — a config file, a script’s own fixtures | . | inputGraphs | graph kinds from <name>.json — cat-harness, beans, schemas, … | anything the declaration already locates | . check:declared-paths rejects a literal path to a declared graph. A second answer to where do the skills live goes stale the moment a directory moves, and the render then hashes a path that is not there, finds nothing, and reports the step unchanged. The subprocess, and why there is one . render-pipeline.ts is in the harness layer. Resolving a graph typology means readDeclaration, which validates every kind in the declaration — and this repository declares a folio directory whose kind is registered by core, on the argument (written on schemas/kg/folio-graph-typology.ts) that a layer which cannot render must not own the renderable kind. So the harness layer cannot resolve any kind in-process without importing core, which check:partition rejects. So it asks across the boundary the way the pipeline asks every renderer it runs — by spawning one. cat-harness-tools/scripts/declared-dirs.ts is core-layer and prints one line of JSON on stdout, {graph: [dirs]}. A failure prints nothing to stdout and exits non-zero, so the caller cannot read could not resolve as declares nothing — the distinction this whole skill turns on. The pipeline reports it: . Graph typologies could not be resolved here, so every step that declared only graphs re-rendered: <reason> . and every graph-declared step becomes undeclared, which always re-renders. Safe direction, said out loud: a silent fall-back to a full render leaves the cache inert with nothing in the output saying why. The cost: a graph is coarser than a file list . kg-current declares the whole cat-harness graph, and everything needs its way back to kg-current, so editing one skill re-renders every step. That is the right trade: over-declaring costs needless runs, under-declaring ships stale pages that look fresh. A finer declaration is available whenever a step’s reads can be expressed without spelling a declared path.

5474605290bd.title: Hash content, never mtime
5474605290bd.content: mtime is the obvious shortcut and it is wrong twice: a fresh checkout rewrites every mtime, so CI would re-render everything; and a file touched but unchanged re-renders for nothing. Hash the content, and hash the path alongside it — moving a file is a change, and an index keyed on filenames notices. Sort before hashing, by codepoint. readdirSync order is not stable across machines, and localeCompare is ICU-dependent — a seed written on one machine would mismatch on another. byCodepoint in render-selection.ts is the comparator.

4aa0070ff987.title: Could-not-determine always re-renders
4aa0070ff987.content: Four states send a step to the “run it” pile, and none of them is an error: . | state | why it runs | . | inputs changed | the obvious one | . | something it needs re-ran | the cascade | . | the seed’s manifest does not mention it | absent is not fresh — it may never have run | . | it declares no inputs | it has not said what it reads, so nothing can be concluded | . And three at the build level: no manifest at all is a full render; a manifest that is unparseable or carries the wrong schema tag is treated as absent; and graph typologies that could not be resolved turn every graph-declared step into the fourth row above. A corrupt manifest is never partially believed — half a cache is worse than none, because the half that is wrong is invisible. This is the repository’s standing rule applied to rendering: could-not-check is never green. Here it costs a re-render, which is the cheap direction.

ccc90ca28f61.title: Under-declaring is the dangerous direction
ccc90ca28f61.content: A step whose real input is not listed keeps a stale output and looks exactly like one that re-rendered. A step that over-declares costs one needless run. So when unsure, list it. bun run cat render:order names every step that declares no inputs, because those are the ceiling on how incremental a build can be — and a step that always re-renders should be a decision (alwaysRun, with a reason) rather than an omission nobody noticed.

119ea69cd9ba.title: Steps that always run
119ea69cd9ba.content: A narrower graph buys more caching: beans reaches only docs-pages and state-dashboards. The two that always run are bootstrap (pending — nothing to cache yet) and kg-dynamic (alwaysRun: it exports the running workflows’ state, whose stuck states are measured against the clock, so no source hash could make caching it correct). Report the cached steps as cached, never as a pass. In this pipeline a “skip” already means its input never rendered, so a served-from-seed step gets its own mark (=). The counts must add up: a cached step returns no error, so it must not also be counted as having run. A build report that sums to more than its own steps is one nobody trusts the rest of.

5ea2bfe1f496.title: Usage
5ea2bfe1f496.content: bun run cat render # full bun run cat render:order # order + which steps are cacheable bun run cat render --write-manifest <path> # full, and record the inputs bun run cat render --seed <path> # incremental against that record bun run cat render --seed <old> --write-manifest <new> .

feb12b28a6be.title: Not built
feb12b28a6be.content: Seeding from the published render. The manifest and the selection are here; copying a previous build’s OUTPUT into place before the run is a deployment step and belongs with feature-staging.yml. Until it exists, a seeded run skips steps whose inputs are unchanged but has nothing to serve — so use --seed only where the previous output is already in place.

5c3805c720e8.title: index.config.json: what this checkout instantiates
5c3805c720e8.content: The schema is folio-index-config/v1 in cat-harness/schemas/kg/index-config.ts. The index is the ONE config. Each instance’s config is written inline in its instances[] entry. A <name>.config.json is a legacy file: imported only as a migration step, then retired with index-config:migrate --inline --write. Never create one — not to make a tool find a recipe, not for a new instance. If a reader only finds config in the file, that reader is the bug; fix it to read the index entry first. index.config.json holds three facts about how a checkout is instantiated: which harnesses are instantiated, which one is / (a checkout has one <base>/index.html), and where each one comes from, so each is stated once rather than spread across every root config. When it exists at the root it is authoritative. When it is absent, readers fall back to the root *.config.json files, their site.landing flags, and remoteMounts on the root declaration. { "$schema": "folio-index-config/v1", "instances": [ { "name": "folio-assistant", "source": { "local": { "at": "." } } }, { "name": "cat-harness" }, { "name": "my-ig", "source": { "remote": { "repository": "owner/my-ig", "ref": "<40-char sha>", "overrides": { "my-ig": { "whole": true } }, "trust": { "consent": { "...": "..." } } } } }, { "name": "my-guide", "contentType": "document", "site": { "build": { "sourceSteps": ["site:document"] } } } ], "site": { "landing": "cat-harness" } } .

4daea946529f.title: Instantiated is a different fact from declared
4daea946529f.content: A declaration (<name>.json) says what an instance declares. It travels with the harness into every checkout that uses the harness. An index.config.json entry says the instance is instantiated in this checkout. Without an index, a <name>.config.json at the root says the same thing. Tiles, the landing and the hub listing are all drawn from the instantiated set, which instantiatedHarnessNames(root) returns. Never derive that set from declarations or from a directory listing. The dependencies of an instantiated harness are not instantiated just because a mount’s closure brought them in. They keep a group of their own rather than disappearing. A harness that a KG subscription chose is instantiated the same way: kg:instantiate adds its entry, with its config inline, when the checkout has an index (and only without one writes a root <name>.config.json).

7449e008f71f.title: Inline, over a legacy import while one remains
7449e008f71f.content: Each entry’s effective config is built like this: . | Start from a legacy imported file, while one remains. That is import when it is given, else <name>.config.json, and only if the file exists. The target state is that no such file exists. | Overlay every other key of the entry (everything except name, import, source and _comment) as an inline HarnessConfig field. Objects merge key by key, and arrays and scalars are replaced. Inline fields win. | . effectiveInstanceConfig(root, name) computes it. readHarnessConfig(dir) returns it for any instance that an index lists, walking outward from the instance root and stopping at the first directory that holds either the index or the instance’s own config. An instance the index does not list is read from its own config file. Readers that are handed a root and a name (the site recipe in build-instance-site.ts) use readInstanceConfig in cat-harness-tools/scripts/instance-config.ts, which reads the same way and REPORTS every legacy file it reads. Retiring the files is index-config:migrate --inline --write: each imported file is folded into its entry by exactly the overlay above, so no effective config changes, and the file is deleted. index-config:inline:check fails while one remains.

472af5419bf4.title: Local or remote
472af5419bf4.content: . | source absent: local, at <name>/. | source.local.at: local, at that path. Use . for the instance declared at the root. | source.remote: a remote mount. It is a remoteMounts entry minus harness, which is the entry’s name. It reuses RemoteMountSchema instead of restating it, so it has ref (not pin), overrides.<name>.whole and .path, note, trust.consent and track, and every field added to RemoteMountSchema arrives with no edit here. | . There is one read path and one write path for remote mounts: . | Read: readDeclaredMounts(instanceRoot) returns the index’s remote entries when an index exists, else the declaration’s remoteMounts. If both carry mounts it throws and names both files. It never picks one. | Write: writeDeclaredMounts(instanceRoot, mounts) always writes index.config.json, seeding the index from the checkout first if there is none. It refuses while the declaration still carries remoteMounts. Nothing writes remoteMounts on a declaration. | .

4c258e350dab.title: Which harness / is
4c258e350dab.content: resolveLandingInstance(root) is the only reader. It applies these rules in order: . | condition | / is | . | the index is unreadable | invalid: the gate fails. There is no fallback to the flags, because the index was written to override them | . | the index’s site.landing names an instance it lists | that instance (by: "index") | . | the index’s site.landing is "hub" | the neutral hub: the harness listing and the todo panel | . | the index’s site.landing names an instance it does not list | invalid: the gate fails, and it is never a silent fallback | . | no site.landing (or no index), one instance | that instance (sole) | . | no site.landing, several instances, exactly one config flags site.landing: true | the flagged one | . | several flagged | the hub | . | none flagged | ambiguous: check:landing-instance fails, because the answer is never guessed | . | nothing instantiated | none: a state of its own, not a default | . gen-landing-data.ts and sync-docs-harness.ts ask this resolver. They do not use their own location. check:landing-instance also checks that the index and the root *.config.json files agree: . | A root config that the index does not import fails the check: without the index it would instantiate a harness, with it it does not, and nothing picks between them silently. | An import that names a missing file also fails the check. | An entry with no config file at all is the target state, and passes. | A legacy file an entry still imports is reported every time. It passes while it is a pending migration (every key it holds is either not inline or inline with the same value). It fails when the entry overrides one of its keys with a different value: the file’s value is then dead text that a reader of the file alone takes for the config. | .

f9f95a9643ea.title: A harnessed repository runs its checks on its own pull requests
f9f95a9643ea.content: Instantiating a harness in a repository includes turning its checks on there, through one reusable workflow the harness owns, never a copy per repository, so a layer is judged on its own pull requests and not only when an index re-pins it. Switching off a repository’s builds must not switch off its gates. The workflow is the tools layer’s .github/workflows/layer-pr-checks.yml. A repository calls it from a workflow of about fifteen lines that runs on pull_request: . jobs: checks: uses: <owner>/<tools-layer>/.github/workflows/layer-pr-checks.yml@main with: mode: layer # or `index`: the repository is its own index instance: <instance> # layer mode: its directory in the folio-assistant index path-in-repo: <instance> # where the instance sits in the repository ('.' at the root) . | layer mode is for a repository that an index mounts, such as cat-harness or the DAK layer. The workflow checks out folio-assistant and puts the PR in place of the locked mount. | index mode is for a repository that is its own index: an IG repository over the DAK layer, smart-ra, or a folio. Its own index.lock.json is replayed. | The gates are the harness’s graph checks over the repository’s own instance, plus every check:* / *:check script of that instance and its whole dependency harness (its transitive needs). Each is named <owning-instance>:<script>. | A PR fails only on what it newly breaks. Each gate and test runs on main and on the PR. Anything already red on main is listed, never hidden, and never counted against the PR. | . A layer PR that declares a new directory is red on two index gates it cannot clear. The index README lists every declared directory, so the PR leaves index:render:check and readme:sync:root:check stale, and only the index re-pin that takes the PR regenerates the README. Read those two as expected when they are the only new failures, and run them green in the index re-pin instead. Disabling a repository’s automatic builds is not disabling its checks. When an IG repository’s automatic gh-pages or IG Publisher triggers are switched off (the onboarding question in the FHIR IG layer’s ig-build-pipeline), the harness caller stays on.

15c085779cf3.title: The exemptions of the index’s own workflows
15c085779cf3.content: .github/workflows/ belongs to the index, so the steps CI runs there that the local gate set does not are exempted HERE, under gateExemptions.steps, each with a kind and a reason (GateExemptionsSchema, the same shape an instance declaration carries). They land in the same change as the workflow step, never ahead of it in a layer: an exemption for a step CI does not yet run matches nothing, and gates-workflows.test.ts refuses a stale exemption as it refuses an unclassified step. "gateExemptions": { "steps": [ { "match": "bun run cat state:push -- --id health", "kind": "ci-only", "reason": "…" } ] } . An instance still exempts its OWN scripts and steps in its own declaration.

23f05cfc130f.title: index.lock.json, and the legacy name
23f05cfc130f.content: The lock records what the declared mounts resolved to. It is generated by mount:remote and kept as a separate file. The legacy name is <root-instance>.mount-lock.json. The rules for each reader and writer: . | Writers write index.lock.json. mount:remote first renames a legacy lock onto the new name, so the old file is moved, never dropped. | Readers take index.lock.json first, then fall back to the legacy *.mount-lock.json, so downstream folios and old branches still replay. The readers are: . | mount-from-lock.ts | mountedInstanceRoots | mountedUnder in git-corpus.ts | mount:remote:check | . | Both files present is an error that names both. Two locks are never merged. | . mount-from-lock.ts imports only node:*, so it restates the rule inline and its test holds it to lockFilesIn.

428af76a8adc.title: The reserved index stem
428af76a8adc.content: index.config.json ends in .config.json, so a scan that treats “each root *.config.json is a harness” would find a harness called index. The index stem is therefore reserved across the board: . | rootConfigStems skips every index.* file. It is the one root scan; every other reader calls it or instantiatedHarnessNames. | findDeclarationFile skips every index.* file too. | The index schema refuses an instance named index, and hub, because that is the landing keyword. | . Do not add another copy of the scan: a new copy is how the reserved name leaks back in.

d14ae97fb945.title: The generated .gitignore block
d14ae97fb945.content: # BEGIN index mounts (generated from index.config.json — do not edit) /my-ig/ # END index mounts . The block holds one /<path>/ line per remote instance in the index, where the path is overrides.<name>.path, else <name>/. After those it lists every further instance root the lock records, because a mount’s closure can land instances that the index never names. Three things write the block: . | mount:remote | writeDeclaredMounts | index-config:migrate --write | . check:index-ignores fails when the block is missing or disagrees with the index. When an index exists, mount:remote does not append to .git/info/exclude: a local exclude rule is invisible to every other clone, so a path the committed block does not cover is reported as not ignored. Without an index, it still appends there.

1fff60799d02.title: Converting a checkout: index-config:migrate
1fff60799d02.content: bun run cat index-config:migrate # print the index it would write, and its findings bun run cat index-config:migrate --write # write it; move remoteMounts; write the block; rename the lock bun run cat index-config:migrate --check # exit 1 when --write would change anything (a gate here) bun run cat index-config:migrate --inline --write # also fold each <name>.config.json into its entry, and delete it bun run cat index-config:inline:check # exit 1 while any imported <name>.config.json remains bun run cat index-config:migrate --root <clone> # a separated repository's standalone checkout . The converter reads only the files under --root, so it runs on a standalone clone of any separated repository. | Which root configs it imports: a root <name>.config.json is imported only when name is an instance the checkout declares (at the root or one level down) or mounts. Anything else becomes an unmatched-config finding and is not imported. A repository cut from a fork, for example, can carry the fork’s own <fork>.config.json; importing it would instantiate a harness the repository does not hold. | Re-runs: it is idempotent. A re-run moves only the remoteMounts entries that the declaration has gained since the last run. An entry the index already holds identically is dropped from the declaration. An entry the index holds differently throws, and you reconcile it by hand. | .

d7505c5e09d3.title: The upload step
d7505c5e09d3.content: The first step of document ingestion — what puts a file into the queue everything downstream assumes it is already in — and the Tools that perform it. Generated from the Tool documentation and from the process diagram. Nothing here is authored on this page: edit the Tool node or the .bpmn and re-run bun run cat-harness-tools/scripts/gen-upload-step-docs.ts.

1e1533bd81ae.title: Where this step sits
1e1533bd81ae.content: |   |   | . | process | Basic ingestion — an upload to an asset catalogued in library/ (Process_Ingestion) | . | begins at | A contributor has a file for the folio | . | first step | Place it in uploads/ by a declared route (Task_Place) | . | performed in the lane | Contributor (human or agent) (role user) | . | governed by the skill | upload-routes | . | Tools that satisfy it | 2 | . What the diagram says about the step itself: . THE FIRST LINK: everything downstream of here takes a file that is already in the queue, so without this step how the file got there is governed by nothing. WHAT THIS STEP IS. The basic flow’s ACCEPT step: choosing an arrival route, writing the bytes into the declared queue of the instance that will own them, and discharging what that route does not discharge for you. The routes, what each writer owes, and the two that are mechanisms against the one that is a persona are in the upload-routes skill; upload-url composes the forge URL for the web route from the declaration rather than from a literal, because a hand-written one can 404. WHY A PLAIN bpmn:task AND NOT A userTask. A userTask asserts a human performs it, and this lane is “Contributor (human or agent)” because both do; asserting human-only would be an activity-fulfilment-kind contradiction. A plain task asserts nothing about the performer. WHY THE BEAN OP IS note AND NOT claim. Placing a file claims nothing; it adds to a queue. What it owes the work plan is visibility. A note against the ingestion bean is what makes the queue’s growth something another session can see. The skill is the prose an actor reads; each Tool below is one concrete way to exercise it. See upload-routes.

fdbf2878cb6c.title: Directory READMEs from the Knowledge Graph
fdbf2878cb6c.content: subgraph-readmes · satisfies docs-generation, upload-routes . Write a README for every directory an instance declares, from the declaration and the files themselves: the declared title and description, the Graph Typologies, and one row per file described from the file, with ‘used by’ only where a diagram records it. Renders the Liquid templates in tools/templates/readme/, part of the tools graph, which may include one another with Jekyll-style include tags. Writes only between <!-- kg:subgraph:begin --> and :end; a README without the markers is left alone and reported. Records every missing title, missing or over-long description, absent directory and unmarked README in test/results/subgraph-readmes.qa-results.json. |   |   | . | install | nothing to install | . | invoke | bun run cat readme:subgraphs | . | requires | runtime bun · no network | . Inputs . | name | required | how it is passed | what it is | . | check | no | --check | Fail if any directory README or the QA record is stale; write nothing. | . Outputs . | name | what it is | . | readmes | <directory>/README.md for each declared directory, and the QA record. | . Choosing it . This Tool declares no selection, so when to reach for it, what it will not do and what it costs are undocumented. That is a gap in the Tool node, not on this page.

54249bc1c6a8.title: Where to drop a file — the queue’s upload URL
54249bc1c6a8.content: upload-url · satisfies upload-routes, content-acquisition . Compose the forge URL a person can drop a file at, from the instance’s own declaration: the uploads graph’s directory, resolved against the ROOT its scope names, expressed relative to the repository, and appended to the origin remote as GitHub’s /upload/<branch>/<path>. Every failure is NAMED and no URL is guessed — no declaration, no declared uploads graph, a declared queue absent from disk, no origin remote, and a non-github.com remote each return a reason and a remedy instead. The declared path is relative to the INSTANCE and a forge URL needs it relative to the REPOSITORY, so pasting the declared path can mint a 404. |   |   | . | install | nothing to install | . | invoke | bun run cat upload:url | . | requires | runtime bun · no network | . Inputs . | name | required | how it is passed | what it is | . | branch | no | positional 0 | The branch the upload form targets. Defaults to main; pass the working branch to send somebody to a pull request’s head instead, so the upload lands on a commit CI judges. | . Outputs . | name | what it is | . | url | The upload URL on stdout, exit 0 — or, on stderr and exit 1, the reason it could not be composed and the remedy for that reason. Never a guessed URL: a URL is believed, and somebody sent to a wrong one cannot tell it from an empty directory. | . Choosing it . When. You are about to tell somebody where to put a file, in any channel. Reach for it every time, not only when unsure: a hand-written path breaks silently when a directory moves. It also answers “which queue” when a checkout declares more than one (one per instance): the answer is whichever instance root you pass, never a literal. Limits. It answers WHERE, and nothing else. It does not upload, does not check whether the person has write access, and cannot tell you which of several declared queues should own a given file — that is undecided and upload-routes says so rather than picking. The /upload/<branch>/<path> form is GitHub’s, so another forge gets a named refusal rather than a guess. And the URL it hands back opens the route with the FEWEST guarantees: the web form has no working tree, so no pre-commit hook and no generator run happen on it, and everything upload-routes lists has to be discharged afterwards from a checkout. Cost. One read of the declaration and one of the git remote; no network at run time and nothing installed.

1091f8adffaf.title: indicator-extraction
1091f8adffaf.content: Skill id: indicator-extraction · Package: authoring-who-smart-guidelines · Follows dak-l1-library, which ingests the source. Sibling of recommendation-extraction: that one takes a source’s recommendations, this one its indicators. It is a step of L1 → L2 extraction for a DAK or DTH, bound to Task_Indicators in l2-dak-authoring and Call_Data in dth-authoring.

f9bbf786dc3c.title: Two layers, kept apart
f9bbf786dc3c.content: | layer | what | kind / model | written by | . | L1 | the indicator as the source prints it, verbatim | indicator block (folio type smart-base:Indicator; KG L1 indicator, kg/src/l1.ts) | scripts/l1-indicator-sheets.py → candidates.json → gen-library-jsonld | . | L2 | the DAK’s or DTH’s own operational measure, a draft that points back | program-indicator (sgkg-l2), logical model ProgramIndicator | scripts/l2-program-indicators.py | . sgkg-l2 keeps them apart: merging them would merge a WHO definition with a country’s implementation of it. The L2 record is a draft with derivedFrom its L1 node, and the L2 author adopts, edits or drops it.

702faa51837e.title: Rules
702faa51837e.content: . | Ids come from the source. number / indicatorId is the printed indicator number (“1-01”, “4-01.3”). A sheet whose header prints none is reported and skipped, never numbered by an agent. The L2 id is <prefix>.<number> (“NHWA.1-01”); the prefix only namespaces it. | Verbatim. Every field is the printed text: lines joined, letter-spacing artefacts closed up, nothing reworded. A printed list (glossary terms, data sources) is one string joined with “; “. | Every printed field, not only name, numerator and denominator. The L1 node’s meta holds indicatorId, module, abbreviatedName, name, numerator, denominator, disaggregation, definition, glossary, reportingFrequency, reportingFrameworks, dataSources, furtherInformation and dimension where printed; a sub-indicator adds parentIndicator and guidingQuestions. These are the keys the structured-block cards read. | No gap is filled. ProgramIndicator makes definition, numerator, denominator and disaggregation 1..1. Where the source prints none (a composite or self-assessed indicator), the L2 draft lists it in gaps and the L2 author decides. Nothing is copied from another source to fill it. | A composite indicator keeps its sub-indicators as their own L1 nodes; in L2 they are the parent’s components, not program indicators of their own. | Read the page layout, not the section text, when the source prints sheets as a label column and a value column: Stage A’s text reads side bars and columns out of order. | .

f2ace8b3618a.title: Steps
f2ace8b3618a.content: . | The source is in the library (dak-l1-library), with its PDF in uploads/<doc-id>/. | L1 candidates. From the library repository root: . python3 smart-base/scripts/l1-indicator-sheets.py --entry library/<doc-id> \ --pdf uploads/<doc-id>/<doc-id>.pdf --pages <first>-<last> --json # look first python3 smart-base/scripts/l1-indicator-sheets.py --entry library/<doc-id> \ --pdf uploads/<doc-id>/<doc-id>.pdf --pages <first>-<last> --write . --write merges into candidates.json as the indicators aspect, replacing an indicator candidate with the same number (re-runs are idempotent). Check the count against the source’s own list of indicators (NHWA: the synthesis table, 29 indicators). | L1 nodes. bun cat-harness-tools/pipeline/gen-library-jsonld.ts --entry library/<doc-id> writes blocks/indicator-<section>-NN.{jsonld,md}, each derivedFrom its section, provenance: ingested, with the fields in meta. Existing indicator IRIs do not change when the first candidate of a section stays the same indicator. | L2 drafts. python3 smart-base/scripts/l2-program-indicators.py --entry library/<doc-id> \ --prefix <PREFIX> --out <where the L2 author will review them> . | Into the DAK or DTH. The L2 author takes the drafts into the guide’s indicators component (DAK component 8; a DTH’s data elements, indicators and requirements), through the guide’s own review (l2-component-edit-review) and, for a DTH, a change set. | .
