865131612350.title: Review-log watch
865131612350.content: A review log is a drafting or public-comment sheet (skill review-sheet-script) for one folio repository. The steps below are for a drafting log; a public-comment log differs as set out in “Public-comment logs”. A watcher is the agent thread that keeps it moving. This skill is what the watcher does on each wake. Process: processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn (checklist beside it).

d492c9e018db.title: Why mechanical
d492c9e018db.content: The watcher runs a core tool on every poll, and each issue gets a row on Contributor Feedback, including existing issues; a closed issue’s row is hidden, its text struck through. The poll wakes the watcher thread every 3 minutes. Until the tool says changed, the watcher only reads and runs the tool. It does not reason about the rows, edit anything or post anything.

44855a31cde4.title: Each wake
44855a31cde4.content: . | Read two small ranges: . | Watch!F1:I1, where the sheet script writes Cells hash, the hash itself, and the time it last checked. The script rewrites it on every refresh and every timer tick, from the cells people set. | Contributor Feedback’s header row with its Change-set and Issue columns (A to K), so the tool can give a new row the next Change-set id. | . Save the values as JSON, with the header row and with an empty first row for each sheet row above it, so the row numbers stay the sheet’s. A sheet whose script has no Watch tab yet is read whole, from row 1, and gets no --sheet-hash. | Check: . bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch/watch.ts \ --repo litlfred/dth-phc --sheet values.json \ --state ~/.cache/review-log-watch/<sheet-id>.json \ --sheet-hash <Watch!G1> . | Exit 0 is {"status":"unchanged"}. Queue the next wake and stop. | Exit 10 is changed. The output has changes (an issue opened, updated or closed, or a cell’s old and new text) and append. | . Inserted rows. People may insert a row anywhere. The state keys each cell by its row’s Change-set id (CS-004:Ready for agent), and by sheet row only for a row with no id, so an insert moves no change set and reports nothing. A cell change carries cs and the row it is on now. Every row number in the output (changes[].row, closedRows) is from this read, so write only from the read you just checked, never from a row number kept from an earlier check. | Append each append[].row below the last row of Contributor Feedback. The row is already lined up with the header: . | Change-set: the next id, also in append[].agent.csId. | Title: the issue’s title. | First Contributor Feedback column: @login (#N): first paragraph. | Issue: the issue’s URL. | . The issue’s Markdown is turned into plain cell text: a [label](url) shows its label, and bold, italic and code marks are dropped. Its links are in append[].links (the column and each link’s start, end and URL). Write the cell with those as textFormatRuns (updateCells), so each link is clickable. Then write append[].agent to the Agent tab as a new row: its Change-set and Issue columns. The script fills Contributor Feedback’s Issue column from the Agent tab, by Change-set, on every refresh, so an Issue written only on Contributor Feedback is cleared on the next refresh. Every other cell stays empty. This tool is the only thing that adds issue rows, so nobody adds them by hand. A row with closed: true is appended like the others and then treated as in step 4. | Closed issues. Hide each row in closedRows, plus the rows just appended for closed issues, and strike its text through. Hiding and striking are formatting only, so the row’s text and history stay. A reopened issue’s row is shown again, without the strike-through, by hand. | Agent pass. Run Contributor feedback on each changed row, and record the step on the Agent tab at once. A Ready for agent = Yes gets its edit, and a Ready for merge = Yes gets its merge. A Blue answer to a Decision needed question is taken up. Feedback on every Blue change and every new row. In every log the watcher keeps, the agent writes or rewrites Feedback (agent), in the layout of review-sheet-script (“The agent’s feedback cell has a fixed layout”), for each row that: . | is new, however it got there: from a GitHub issue (step 3), typed by a person, or copied from a TWG workbook; | has an empty Feedback (agent) cell; or | has Blue cells (Title, Selected Sections, any Contributor Feedback column, Disposition) that no longer match the Agent tab’s Feedback basis (feedbackBasis()), which is when the script shows “⚠ Stale”. It does this in the same wake, before accepting the state. A row it cannot finish keeps its stale mark and comes back on the next wake. The digest covers every row, not only issue rows, so a row with no issue still wakes the watcher. | . | Accept. Run the check again with the same inputs plus --accept, so the state file records what was handled. A row the pass could not finish still differs from the stored state, so it comes back on the next wake. | Queue the next wake. | .

2059933e9439.title: Public-comment logs
2059933e9439.content: A log whose Config has MODE public-comment has Review Public Comments, Review Change Sets, Agent - Comments and Agent - Change Sets instead of Contributor Feedback and Agent. The watcher runs the same check, with these differences: . | Hash. Watch!G1 covers the cells people set on both people’s tabs: on Review Change Sets Title, TWG (CS), every Committee Feedback column, Ready for agent, Dispositions confirmed, Ready for merge and Change Set (human); on Review Public Comments every Committee Feedback column, Disposition, Change Set (human) and TWG (human). Lines are keyed by Change-set id and comment No., so an inserted row changes nothing. The script writes it on every refresh, and the timer refreshes only after an edit or an Agent tab change, so Checked (UTC) can be old on a quiet sheet. | Read. Review Change Sets’ header row and Change-set column, as --sheet. It has no Issue column, so the tool tracks only issues labelled change-set (--label overrides) and appends no rows: each open one comes back as an issue-unlinked change. Handle those as in “Change sets people make” below. | Without a Watch tab, read Review Change Sets whole. The tool then compares its cells itself; Review Public Comments’ cells are seen only through the hash. | Steps 3 and 4 (append, hide closed rows) do not apply. The agent pass of step 5 is the change-set work of Public comment. | .

a3fa2a050ddd.title: Lint each poll
a3fa2a050ddd.content: After the change check, run bun tools/review-log-watch/lint.ts --feedback <Contributor Feedback values.json> --agent <Agent values.json>. It reads each Agent row’s pull requests from GitHub and prints, per change set, what breaks the feedback layout in review-sheet-script (“The agent’s feedback cell has a fixed layout”): . | Needs human with no Decision needed: question, or a question without Needs human; | the question not first, fewer than two lettered options, no single (recommended), or no line saying where to answer; | history in the cell (Decided, Step n, Already done), Markdown **, more than 10 lines; | a PR that GitHub says is merged or closed while the Agent tab’s status still says open; | feedback on a row with no Selected Sections and no question asking which, or a PR that changes a chapter outside the Selected Sections without an Outside the selected sections: line. | . Exit 0 is clean. Exit 10 lists problems: the watcher fixes the Agent tab status or rewrites the cell to the layout in the same wake, and records the Agent step. The lint writes nothing itself.

5dbb71218357.title: Previews follow main
5dbb71218357.content: A preview is built from its pull request’s head, so once main moves on, a branch that lacks main’s head shows a document main no longer is. The watcher brings main into every open change-set branch. Modes. The log’s Config tab may hold a PREVIEW_REFRESH row: . | automatic (the default, also when there is no row): on every poll, whether or not a cell changed, check every open change-set PR. A move on main changes no cell, so the change check alone would never wake it. | on-feedback: only in the agent pass for a change set people acted on. | . People’s feedback triggers it in either mode: new or changed Blue feedback on the change set, Ready for agent set to Yes, or feedback that asks, such as “update the preview” or “rebase on main” (bun tools/review-log-watch/previews.ts request --text <feedback>). Each check: . | Run bun tools/review-log-watch/previews.ts --agent <Agent values.json> for every open change set, or --prs owner/repo#n,... for one. It prints merge-main, resolve-conflict or none for each PR. Exit 0 means current; exit 10 lists the work. | For merge-main: merge main into the branch (a merge commit, never a rebase or force-push), regenerate generated files with the repo’s own tooling, push, and record the push with the agent-record tool. The sheet then shows the preview as stale until the new build is live. | For resolve-conflict: resolve it when both sides are generated or mechanical. When a person must choose, ask in the change set’s feedback cell (a Decision needed: question) and leave the branch as it is. | This only brings main into the branch. Committee content is never merged into main by the watcher. Closed PRs and PRs from forks are skipped. | .

3fdf70848733.title: Change sets people make
3fdf70848733.content: People make change sets, the way they open issues; how one came about does not matter once people have adjudicated it. On a public-comment log the watcher finds four kinds of request on each poll, and answers each in the same wake: . | A row with only a Title on Review Change Sets. The sheet script gives it the next Change-set id. The watcher adds the matching row on Agent - Change Sets (same id and Title) and a change-set record, and proposes a direction in Change Set Feedback (agent), as for any change set. | A change-set issue (form templates/issue-forms/change-set.yml, label change-set). bun tools/review-log-watch/cs-requests.ts issue --body <file> reads its fields. For “New change set” the watcher adds the Agent - Change Sets row, and the script then adds the Review Change Sets row with that Title. Split, merge and move go as below. | Feedback that asks for it, e.g. “this CS needs to be split”. Run bun tools/review-log-watch/cs-requests.ts request --text <the person's feedback> on every changed feedback cell; only the person’s words, never the agent’s or the script’s lines. For a split, merge, move or new request, write a Decision needed: question naming the change sets and which comments go where, with lettered options and one recommended. Make them only once an Editor sets Ready for agent to Yes. | Change Set (human) on Review Public Comments: a person typed another change set’s id, several ids, or new. The script already counts the comment in its new change set; the watcher records the move on Agent - Comments (Change-sets) and on the change-set records, and for new makes a change set for the comment and proposes a Title. | . Triage each new comment. A comment with no change set yet gets the agent’s suggestion: run cs-requests.ts triage --input <json> with the comment’s sections and the open change sets (id, sections, TWGs, status). It ranks the open change sets that share its sections and always offers new. Write the first as the comment’s Change-sets on Agent - Comments and its committees as TWG (agent). These are suggestions: a person’s Change Set (human) or TWG (human) always wins, and the watcher never overwrites a Blue cell. Sheet comments. People without edit rights use Insert, then Comment. Neither the Sheets API nor the script reads those comments yet, so the watcher does not see them; ask the person to copy the request into a feedback cell, or open the change-set form.

221e125b24b3.title: What counts as a change
221e125b24b3.content: . | Issues: the repository’s issues, open and closed, with their state and updated_at. --author <login> keeps only the issues one person opened. | Pull requests are left out. | So are issues labelled no-sheet, which an Editor sets to keep an issue off the sheet. | . | Cells: with --sheet-hash, the script’s hash stands for them, and a change shows as one change on #hash; the watcher then reads the rows to see which changed. Without it, the tool compares the cells itself. Either way, only the cells people set count, under these headers: . | Title, Selected Sections, every Contributor Feedback column, Disposition and Change Set (human) (Blue); | Ready for agent, Ready for merge and Dispositions confirmed (Orange); | on a public-comment log also every Committee Feedback column, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human). | . The agent’s Green columns and the script’s Grey ones are not watched, so the watcher’s own writes never wake it. | First check (baseline: true): with no state file yet, every issue counts as new and every unlinked issue gets a row. This is how an existing sheet takes in its existing issues. The watcher appends the rows, hides the closed ones and accepts, but starts no agent pass, because a cell that is merely seen for the first time has not changed. | .

5cab2c51e5f8.title: Setting up a watcher
5cab2c51e5f8.content: A log is not set up until a watcher has both of these wakes: . | a chain of 3-minute delayed wakes (send_later), each of which queues the next; | an hourly scheduled task that restarts the chain if it breaks. | . Keep the state file outside the repository, one per sheet. Without it, a fresh container treats its first check as a first check: it reports every issue as opened, and appends rows only for issues that no row links yet.

063188737f37.title: Limits
063188737f37.content: . | The tool reads one tab and one repository, from the issues API (up to 100 issues a page, every page). It never writes the sheet or GitHub. | The summary is the issue’s first paragraph, cut to 300 characters. A link the cut runs through keeps its target on the part that is left. Committee members may rewrite the Title and their own column. | .

f86f0d028188.title: Processes that run this skill
f86f0d028188.content: This skill has its own process: Review-log watch. | process | step(s) that name it | . | Review-log watch | Read the Contributor Feedback tab; Run the review-log-watch check; Append rows for new issues; hide closed ones; Accept the new state | .

96ee6709408d.doc: Keep the review sheet's Agent columns current
96ee6709408d.title: Keep the review sheet’s Agent columns current
96ee6709408d.content: When an agent works on a change set of a sheet that has the Tool enabled, it updates the Agent columns as part of the process. The sheet’s views (Agentic status, Staging review and the ⏳ line on Review Public Comments and Review Change Sets, or on Contributor Feedback in a drafting sheet) are built from the Agent tabs, so a change set worked without writing them shows reviewers nothing, or something old as current. The tabs, their columns and who writes each are the public-comment skill’s (§”The live review sheet”) and, for a drafting sheet, review-sheet-script §”Drafting mode”. How the script reads them, and the tool that makes the cells, are review-sheet-script’s (“Stale staging previews”, “Checked by commit”, “Writing the Agent tab with the tool”, “Where the agent is”). This skill says when the agent writes and what.

b25b7c98408e.doc: Keep the review sheet's Agent columns current
b25b7c98408e.title: When it applies
b25b7c98408e.content: The folio has the Tool enabled: it carries the Tool’s config, review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json (a drafting sheet: review/drafting/sheet-sync.json), and the session can reach the sheet through a Google Sheets connector. The sheet’s id is not in the repository; it is given by the project (its scheduled sheet-sync task, or the owner). It applies to any work on a change set, however it started: a sheet sync, a card, a thread message, an issue or a review comment on the PR. If the Tool is enabled but the sheet cannot be reached, do the work, and say in the reply that the sheet was not updated and why.

d44309608adb.doc: Keep the review sheet's Agent columns current
d44309608adb.title: The tabs
d44309608adb.content: . | Agent - Comments (public comment only): one row per comment (No.), with Agentic status, Agentic action taken, Agentic applied in, Agentic handled by, Agentic date actioned and Change-sets. | Agent - Change Sets (a drafting sheet: Agent): one row per change set, with Pull request, Staging review page, What the PRs changed, Agent completed, Feedback basis, Staging built, PR head, Staging built from, Staging deploy and Agent step (each header ends “(change set)”). | . A public-comment sheet may instead have one Agent tab (comments left, change sets right, the Config’s AGENT_CS empty). Write it the same way, by header.

e848a1d2289b.doc: Keep the review sheet's Agent columns current
e848a1d2289b.title: When to write
e848a1d2289b.content: Write as each step completes, not once at the end. Times, heads and steps come from bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/agent-record.ts, never typed. | step | per comment (Agent - Comments) | per change set (Agent - Change Sets) | . | work starts | Agentic status Working | Agent step reading (agent-record.ts step reading) | . | proposing, editing |   | Agent step proposing or editing | . | PR opened, or a push to it | PR open; action taken, applied in, handled by, date actioned | Pull request, Staging review page, What the PRs changed; PR head, Staging deploy and Agent completed from agent-record.ts push; Agent step pushing | . | preview on gh-pages, then live |   | Staging built from, Staging built; Staging deploy pushed, deploying, deployed; Agent step staging, deploying | . | Ready for agent acted on, no new commit | date actioned | Agent completed from agent-record.ts done | . | blocked on a decision | Needs human, and what is needed in action taken | Agent step idle | . | ready for review | Ready for review | Agent completed; Agent step qa-review or idle | . | merged | Change merged | clear the Staging review page (a merged branch’s preview 404s); Agent step idle | . | closed unmerged | Not started, and say so in action taken | remove that PR’s line from Pull request, What the PRs changed, Agent completed and PR head; Agent step idle | . A disposition for the change set is written only from agent-record.ts dispositions (review-sheet-script, “Writing the Agent tab with the tool”).

45a87add4921.doc: Keep the review sheet's Agent columns current
45a87add4921.title: What to write
45a87add4921.content: . | Re-read the headers first. People move columns. Find each column by its header, never by a letter remembered from an earlier run. | Write only the Agent tabs. Every other tab is people’s, or formulas, or the Apps Script’s. The exceptions are the agent’s own Green feedback column (review-sheet-script) and an explicit instruction from the owner for a named cell. | Per comment (every PC in the change set): Agentic status; Agentic action taken (what was done, in a sentence); Agentic applied in (the sections or blocks changed); Agentic handled by (the agent and its session); Agentic date actioned (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MMZ, UTC, from the clock). | Per change set: Pull request (one PR URL per line); Staging review page (branches/<slug>/en/review/ while the PR is open); What the PRs changed (one line per PR, in the same order as the URLs: what that PR changes in the document, in a reader’s words); Agent completed and PR head (one line per PR, same order). A change set may have several PRs, and a line in any per-PR column always matches the line of its URL in Pull request. | Staging built and Staging built from: when, and from which commit, the preview was last built, read from the newest gh-pages commit under branches/<slug>/. Write them on every rebuild. The script compares them with Agent completed and PR head and flags a preview built before the last push as stale. | Agent step: write idle (or the next step) before leaving a change set. A step left behind shows “no update for N min” on the sheet. | Append, never reorder. A change set new to the tab goes at the end. Review Change Sets’ typed columns sit beside rows derived from it, so moving a row moves people’s inputs onto the wrong change set. | No reviewer names or emails anywhere the agent writes, in the sheet or in the repository. Name feedback by tab, row and column header. | Only a PR that edits the document for the change set goes in Pull request (public-comment §”Which PR counts”). | .

bf57f59fd3a7.doc: Keep the review sheet's Agent columns current
bf57f59fd3a7.title: Checking it
bf57f59fd3a7.content: After writing, read the change set’s row on Review Change Sets (or Contributor Feedback) back. Once the Apps Script has refreshed (its timer runs every minute), its Agentic status shows <repo>#n (status, completed) · what it changed for each PR, and Staging review shows no ⚠ unless the preview really is behind. A missing or wrong line there means an Agent cell is missing or out of step.
