d4a8e5018d6a.title: The review sheet’s Apps Script
d4a8e5018d6a.content: The sheet itself, its tabs and who writes each column are the public-comment skill’s (§”The live review sheet”). This skill is the script that keeps that sheet’s links current, and the Tool review-sheet-sync that builds it. Links inside a cell’s text (a section, a page, a “No. n” in a joined column) cannot come from a formula, which makes at most one link per cell. They are rich text, which goes stale when the sheet changes, so a Google Apps Script bound to the sheet keeps them. Never paste them by hand from an agent: the next edit undoes it.

acf40d2a7ec6.title: Inputs and outputs
acf40d2a7ec6.content: Every actor on a review sheet reads and writes only what this table says. Columns are named by header, never by letter. “People’s tab” is Contributor Feedback (drafting) or Review Public Comments and Review Change Sets (public comment). | actor | reads | writes | never writes | . | People (Authoring Committee, Feedback Review Committee) | the whole sheet | Blue columns on the people’s tabs; cell comments | Green, Grey, Orange, Agent tabs, Config | . | Editor (the Config EDITORS list) | the whole sheet | Orange Ready for agent, Ready for merge | Green, Grey, Agent tabs, Config | . | Owner | the whole sheet | Config EDITORS | anything the agent or script writes | . | Apps Script (review-sheet.gs, built by Tool review-sheet-sync) | Config (CFG, COLS, DATA, EDITORS); the people’s tabs; the Agent tab(s) | Grey columns (ids, links, joins); Green columns copied from the Agent tab(s); the STALE mark on the agent column; Ready for agent back to No once, on the turn to stale; the Watch tab; protections on the Ready columns; the QC problems at the top of Disposition (agent) | Blue columns’ contents; Orange except the stale reset; the Agent tab(s) | . | Agent (sync or watcher) | the whole sheet, and above all the people’s Blue Disposition of each comment, which its dispositions start from; the folio’s repository | the Agent tab(s) (one row per change set, and in public comment one row per comment on Agent - Comments), including Disposition (change set) in the format below; the agent column, Feedback (agent) (drafting) or Change Set Feedback (agent) (public comment); Config rows other than EDITORS | Blue, Orange, Grey; the Title (on both kinds of sheet); Change Set (human) | . | QA reviewer (independent: an agent session that did not write the PR, or a person) | the change set’s Disposition (change set), the people’s Blue Disposition and feedback, the PR’s diff at its head commit, the staging QA report | QA gate (change set) and QA report (change set) on the Agent tab, nothing else | everything else, and never a change set whose PR it wrote | . | Tool review-sheet-sync | the folio’s review/*/sheet-sync.json, anchors, line map | Code.gs (generic); the Config rows for one sheet (--config ... --out rows); a drafting sheet’s TOC rows (--toc-out rows) | the sheet itself | . | Script review-anchors-from-folio.ts | the folio’s document manifests and block prose; optionally the library file it was seeded from | folio/<doc>/review-anchors.json (--check compares) | the sheet | . A question to people goes in the sheet, not only in chat. The agent’s feedback cell has a fixed layout. The agent writes, in this order and nothing else: . Decision needed: <one question, in plain words, naming what it is about> A. <option> (recommended) B. <option> Answer in your feedback column, then an Editor sets Ready for agent to Yes. Proposed direction: <what the agent proposes or did, in one to three lines> Next: <what happens next, and who does it> . | The ask comes first. Leave the Decision needed block out when nothing is asked; the cell then opens with Proposed direction:, and the script puts a “Please review: do you agree with the proposed direction below?” ask on its status line. | One option says (recommended); options are lettered so people answer with one letter. | Tags (Decision needed:, Proposed direction:, Next: and other line-start labels) are the only bold text, in black. The script bolds them; never write Markdown **. | Say only what stands now. History (“Step 2”, “Already done”, “Decided (Q1 …)”) goes to Disposition (agent), never here. Pull request state comes from the script’s ⏳ line, so the agent does not restate it. | At most 10 lines, so the row shows it whole. | Name pull requests and issues as repo#n (e.g. dth-hrh#82). The script links each one, and under its ⏳ line adds ↳ Where to review:, one link per Selected Section to that section on the change set’s preview (or on the published draft while there is no preview). The agent writes no URLs of its own for these. | . Selected Sections bound the work. The agent reads the row’s Selected Sections before it proposes anything, and its proposal, its edits and its PR stay inside them. A row with no section picked gets a Decision needed: question asking which sections (with the agent’s guess as the recommended option), or, for a row from an issue that names its block, the agent fills them in from the issue. When an edit must reach outside them (a glossary term, a figure in another chapter), the cell says so on its own line: Outside the selected sections: <which, and why>. The watcher checks every row against this layout on each poll (tools/review-log-watch/lint.ts, skill review-log-watch) and fixes any cell it flags. The lint also fails a row with feedback and no section picked, and a row whose PR changes a chapter none of its sections are in without the Outside the selected sections: line. When the agent needs a person to decide something about a change set, it writes the Decision needed block into that row’s agent column and sets the row’s Agentic status to Needs human on the Agent tab. The sheet never shows those words: Agentic status opens with Needs you: answer the agent’s question, and Agentic status (filter) reads Needs you: answer the agent's question, so the “Needs you” filter view finds it. The ⏳ line says “Needs you” only when the cell holds a Decision needed block; with none it says the question is missing. A card in the agent’s chat may carry the same question, but the sheet is the record people see. When the question is answered, the agent removes the block from the feedback and adds the decision, with who made it, to Disposition (agent). Disposition (agent): the change set’s decisions and dispositions. The agent keeps one record per change set in the Agent tab’s Disposition (change set), and the script shows it, read-only, in the Green Disposition (agent) column, just right of Ready for merge, on Review Change Sets or Contributor Feedback. An empty one reads, in bold, ⚠ No disposition yet for Nos. 127 to 131 and 134 when the change set has comments. It holds: . | The decision history, oldest first, one line per decision, never removed or rewritten: Decided (Q1, 2026-10-31): A, by the Editor; <what it means>. Change Set Feedback (agent) holds only the current proposal and any open question. | One disposition per comment, after an optional overall statement for the whole change set: . Overall: <a statement for the whole change set> No. 136: Accepted. DPI-F defined at first use, with a glossary entry. Nos. 127 to 135, 138 and 139: Not accepted. Already addressed. No. 326: Partially accepted. <what was done, and what was not> . A disposition is one of Accepted, Partially accepted, Not accepted, Noted, Deferred, Duplicate, Out of scope or Withdrawn, first after the colon. Every comment of the change set gets exactly one. The script checks this (dispositionProblems) and puts any problem, in bold, at the top of Disposition (agent): ⚠ No disposition yet for No. 140, 141, ⚠ No. 9 is not in this change set, ⚠ No. 136 has two dispositions, or a line whose word is not a disposition. It never edits the Agent tab. Drawn from the people’s dispositions. Before writing a comment’s line, the agent reads that comment’s Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments (drafting: the row’s Blue Disposition). Where a person has set one, the line uses the same word; where it is empty or Pending, the agent proposes one. A word that differs from the people’s is flagged (⚠ No. 136: Accepted here, Noted in the people's Disposition) for the committee to settle, and never corrected by the agent or the script. The record is written before the staging preview is made, and kept current with each push. | . Once an Editor sets Ready for merge to Yes, the record as it stands is the summary: the agent puts it in the merge commit and posts it as the closing comment on the change set’s issue. From a sibling agent. An agent that is not the one talking with the owner, such as a project thread or a subagent, also writes its question here when the sheet governs the work. It is the review-sheet channel of the harness skill hand-back-to-discussion (cat-harness schemas/skills/hand-back-to-discussion/input.schema.json): . | channel field | on the sheet | . | spreadsheetId | the sheet, as the folio’s review/*/sheet-sync.json names it | . | tab | Review Change Sets, or Contributor Feedback on a drafting sheet | . | row | the change set id or comment number, never a row index | . | column | Change Set Feedback (agent) or Feedback (agent), by header | . The block, the Agentic status and the replacement on answer are the same as above. The sheet is an extra copy, never the only one: the sibling still hands the question back to the discussion agent, which asks the owner. A Blue-column answer counts as the answer in either place. The agent that takes it routes it to the other copy and marks that copy answered (the chat copy is struck through, with [Edit: …] added). What it keeps current. Columns are found by header text, so people may move them. | tab | column | becomes | . | Review Public Comments | No. | a link to the comment’s page (commentUrl + its ref from Agent’s Comment ref) | . | Review Public Comments | Sections | each section number, appendix, named section or chapter links to its first page in the draft | . | Review Public Comments | Page | each printed page or range links to that page | . | Review Public Comments | Agentic status | one line per pull request of the PC’s change-sets (Agent’s Pull request (change set)), <repo>#n (status, completed) · what it changed (the repository in the link text, because Sheets’ link popup cuts the URL short): the PR linked; the PC’s Agentic status and the matching line of Agent completed (UTC, change set) in bold; then the matching line of What the PRs changed (change set). A PC in several change-sets lists all of their PRs, each once. With no PR, the status alone | . | Review Public Comments | Line no(s) / Table / Figure | each p.N and each line(s) N–M / L N links to its page. Draft line numbers restart, so a line is placed on the page, near the row’s own pages, whose numbered lines hold it | . | Review Change Sets | Sections, Pages | the union over the change-set’s comments, sorted by page, each linked | . | Review Change Sets | Agentic status | the same, per change-set; the status is its PCs’ Agentic statuses, each once | . | Review Change Sets | Agentic status (filter) | one plain value per change set, for a filter view: “Needs you: answer the agent’s question” if any of its comments needs a person, else the least advanced of its comments’ Agentic statuses (Not started, Working, PR open, Ready for review, Change merged); “Not in comment record” only when all are | . | Review Change Sets | Public Comments | No. n (Status) · comment, status in bold, joined by a blank line | . | Review Change Sets | Suggested Revisions, PC Committee Feedback, Dispositions | No. n · text, one per comment | . Change Set Feedback (agent) (Review Change Sets, green, right of Ready for merge). The agent writes its proposed direction for resolving the change set here, and any question for people (§”Inputs and outputs”). The script only marks it stale. It is a proposal, never a person’s feedback: a tool that collects the people’s Committee Feedback (…) columns by header must leave it out, or show it apart, and it decides nothing. Column names live in Config COLS (rcs.agentFeedback, draft.agentFeedback). The script finds each column under any of its names (aliasOf, SAME_COLUMN), including the earlier Architect Feedback …, Architect Feedback (agent) and Contributor Feedback (agent), and a feedback basis written under those still matches. Every No. n in Review Change Sets links to #gid=<Review Public Comments>&range=A<row>. Do not link to a named range by #rangeid=: Sheets shows “Invalid range” for a named range whose id was set through the API. One script, one Config tab per sheet. Code.gs is the same file for every document: review-sheet.gs, stamped with its commit and made plain ASCII. Nothing about a document is in it. What differs per document lives in the sheet’s Config tab: visible, locked to the sheet’s owner, columns Key and Value, rows CFG, COLS and DATA, each JSON with a leading | (so Sheets never reads it as a number or formula), a long value continued on the next rows under the same key. DATA explains itself in its ABOUT entry. In public-comment mode it holds SECTIONS (each section the comments can name: key → [name shown, PDF page]), ABBREVIATIONS (short names such as HWR → a section key), PAGE_LINES ([PDF page, first line, last line]), PAGE_OFFSET (PDF page = printed page + this) and LAST_PAGE. In drafting mode it holds TOC (the dropdown: [name shown, anchor]). The script also reads the short names K, ABBR, LP, OFFSET and MAX. # the script, once per platform version bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/build-review-sheet-script.ts --script Code.gs # one document's Config rows, from the folio's repository root bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/build-review-sheet-script.ts \ --repo . --config review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json --out config-rows.json . A drafting sheet also gets its TOC tab (the Selected Sections dropdown): . bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/build-review-sheet-script.ts \ --repo . --config review/drafting/sheet-sync.json --out config-rows.json --toc-out toc-rows.json . The agent writes config-rows.json into the Config tab (A1 down, columns A and B, clearing rows below) with the Sheets connector, which runs as the owner, and keeps the tab protected so only the owner can edit it. CFG and COLS, which a person might edit by hand, are indented JSON cut into cells between lines, and column B wraps; DATA, generated from the folio, stays compact. The script joins a key’s cells and parses them. Neither file is committed: both are rebuilt. Install it, once per sheet, from the sheet owner’s account, because Google asks the owner to authorise the script: §”Installing the script, step by step” below. installTriggers runs a full refresh, then installs two triggers: every edit of the three tabs marks the sheet dirty, and every minute a dirty sheet is rebuilt. The agent writes the Agent tab through the API, which fires no edit, so the timer also rebuilds after an Agent change: . | Drafting sheets rebuild incrementally. An edit rebuilds only the rows it touched, at once, so a pick shows its link and a new row its Change-set within seconds. The timer rebuilds only the rows whose change set’s Agent row changed (the script keeps a short hash per change set). A new table of contents in Config, an edit of the header row, or Refresh now rebuilds everything. | Public-comment sheets rebuild whole, since a comment feeds its change sets: at once while a rebuild takes under 5 s, otherwise gathered for the timer, which also rebuilds when the Agent tab changed since the last rebuild. On a sheet too slow to rebuild per edit, an edit of Review Change Sets still flags a stale proposal at once (staleNow, reading only that tab and the agent’s change-set tab). | . Folio Assistant → Refresh now rebuilds at once. Stale staging previews. The agent records when it built a change set’s preview in the Agent tab’s Staging built (UTC, change set), beside Agent completed (UTC, change set). When a PR of the change set was completed after the build, the script writes the Staging review cell as review ⚠ stale: built <time>, PR changed since, in both modes (Review Change Sets takes the link from the Agent tab’s Staging review page (change set) where it names one). Without a build time it claims nothing. The preview page shows its own live banner too (the site’s staging build, cat-harness-tools). Checked by commit. Times can agree while the preview is still wrong, so the agent also records, on each pass over a change set with an open PR: . | Agent tab column | what the agent writes | where it reads it | . | PR head (change set) | each PR’s latest commit, one per line, in the PR order | the PR (gh pr view --json headRefOid) | . | Staging built from (change set) | the commit the preview was built from | the newest gh-pages commit touching branches/<slug>/. Its message is staging(<slug>): from <sha> when an agent staged it (stage-local.ts), or Publish <site> <sha8> preview of <branch> when the site-publish workflow did; both forms are accepted | . | Staging deploy (change set) | the restage’s stage, updated as it moves: building (the site is being built), pushed (on gh-pages, waiting for Pages), deploying (Pages is deploying it; pending reads the same), deployed, or failed | the Pages deployment of that gh-pages commit: gh api repos/<o>/<r>/pages/builds/latest, or, where that endpoint is blocked, the conclusion of the “pages build and deployment” run in actions/runs?head_sha=<gh-pages commit> | . On every push, in the same pass: write the new PR head, set Staging deploy to building, set each comment’s status, and stamp Agent completed with the clock (date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%MZ'), never an estimate. A push recorded only in prose leaves the sheet saying the old preview is current and the row is “Not started”. Then, as the restage moves: on the gh-pages push, write Staging built from and Staging built and set pushed; when the Pages run starts, deploying; when it succeeds, deployed. The sheet shows each stage in Staging review and the ⏳ line. With each stage before deployed the agent adds when it expects the preview live, from the clock and recent runs of the same site (gh run list --workflow pages-build-deployment and the build’s own duration): building, expected 2026-10-31 15:20Z. The sheet shows “expected live " after the stage. Writing the Agent tab with the tool . The agent does not type numbers or times into the Agent tab: a tool makes the cells, and the agent runs the sheet’s own check before writing. | Dispositions. Read Agent - Comments (No., Change-sets) and Review Public Comments (No., Disposition) with their header rows, and the change set’s current Disposition (change set) cell. Put them in an input file with the items (which numbers, which word, why; rest for “every other comment of the change set”), and run bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/agent-record.ts dispositions <input.json>. The tool takes the change set’s numbers from the sheet, groups them (Nos. 127 to 131, 134, 135, 138 and 139), uses the people’s Blue word where an item names none, keeps every earlier Decided line, and runs dispositionProblems from the same review-sheet.gs the sheet runs. If anything would show a ⚠, it prints the problems, exits 1 and writes nothing: fix the input and run it again. Write its output, unchanged, to Disposition (change set). | On every push. agent-record.ts push --head <full sha> --expect <minutes> prints PR head, Staging deploy (building, expected <time>) and Agent completed, the times from the clock. Write all three in one update. | After acting on Ready for agent with no new commit (the PR already held the change), run agent-record.ts done and write the Agent completed it prints, so it is later than the Ready time and the ⏳ line moves on. Not push: nothing is restaged, so Staging deploy stays as it is. | When the QA gate passes, run agent-record.ts qa-pass --cs <CS-nnn> --head <sha> --summary "<one line>" --report <url> (or pass --qa-gate "Passed <sha>: <one line>" and optional --blocks <b1,b2> / --since <ref>). It checks the gate string with the sheet’s own qaGate and writes one editing-hci-validation workflow instance (beans/workflows/editing--<block>.json) per changed block, advancing through Task_Commit with the change-set id, the Passed <sha> QA review and the editor’s review-sheet decision, so check:corpus-gate goes green. | The PR’s review brief. agent-record.ts brief <input.json> --look "<where to look>" prints the same Overall and per-comment lines as Markdown between <!-- review-brief --> and <!-- /review-brief -->. Put it in the PR body: the staging review page’s “What to expect in this review” pane shows only that section. Add --pcs <public-comment dashboard url> (on smart-ra, https://litlfred.github.io/smart-ra/en/folio-assistant-core/public-comments/folio/dpi-h-ra/) and every comment number links to its row there. The link target is the comment’s own id from the Agent - Comments “Comment ref” column (pass those rows as comments): the sheet’s No. is not the id (on DPI-H, No. 136 is PC-0137). A run such as “127 to 131” is spelled out, so no comment hides behind a range. | Each move. agent-record.ts step <name> (§”Where the agent is: Agent step”). | . Drafting sheets have no comment numbers: pass "nos": []; the tool then only keeps the history. The script compares only; it stays @OnlyCurrentDoc with no internet access. Short and full shas both work: it compares the common prefix, at least 7 characters. It reads the active PR as the last one listed (one branch, one active PR per row) and writes, in this order of precedence: ⚠ deploy failed; ⚠ stale: built from <sha>, PR now at <sha> (with ; restaging: <stage> while one runs); ⚠ restaging: building the preview | on gh-pages, waiting for Pages to deploy | Pages is deploying it. A change set with a recorded PR head but no preview link shows ⚠ no preview yet: not ready for merge. A change set is never ready for merge without a preview to review: the agent stages a preview for every PR it opens, and the “Merge decision due” filter view leaves out rows whose Staging review starts with ⚠. Without these columns the script falls back to the time check above. It finds them by header, so on a sheet that lacks them the agent adds them at the right of the Agent (change sets) tab. Ready for agent after the preview. The PR has not changed yet when an Editor sends a row back, so the commit check above passes. The script records, as a document property ready:<CS>, the time it first sees a row’s Ready for agent at Yes (cleared on No). A Yes it first sees on a row the agent has already completed counts from that completion instead, since the script cannot know when it was set. When that time is later than Staging built, after the deploy checks, it writes ⚠ missing feedback from <time>: the preview still shows the PR, but not the feedback an Editor has just sent to the agent. Only the sheet says so; the review page cannot know the sheet. The same time makes Agentic status open with **Waiting on the agent since (Ready for agent set)**, until the agent records a later completion or sets the status to Working. Stale agent proposals. Feedback (agent) (drafting) and Change Set Feedback (agent) (Review Change Sets) carry the agent’s proposal. The agent records what it wrote against in the Agent tab’s Feedback basis (change set): feedbackBasis() in tools/review-sheet-sync/feedback-issue.ts, a hash of the row’s blue cells (drafting: Title, Selected Sections, people’s Contributor Feedback; public comment: Title, TWG (CS), people’s Committee Feedback). The script computes the same hash; while they differ it puts “⚠ Stale: the row changed since this proposal; the agent will propose again.” on the proposal’s first line, and takes it off if the row changes back. The agent’s next sync replaces the proposal and the basis. In a public-comment sheet the agent writes a 2: basis: feedbackBasis(header, row, ["Title", "TWG (CS)"], "Committee Feedback", PC_BASIS_GREY). It also covers the grey content Review Change Sets joins from the change set’s comments (Sections, Pages, Public Comments, Suggested Revisions, PC Committee Feedback, Dispositions, TWG (PCs)), so a proposal goes stale when a comment it rests on changes, not only when a blue cell on its own row does. The agent’s own columns (Agentic status, Staging review page, the proposal) are never part of it, so the agent’s writes never make its own proposals stale. A stored basis without 2: is compared with the blue-only hash, so a sheet moves over one row at a time as the agent rewrites each basis. Where the change set is. Below any stale mark, the script keeps one bold line starting with ⏳ at the top of the agent’s proposal (progressLine, withProgress), and replaces it on every refresh: “Ready for merge set: the agent will merge dth-hrh#7.”; “Ready for agent set <time>: the agent will act on this and rewrite it.”; “The agent is working on dth-hrh#7.”; or “dth-hrh#7 open; no preview yet | preview current (built <time>) | preview missing feedback from <time>.” An open PR’s line carries the agent’s last completion time (“smart-ra#185 open, updated 2026-10-31 14:41Z; preview stale: built from 420acd3, PR now at e7b4094.”). No pull request, a merged one, or an empty proposal gets no line. The agent never writes this line or any status line of its own, and drops it when it rewrites the proposal; the next refresh (within a minute) puts it back. The agent records the facts in the Agent tab (PR head, Staging deploy, Agent completed from date -u) and the sheet says them. An Editor’s Orange change (a Ready column) is not part of the basis, so it never marks the proposal stale: it shows here as a note, and Ready stays as the Editor set it. The note appears at once: an edit of a Ready for agent cell records its time (noteReady_) and, on a slow public-comment sheet, staleNow writes that row’s line without waiting for the timer. How to tell it works. The first run of installTriggers takes about 20 seconds for 800 rows and its execution log ends “Execution completed” (a one-second run means onOpen was picked). Then No. is a blue link, and hovering a No. n on Review Change Sets shows a row such as A327. Failed runs are listed with their error under Executions (the clock icon) in the Apps Script editor. An agent checks from outside by reading a No. cell’s formula (=HYPERLINK(…)) and a joined cell’s text-format runs. Protected columns. The script runs as the account that installed it, so it writes the grey and green columns even when they are protected, as long as that account is an editor of the protected ranges. Install it from the owner’s account. Reuse it for another document’s public comment. Nothing in the template names a document. Give the new folio: . | The frozen review version in library/<slug>/, with its pdf-line-map.json, and the folio’s review-anchors.json (the extraction described in public-comment §”The one fact everything rests on” makes both). | A draft/ redirect on its site to the library viewer, or use the full viewer address as draftUrl. | review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json: . { "anchors": "folio/<doc>/review-anchors.json", "lineMap": "library/<slug>/pdf-line-map.json", "draftUrl": "draft/#page=", "commentUrl": "en/folio-assistant-core/public-comments/folio/<doc>/index.html#", "namedSections": { "CR": "Client Registry" }, "aliases": { "how to use the guidance": "How to use this guidance" }, "tabs": { "RPC": "Review Public Comments" }, "columns": { "rpc": { "lines": "Line no(s) / Table / Figure" } } } . namedSections lists the unnumbered sections reviewers cite by name, and their abbreviations, which are matched only in capitals. aliases gives other names for front-matter chapters. tabs and columns override the defaults in build-review-sheet-script.ts only where the new sheet’s headers differ. The printed-to-PDF offset and the last printed page are read from the line map. | A sheet with the tabs above, Agent’s No., Comment ref and Change-sets columns filled, then build and install as above. | . Test it without a sheet. bun test folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/review-sheet.test.ts builds the script for a small fake folio and runs it against a fake of the Apps Script services over the three tabs. It checks every link and join in the table above, the Agentic status lines, and the edit-and-timer refresh. It does not prove a given sheet has the script installed or current: that is How to tell it works. Change the template, the builder or this table only together with that test. Rewrite the Config tab when the review anchors change, the draft link moves, or a tab or a header the script reads is renamed. Re-paste Code.gs only when the script itself changes. Renaming a header the script reads, without rewriting Config, leaves that column unlinked; it fails nothing.

2ef04316c117.title: Ready for agent: Yes, No, Completed
2ef04316c117.content: The script sets Ready for agent from Yes to Completed once the agent’s last push is later than the time Yes was set and the preview of it is live and current (no ⚠ in Staging review). An Editor sets Yes again to send the row back to the agent. A row that turns stale goes back to No from Yes or Completed. The agent never writes the Orange columns. Every pass ends with a finish stamp after the Ready time: . | The agent ends EVERY pass with a stamp from the tool: push --head <sha> when it committed, else done, which writes Agent completed and the step idle together. A proposal that waits for the Editor ends with step proposed. The script counts a later idle or proposed step as the end of the pass, the same as Agent completed. | Before stopping, the agent re-reads Ready for agent: if it was set after the pass began, the pass is not over; act on it (or done if there is nothing new). | A Ready for agent with no step recorded after it for 20 minutes shows “⚠ no agent has picked this up for N min: ask in the project chat” on the ⏳ line and in Agentic status, so a row with no agent never looks like quiet work. | Every log needs a watcher: the setup is not complete until an agent thread is watching the sheet. A thread acts only when something wakes it, so the watcher needs a scheduled wake: an hourly scheduled task, plus a chain of 3-minute delayed wakes (send_later) that each pass renews. Each wake runs the mechanical check of skill review-log-watch first, and does agent work only when it reports a change. For that check the script writes, in a drafting sheet, a hash of every cell people set on Contributor Feedback to the hidden Watch tab (F1:I1: Cells hash, the hash, Checked (UTC), the time), on every refresh and timer tick. In a public-comment sheet it covers Review Change Sets (Title, TWG (CS), every Committee Feedback column, Ready for agent, Dispositions confirmed, Ready for merge, Change Set (human)) and Review Public Comments (every Committee Feedback column, Disposition, Change Set (human), TWG (human)), keyed by Change-set id and comment No., so an inserted row changes nothing; it is written on every refresh, which the timer runs only when an edit or the Agent tab changed. Without a watcher, a Ready for agent waits until somebody happens to ask. | .

9d239368f776.title: One agent column, status on top
9d239368f776.content: A sheet without an Agentic status column gets the status on top of the agent column (Change Set Feedback (agent) or Feedback (agent)) instead: . ⏳ smart-ra#185 open, updated 2026-10-31 15:26Z; preview current (built 15:19Z). ↳ smart-ra#185 (PR open, 2026-10-31 15:26Z) · DPI-F at first use <the agent's proposal and any Decision needed question> . The ⏳ line and each ↳ line (one per pull request, linked; and the ask when people must answer) are the script’s; it replaces them on every refresh and never stacks them. The agent writes only what is below them and never starts its own text with ⏳ or ↳. Agentic status (filter) stays, for the filter views. A sheet that keeps its Agentic status column keeps the status there; delete that column to switch.

a510f5a981b0.title: The QA gate, before Ready for merge
a510f5a981b0.content: Who. A reviewer that did not write the change: another agent session, or a person. The authoring agent never gates its own pull request. What it checks, against the PR’s head commit: . | every comment (drafting: every feedback item) of the change set has one disposition (the script’s dispositionProblems already flags gaps); | each disposition agrees with the people’s Blue Disposition, where one is set; | each Accepted or Partially accepted item has its change in the PR’s diff, and the change does what the line says; | a Not accepted, Noted, Deferred, Duplicate or Out of scope item has no change in the diff that contradicts it; | the diff changes nothing that no disposition accounts for; | the staging QA report for that commit has no failing gate. | . What it writes, on the Agent tab’s change-set row and nowhere else: . | QA gate (change set): first line Passed <head sha>: <one line> or Failed <head sha>: <the first problem>, then one line per problem; | QA report (change set): the link to the QA report for the staged commit: the tree pr/<n>/<sha> on the folio’s QA reports branch (in smart-ra, cat/cat-harness/qa-reports; check the branch name, it varies). | . When the gate passes, run agent-record.ts qa-pass (§”Writing the Agent tab with the tool”). What the sheet shows. Staging review reads review · QA report (both links), then the gate: ✓ QA gate passed (b20534f), or in bold ⚠ QA gate: no independent review yet: not ready for merge, ⚠ QA gate failed: <why>, or ⚠ QA gate stale: reviewed 1234567, PR now at b20534f: not ready for merge once the PR moves on (qaGate). If Ready for merge is set before the gate passes, the agent’s ⏳ line says it will not merge until it does, and the agent does not merge. A failed gate sends the change set back to the author, who updates the PR and its dispositions; the gate then runs again on the new head.

00515b00cad2.title: Unconfirmed dispositions block the merge
00515b00cad2.content: The agent’s disposition for a comment is a proposal until the committee records its own word in the people’s Disposition column. While any comment of a change set is still Pending (or empty) there, Disposition (agent) shows “⚠ Not confirmed by the committee (Disposition still Pending): Nos. …”. Staging review shows “⚠ dispositions not complete or not confirmed: not ready for merge”, and the ⏳ line says the agent will not merge until every disposition is complete and confirmed. The agent never merges such a change set, even with Ready for merge = Yes. agent-record.ts dispositions does not stop on this line, because confirming is the committee’s step, not a fault in the agent’s record. An Editor confirms in the Orange Dispositions confirmed column, left of Ready for merge. There are only three ways to confirm, and no per-comment checkbox: . | Yes confirms every agent disposition in the change set; | comment numbers typed in the cell (“No. 327”) confirm just those; a number outside the change set is flagged; | to differ on one comment, the committee sets that comment’s own Disposition on Review Public Comments, and a mismatch is flagged. | . The script adds the column itself, inside its locked run (so no other refresh writes by a shifted position), and keeps its Yes/No dropdown.

55ecd1d8ede9.title: Where the agent is: Agent step
55ecd1d8ede9.content: At every move the agent writes Agent step (change set) on its change-set tab, with agent-record.ts step <name> so the time comes from the clock. The script shows it on the ⏳ line for as long as it holds, e.g. “⏳ Agent: editing the document (since today 17:20Z)” (or “yesterday …”, or “3 days ago, 2026-10-28 …”), and adds “⚠ no update for N min” after 30 minutes. A question for a person (“Needs you: answer the Decision needed below, then set Ready for agent to Yes”) always comes first. The script adds the column, at the end of the tab, inside its locked run. | step | when the agent writes it | BPMN task | . | reading | it starts on new feedback or a Ready for agent | (start of Task_Propose / Task_EditInPullRequest; public comment: Task_AuthorEdits) | . | proposing | it writes or rewrites its proposal | Task_Propose (public comment: Task_ProposeChangeSets) | . | editing | it edits the document on the branch | Task_EditInPullRequest (Task_AuthorEdits) | . | pushing | it commits and pushes | end of the edit task, with push | . | staging | the preview is building | the staging step of the edit task | . | deploying | Pages is publishing the preview | as above | . | qa-review | it waits for the independent reviewer | Task_QaGate | . | merging | it merges after Ready for merge | Task_Merge (Task_Incorporate) | . | proposed | it has written a proposal and waits for Ready for agent = Yes; the ⏳ line says “Proposal ready: set Ready for agent to Yes” | end of Task_Propose | . | idle | it stops: done, or waiting on a person | — | . The agent writes its proposal straight into the feedback cell, which drops the ⏳ line; the timer watches that column (without the script’s own lines), so the status comes back on the next tick without anyone pressing Refresh. Write idle (or the next step) before leaving a change set; a step left behind turns into the “no update” warning.

c0f02e0f0ef8.title: Rows at most 10 lines high
c0f02e0f0ef8.content: Sheets cannot scroll inside a cell, so on the people’s tabs (Review Public Comments, Review Change Sets, Contributor Feedback) a row whose text would run past about 10 lines is fixed at that height and the rest is clipped. Clicking the cell shows the whole text in the formula bar, and double-clicking opens it scrollable. Rows that fit size themselves, and a row that shrinks back under the cap is released. The script estimates lines from column widths (capRows), so it needs no layout access.

7a9f9eac054c.title: Structured cells and column hover text
7a9f9eac054c.content: A list is never run together with semicolons. Agents write “What changed” and “What the PRs changed (change set)” one item per line, as • <item> (No. n), under a label line ending in a colon. The script splits any remaining a; b; c into bullet lines, and bolds line-start labels (What changed:, Proposed direction:) and comment references (No. 326, Nos. 1, 2 and 5). Every column head carries a hover note saying what the column holds and who fills it in, without naming its colour. The notes are HEADER_NOTES in the script, keyed by header (or <tab kind>|<header> where one header means different things on different tabs); a head named Name (initials) uses its Name (*) entry. The script owns the note on every head it knows and writes only notes that changed; a head it does not know keeps its own. A new column gets its note in the same change that adds its header; review-sheet.test.ts checks that every known head has one and that none names a colour. The QA report link opens the viewer, the preview review page’s per-section QA table (<review page>#heat), with the raw qa-reports entry beside it as “files”. Text in a cell that is not a link is written plain, so it never inherits a link’s blue underline.

323c4bdc7717.title: Sheet conventions (any agent-written Google Sheet)
323c4bdc7717.content: These hold for every Google Sheet an agent writes or keeps current, not only the review sheets: . | colour | who controls it | lock | . | grey | mechanical: ids, headers, copied source text | owner only | . | blue | people: the human-controlled columns | open to the sheet’s editors | . | orange | editor gates (Ready for agent, Ready for merge) | its own lock, owner plus the named editors | . | green | agent-derived: links, joins, status | owner only | . | Templates are locked to the owner except the blue columns; the orange gates carry their own lock that starts with the owner alone. | The Config tab is visible, never hidden, and locked to the owner: the agent writes it, people can read what the sheet is set up for. | Instructions name no colour. The key on the first line reads “Column colours:” then one phrase per colour (“your input, by …”, “written by the agent”, …), each shown in its colour, and the steps name columns (“Reviewers update Contributor Feedback”, “an Editor sets Ready for agent”), never a colour. The script’s colourInstructions shows each column name bold in a darker shade of that column’s header fill, on every refresh, so text the agent rewrites through the API, which drops the colours, gets them back within a minute. | Which template depends on the document’s authoring stage: the Contributor template while it is being drafted and authored, the Public Comment Review template once public comment opens. | .

24999ba32522.title: Published with the document’s site
24999ba32522.content: scripts/review-sheet-site.ts --out <site> (package script site:review-sheet in a folio, a sourceSteps entry of its site build) writes <site>/review-sheet/: the generic Code.gs, each review/<mode>/sheet-sync.json as <mode>.config-rows.json, review-sheet.jsonld (the script as schema:SoftwareSourceCode with its SHA-256 and commit; each document’s settings as a schema:Dataset linked to its sheet and to the Tool), and an index.html with the setup steps and the SHA-256 to check a pasted copy against. Point people there rather than sending the file.

f86b3f4324db.title: Trusting the script
f86b3f4324db.content: A copy of a sheet carries its Apps Script, so anyone starting from a template should know what they are running. | Nothing runs until the sheet’s owner allows it. The owner runs installTriggers; Google then shows the scopes, and the triggers run as the owner, whoever’s edit fires them. So an editor’s edit makes owner code read what they typed: the script therefore never writes typed text as a formula (asText, q), and touches only this sheet. | Security review. tools/review-sheet-sync/security-review.md records the threat model and findings F1 to F10, each fixed with a test or accepted with its reason. Re-review on any new write sink, service, or editor-writable tab. | The agent caps new issues (finding F6): it opens a change set’s issue only for a row with a Title or feedback text, and asks a person before opening more than 20 in one sync. | This sheet only. The template starts with @OnlyCurrentDoc, so the consent screen asks for “this spreadsheet”, not all of the owner’s spreadsheets. The script uses only SpreadsheetApp, PropertiesService, LockService and ScriptApp: no UrlFetchApp, mail or Drive, so it sends nothing out. review-sheet-security.test.ts fails if one of those, or eval/new Function, appears. | Three permissions, one file. Google works out a script’s permissions from its code, and @OnlyCurrentDoc narrows the spreadsheet one to this sheet. So the consent screen asks for exactly three: this spreadsheet, the script’s own triggers, and its menu. tools/review-sheet-sync/appsscript.json records those three for the security test, which fails if the code would need more. It is a record, not a file to paste. | Plain ASCII. The built script escapes every non-ASCII character, so a paste cannot mangle it. The build prints its SHA-256; compare it with the pasted copy. | Wrong sheet. Pasted into a sheet it was not built for, it stops with a message naming the config and tab it expected, before installing triggers. | Check a copy against its source. The script is the same for every document, so one review covers all copies. Its header names the folio-assistant-core commit it was built from. Build again at that commit with the folio’s config and compare; or ignore the copied script and paste one you built yourself. | “Google hasn’t verified this app.” Bound scripts are unverified, so the owner clicks Advanced to continue. Publishing as a verified Workspace add-on would remove the warning. | .

ff2551bc8c8e.title: Drafting mode: editors’ and contributors’ feedback
ff2551bc8c8e.content: Before a document goes to public comment, editors and contributors give feedback on the working draft. That needs a simpler sheet: no Public Comment Source, no Review Public Comments, no TWGs. Each row of feedback is a change set (CS: a list of related comments on one topic), and each change set gets a GitHub issue. Tabs. | tab | who writes | columns | . | Contributor Feedback | people, plus the Apps Script | one row per change set. Grey, mechanical: Change-set (the script gives a used row the next CS-nnn once; it stays with the row). Blue, people: Title; Selected Sections (a multi-select dropdown of the document’s table of contents, each section indented under its chapter by three U+2800 blanks per level, since a dropdown cannot nest; not real spaces, because Sheets trims a multi-select cell and the first chip would lose them and read as Invalid; plain, because a dropdown chip cannot carry a link); any number of Contributor Feedback (…) columns, one per contributor, with their initials or name in the brackets (e.g. Contributor Feedback (CL); the script reads every column whose header is Contributor Feedback or starts Contributor Feedback (); Disposition (a dropdown: Pending, Accepted, Partially accepted, Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate, Out of scope), the committee’s verdict on the row. Orange, editors: Ready for agent (Yes, No, Completed), Ready for merge (Yes/No). Grey, by the script: Section links (each selected section on its own line, linked to its place on the document page, like the Sections column of the public-comment log). Green, by the agent: Feedback (agent), right of Ready for merge, the agent’s proposed direction (not a person’s feedback: the script leaves it out of the Contributor Feedback columns, and it decides nothing). Green, by the script from Agent: Issue (<repo>#n, linked), Agentic status (as in public-comment mode: one line per PR, <repo>#n (status, completed) · what it changed), Staging review (a “review” link to the change set’s review page on its staging preview, branches/<branch>/en/review/, while its PR is open), Agentic status (filter) (the change set’s status as one plain value, for the “By agentic status” filter view) | . | Agent | the agent only | one row per change set: Change-set, Issue (URL), Agentic status, Pull request (change set), What the PRs changed (change set), Agent completed (UTC, change set), Staging review page (change set), Feedback basis (change set). The agent writes it as each step completes, by the steps of the review-sheet-agent-columns skill; a drafting sheet has no per-comment rows, so only its change-set columns apply | . | TOC (hidden) | the script | the Sections dropdown’s list and each entry’s link. Rewritten on every refresh, so it follows the document | . Colours as in public-comment mode: grey mechanical, blue human, orange editor gates, green agent-derived. Built from the folio’s review-anchors.json: each chapter (Ch 3 Digital Transformation Approach), each numbered section (3.1 DIIG alignment) and each unnumbered section, prefixed by its chapter (Ch 3 · Objectives and key messages). A multi-select cell joins its choices with , , so commas in titles become ;. Each links to sectionUrl + the anchor (sec:3-1, chap:<dir>), which the document page carries as element ids. Config, review/drafting/sheet-sync.json: . { "mode": "drafting", "anchors": "folio/<doc>/review-anchors.json", "sectionUrl": "en/<doc>/#" } . Write the URLs relative to the folio’s site: the build resolves them against iriBase in the folio’s <instance>.json (e.g. https://litlfred.github.io/dth-hrh/), so no organisation name is written in sheet-sync.json and a folio that moves changes one iriBase and rewrites its Config. An absolute https:// URL is taken as written. tabs and columns (draft, draftAgent) override the headers as in public-comment mode. Write its Config with --config review/drafting/sheet-sync.json and install as above. The Sections dropdown is a data validation “dropdown from a range” on TOC!A2:A with Allow multiple selections ticked (step 6 below). Without the tick, a cell with two or more sections shows “Invalid: Input must fall within specified range”. The agent’s part: every change set has an issue. On each sync, for every Contributor Feedback row with a Change-set: . | If the Agent tab has no row for it, add one (Change-set, Agentic status Not started). | If that row has no Issue, open a GitHub issue in the folio’s repository: title CS-nnn: <Title> (or the first feedback line while Title is empty), body the linked sections, every Contributor Feedback (…) cell verbatim, and a link back to the sheet row. Write its URL into Issue. | When feedback is added to a row later, comment the new text on its issue. | Propose a direction in Feedback (agent) for every new row (from an issue, a person or a TWG workbook) and whenever the row changes, whoever changed it. The watcher does this on its next wake (skill review-log-watch, step 5). A question for people goes there too, as a Decision needed: block (§”Inputs and outputs”). On each sync compute feedbackBasis(header, row) (tools/review-sheet-sync/feedback-issue.ts: a short hash of Title, Selected Sections and the people’s Contributor Feedback columns). Where it differs from the Agent tab’s Feedback basis (change set), or the proposal cell is empty (a person clears it to ask for a fresh one), write a new proposal and the new basis. The script’s own writes (ids, links, tree marks) do not change the basis. | Work a change set only when Ready for agent is Yes; its PRs say Closes #n for the change set’s issue, and go to Agent’s PR columns. | When you pick a row up, say so first: set its Agent status to Working and put the URL of your conversation (the session, thread or PR discussion) in Agent conversation (change set). Agentic status then opens with An agent is working on it: conversation, linked. The script finds that column by header; on a sheet that lacks it, the agent adds it at the right of the Agent (change sets) tab. | . Title is the people’s on both kinds of sheet: the agent never writes it. In public-comment mode a Title-only row on Review Change Sets is a new change set, and the agent’s title is only the first value of a row it adds (skill review-log-watch, “Change sets people make”). Feedback from the site. A folio with .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/block-feedback.yml (copy the shared templates/issue-forms/block-feedback.yml) gets 📣 feedback links that open that form with Content, Section, Block, page and Source prefilled; the contributor picks a Type and writes Comment and Proposed change. On each sync the agent lists open issues labelled feedback that no Agent row names, and for each appends a Contributor Feedback row from tools/review-sheet-sync/feedback-issue.ts (feedbackRow): Sections the block’s TOC entry, Title a draft (<section>: <first sentence>, which people may rewrite), Contributor Feedback @login (Type): comment plus Proposed: …. The script then gives it a CS id, and the agent writes the issue’s URL into that change set’s Agent row: the feedback issue is the change set’s issue, so step 2 above opens none. A comment added to the issue later is added to the row’s next empty Contributor Feedback cell. Linked templates. Each mode keeps one template sheet in the informatics.avengers Drive, laid out as above, script installed, no rows. A new document starts from its “make a copy” link (table at the end); then the agent writes the new document’s Config tab, and the owner runs installTriggers. The script in the template needs no change. Locks in a template and its copies: every cell is locked to the owner except the blue, human-controlled columns, and the heads of the Contributor Feedback (or Committee Feedback) columns, where each contributor writes their initials. The lock covers the other headers, the grey mechanical and green agent-derived columns, the Config tab, the Agent tab and the hidden TOC. The orange Ready-for-agent and Ready-for-merge columns have a lock of their own, “Ready columns: editors”, which starts with only the owner; the owner adds each document editor to it in each copy (step 4 below). Setting up a sheet for a new document . The owner (informatics.avengers) does steps 1 to 6; the agent does step 3. | Copy the template. Open the “make a copy” link for the mode (table at the end), name the copy “ Contributor Log" or " Public Comment Log", and keep it in the informatics.avengers Drive. A file copy keeps tabs, colours, dropdowns, locks and the script. **Always copy the file** (File, then Make a copy); never build a log by copying tabs into a blank spreadsheet, which leaves the script behind. The owner keeps the latest `dist/Code.gs` pasted into both templates, so a copy starts current. | Share it. Share > add contributors or reviewers as Editor. The locks still keep them to the blue columns. | Link it to the repository (agent). Give the agent the copy’s URL and the document’s repository. The agent follows “Linking a sheet to a repository” below. Until it does, Config holds only its Instructions, Key and EDITORS rows and the Selected Sections dropdown is empty. The sheet says what to do next: the first line of each tab’s Instructions starts with ⚠ and names the next step, “Not set up yet. Step 1 of 2: ask the agent to link this sheet …” (the templates carry it, so a copy starts with it), then, once linked, “Almost set up. Step 2 of 2: choose Folio Assistant, then Install”. A short toast says the same when the sheet opens, and every run of an unlinked sheet stops with “Ask the agent to link this sheet to its document: give it this sheet’s link (ID …)”. Once installed (the timerMinutes document property installTriggers sets), the ⚠ line goes and each tab’s Instructions ends with a Document: <site> Repository: <repo> line; Config has an Instructions - Links row with the site, the repository and the sheet’s settings file. | Name the editors (owner). Type their emails in Config’s orange EDITORS row, or leave it empty so only the owner can set the Ready columns (below). | Install the script: §”Installing the script, step by step” below. A copy of the template already holds the script, so the paste is needed only when the script changes; installTriggers is needed in every copy, because triggers and the owner’s permission do not copy. A copy keeps the version it was made with: when Code.gs changes, paste it again into each sheet in use, and into the template. | Drafting only: finish the Selected Sections dropdown. installTriggers adds the rule (a dropdown from TOC!A2:A) when the column has none, and leaves an existing one alone (a rewrite would clear its tick). One setting is a person’s, once per sheet: . | click the column letter above “Selected Sections” to select the column; | choose Data, then Data validation; | open the rule for that column (the sidebar lists it by its range, such as 'Contributor Feedback'!E2:E1000, as “Dropdown (from a range)”); | under Advanced options, check that Display style is Chip; | tick Allow multiple selections; | press Done. | . The tick is greyed out unless the style is Chip. A rule that Apps Script writes (requireValueInRange) gets the Arrow style, which Apps Script cannot change. The agent therefore sets the style through the Sheets API at setup, and whenever a log’s rule reads customUiMode: ARROW: setDataValidation with the same ONE_OF_RANGE condition and "showCustomUi": true, "customUiMode": "CHIP", "strict": false. The API reads the tick (condition.allowMultipleSelections) but sets it only for ONE_OF_LIST rules, so ticking it on the range rule stays the person’s step. installTriggers cannot check either directly. It shows the steps in a 30-second toast unless it has evidence they are done: a cell already holding two sections from the list (or dropdownDone). It is a toast, never a dialog: a dialog waits for an answer in the sheet, and an Install run from the Apps Script editor then hangs until Apps Script stops it at 6 minutes (“Exceeded maximum execution time”). Only the menu’s “Which version is this?” opens a dialog. Copies made after the template has them keep them. The same steps are in the Config tab’s Instructions - Dropdown row; the script ignores that row. | . Installing the script, step by step . For the sheet’s owner, once per sheet. The Config tab’s Instructions - Install script row carries the same steps and links here. | Get the latest Code.gs. Open dist/Code.gs on GitHub and press Copy raw file (the two-squares button at the top right of the code), or open the raw file, select all and copy. It is the build of review-sheet.gs on core’s main, rewritten by build-review-sheet-script.ts --dist; a test fails when it is stale. | Open the editor. In the sheet: Extensions, then Apps Script. It opens in a new tab. “Sorry, unable to open the file at this time” (in German, “Datei kann derzeit nicht geöffnet werden”) means the browser is signed in to several Google accounts and Apps Script opened under the default one (/u/0/), which cannot see the sheet: use a private window with only the owner’s account, or change /u/0/ in the failing address to /u/1/, /u/2/, and so on. | Name the project after the sheet. Click Untitled project at the top left, type the spreadsheet’s own name (e.g. “DTH-PC Contributor Log”), and press Rename, so it is found by name in script.google.com, where bound projects are listed apart from their sheets. | Paste. Click Code.gs in the Files list on the left. Select all (Ctrl+A, or Cmd+A on a Mac), delete, paste, and save (Ctrl+S or Cmd+S, or the disk icon). Code.gs is the only file to paste: leave the project’s manifest as it is. | Run installTriggers. Reload the sheet and choose Folio Assistant, then Install. Or, in the editor, the function list next to Run and Debug shows installTriggers (it is the first function, so the default; not onOpen, which only adds the menu); press Run. | Allow it. Review permissions, pick the owner’s account. Google shows “Google hasn’t verified this app. The app is requesting access to sensitive info in your Google Account.” That is expected for a sheet’s own script, which Google never verifies: press Advanced, then **Go to (unsafe)**, then **Allow** ([why](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/7454865)). | Check it. The log shows “Execution completed”. Back in the sheet tab, reload: a Folio Assistant menu appears; Folio Assistant, then Refresh now, checks it. | Drafting sheets only: tick Allow multiple selections on the Selected Sections dropdown (step 6 of “Setting up a sheet for a new document”). | . Updating later: steps 1, 2 and 4, then Folio Assistant, then Refresh now; the automatic refresh stays installed. Sheets may run older builds: Folio Assistant, then Which version is this? shows the build the sheet runs (SCRIPT_VERSION, the stamp on the script’s header line), the Code.gs copy page, and “✓ Up to date” or “New build available” by comparing with the Config tab’s CFG.LATEST_BUILD. The agent writes LATEST_BUILD (the content stamp of the build it publishes, latestBuild()) with the Config rows, so rewrite each sheet’s Config when a new build goes out. The script never fetches. The menu is named Folio Assistant and ends with About Folio Assistant, which points to https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/; the same link is the last line of each tab’s Instructions. The library builds the menu (addMenu) and the stub asks it, so every sheet shows the same menu and a rename needs no new stub. A stub that builds its own “Review links” menu is out of date: paste dist/Stub.gs over it once. A copy of the template needs none of this: the script came with the file. Reload the copy, choose Folio Assistant, then Install, and allow it as in step 6. The menu runs installTriggers, so the editor is never opened. Renaming the bound project (step 3) is optional: a copied project is named “Copy of …” by Google. One library, a stub in each sheet . The code lives once, in a standalone Apps Script project, Folio Review Library, owned by the sheets’ owner, and every sheet runs its latest code (HEAD). Each sheet keeps only dist/Stub.gs, which never changes. Setting the library up, once: . | At script.google.com, New project; name it Folio Review Library. | Replace its code with dist/Code.gs; save. | Project settings (the gear): copy the Script ID. The library is 1us7_ApIq_XvDG-V1XtqdcyHucF0hSlST0qracv1Tw9KTb4-lAFvK1bMQ; the Config tab’s install steps and the stub name it. | . Each sheet, once (templates first, so copies inherit it): . | Extensions, then Apps Script. Replace Code.gs with dist/Stub.gs; save. | Libraries +: paste the Script ID, Look up, Version HEAD (Development mode), Identifier Review, Add. | In the sheet, Folio Assistant > Install. | . An update needs no paste. The library also holds dist/Updater.gs; updateFromGitHub, run from the library’s editor, fetches dist/Code.gs from main and writes it over the library’s Code.gs through the Apps Script API, leaving the library’s other files alone. It refuses anything that is not the review-sheet script (an error page, the stub) and logs “Updated to <version>” or “Already current”. There is no timer: an update runs when the owner runs it. Every sheet runs the new code from its next open, edit or timer. Adding the updater, once: . | Turn on the Apps Script API at https://script.google.com/home/usersettings. | In the library, Files +, Script, name it Updater; paste dist/Updater.gs; save. | Project settings: tick “Show appsscript.json manifest file in editor”, then replace appsscript.json with dist/library-appsscript.json (it adds the script.projects and script.external_request scopes); save. | Pick updateFromGitHub in the function list, Run, and allow it. | . After that an update is step 4 alone. Without the updater, an update is one paste of the new dist/Code.gs into the library. “Which version is this?” reports the library’s stamp. The stub hands its services over (Review.init) because a library has no spreadsheet of its own, so its document properties, document lock and triggers would not be the sheet’s. The stub passes its own PropertiesService, LockService and ScriptApp, and the triggers it installs name the stub’s functions. Pasted straight into a sheet, Code.gs still works alone: without init it uses the sheet’s services. HEAD runs only for people with edit access to the library. The triggers run as the owner who installed them, so that is the owner alone; an editor who uses Refresh now by hand needs the library shared with them as an editor. Linking a sheet to a repository . A copied sheet knows nothing about its document until the agent links it. Linking is repository work first and sheet work second, in this order: . | The folio has a section list. A drafting sheet’s dropdown is the document’s chapters and sections, read from folio/<doc>/review-anchors.json. The folio’s package.json declares review:anchors and check:review-anchors, both running folio-assistant-core/scripts/review-anchors-from-folio.ts --document <doc>. A document seeded from a library file adds `–library --source --source-label `; one authored from scratch (dth-pc, dth-sc) leaves all three out. Run `review:anchors` and commit the file. A new document folio declares both scripts from its first commit. | The folio names the sheet, and the rows are built: one command. From the folio’s root, with the link the person pasted: bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/build-review-sheet-script.ts --link <sheet link or id> --document <doc> --out config-rows.json --toc-out toc-rows.json. It writes review/drafting/sheet-sync.json ({"mode":"drafting","anchors":"folio/<doc>/review-anchors.json","sectionUrl":"en/<doc>/#","sheet":"<spreadsheet id>"}; an existing file keeps its settings and only gets the new sheet), then the rows. The site and repository links come from the folio’s iriBase (https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/ is https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>); a folio on another host sets "repository" in sheet-sync.json. Public comment, or to rebuild after a structural change: --config review/<mode>/sheet-sync.json instead of --link. | The agent writes the sheet. With the Sheets connector, it writes the rows from step 2: the whole Config tab from A1, keeping the sheet’s EDITORS value (the Instructions - Links row sits above Key, so the CFG, COLS and DATA rows land below EDITORS), and for drafting the TOC rows into the TOC tab from A1. The connector writes values, not colours, so the agent also colours Config: the Key row a Grey header (#b7b7b7, bold), EDITORS Orange (#f4b26b), and CFG, COLS, DATA and their continuation rows Grey (#efefef), and fits the Instructions rows’ heights to their text (a Sheets API autoResizeDimensions; an inserted row otherwise inherits its neighbour’s height). Every refresh re-applies these (styleConfig), so a sheet the script runs in heals on its own. The TOC rows are exactly what the script’s refresh writes, so the dropdown works before anyone pastes the script. | The agent says what is left for a person: paste Code.gs and run installTriggers (step 5 above), and tick Allow multiple selections (step 6). | . When the branch carrying the folio is not merged yet, the agent may run steps 1 and 3 from that branch without pushing to it, and write the sheet; the branch’s owner commits the anchors and sheet-sync.json. Re-run step 3 after any structural change to the document (a section added, moved or renamed). Who may set the Ready columns: the EDITORS row. Everyone who works in a log is shared as Editor; protected ranges decide what each can change. Blue columns are open to all of them. The orange Ready for agent and Ready for merge columns are for editors only, and the owner names them in the Config tab’s EDITORS row, column B: plain emails, no names, one per line (Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter starts a line inside a cell), or separated by commas or semicolons. The format is spelled out, with an example, in the Instructions - Editors row and in a note on the cell itself. Anything that is not an email is left out, and the refresh names it in a toast. installTriggers and Folio Assistant > Refresh now lock each Ready for ... column to the owner plus those emails, under a protection the script owns and rebuilds each time (other protections are left alone). An empty row locks them to the owner alone, which is how every new sheet starts; a Config with no EDITORS row leaves them as they are. Both templates carry the Orange EDITORS row, empty. EDITORS is the one Config row a person keeps: the agent writes it empty and keeps the sheet’s value whenever it rewrites the tab, and the emails never go into sheet-sync.json, which is committed. To delegate who decides, the owner can add a delegate to the Config tab’s protection, or send the agent the list. The Instructions rows. Every visible tab opens with an Instructions row that says what that tab is for and how it works, in that tab’s own terms; tabInstructions() in the builder writes the text for each tab. On a people’s tab (RPC, RCS, Contributor Feedback) the row is frozen with the header and grey like it, a lighter grey than the header. Its first line is the colour key: Column colours: then one phrase per colour, in the order Blue, Green, Orange, Grey, worded for the mode by colourKey() and naming no colour (§”Sheet conventions”): . | Blue: input by people, named by their process role: the Feedback Review Committee in public-comment mode, the Authoring Committee in drafting mode; | Green: the agent; | Orange: an Editor (the Ready for ... columns); | Grey: the script. | . Then come the steps for that tab, one per line, naming columns, never colours. On a change-set tab they are the human-to-agent workflow, worded by process role: people write their feedback, the agent proposes, an Editor sets Ready for agent, the agent opens one pull request for the row whose Staging review opens the changes, new feedback marks the proposal stale, a second reviewer checks the dispositions and the QA report, and an Editor sets Ready for merge and the agent merges. On Review Public Comments the steps say that decisions are made per change set. Last come the filter views, and a link to the harness’s page for the process the sheet runs: public-comment.html for public comment and contributor-feedback.html for drafting, under en/cat-harness/processes/ on the folio-assistant site (processPage(); CFG.PROCESS overrides it). The first cell reads Instructions, and the text is one merged cell across the rest of the row. The script reads any leading rows whose first cell starts Instructions (or Colour key) as for people: the header is the row after them, and every write, lock and edit range starts below the header. Insert the row only after the sheet runs a Code.gs that knows it; an older script reads the legend as the header and finds no columns. Filter views and protections start at the header row, so shift them down by one row when the row is inserted. A filter view’s custom formula does not move when a column is inserted, so rewrite it. The Config tab keeps its Instructions short, one subject per row, so no row is taller than the window: Instructions (the tab’s purpose: nothing here needs you unless you install the script), Instructions - Install script (setupSteps(): copy Code.gs, Extensions > Apps Script, name the project after the spreadsheet, paste and save, run installTriggers, allow it, reload), on a drafting sheet Instructions - Dropdown (dropdownSteps()), and Instructions - Editors (editorSteps()), then the Key | Value header. Its rows are not frozen. The EDITORS row is Orange, like the Ready columns it controls, because a person keeps it; the rows the agent writes stay grey. The script reads Config keys by name, so it ignores these rows. A stale proposal hands control back to an Editor. When a row’s proposal turns stale (a blue cell changed since the agent wrote it), the script sets that row’s Ready for agent from Yes to No, once, on the turn. The agent does not act on the row until an Editor sets Yes again, which is the signal to update the row’s pull request. A Yes set while the row is still stale stays. One row, one branch, one active pull request. A change-set row keeps one branch for its whole life, and at most one pull request is open on it. Every later agent run pushes to that branch and updates that PR, so the row’s Staging review link stays the same. If the PR is closed and the committee or contributors want the work back, the agent reopens it, or opens a new PR on the same branch when it cannot be reopened. It never starts a second branch for the row. Each earlier PR stays listed in the row’s Agentic status, one line per PR. Filter views. Each template carries saved filter views, which copy with it. Use Data > Filter views, never a plain filter: a plain filter changes the view for everyone, a filter view only for whoever opens it. Each view is named for who uses it and what it shows. | sheet | view | who | shows | . | drafting: Contributor Feedback | Open | everyone | rows with a Title, Ready for merge not Yes | . |   | Needs contributor feedback | contributors | rows with a Title and every Contributor Feedback column empty | . |   | Waiting for editor (Ready for agent not Yes) | editors | rows with a Title, Ready for agent not Yes | . |   | Merge decision due (PR open, not merged) | editors | Agentic status (filter) is PR open, Ready for merge not Yes | . |   | Needs you (answer the agent’s question) | editors, owner | Agentic status (filter) starts with “Needs you” | . |   | Stale (agent proposal or staging out of date) | owner | the agent proposal starts with ⚠, or the staging link says stale | . |   | Decided (Ready for merge Yes) | everyone | Ready for merge is Yes | . |   | By agentic status (pick values) | everyone | every row; pick values in the Agentic status (filter) column’s filter (a plain copy of the change set’s Agent status) | . | public comment: Review Change Sets | Change sets: the same eight | as above | on its own columns; “Needs architect feedback” checks the three Committee Feedback (initials) columns | . | public comment: Review Public Comments | Comments: Open (no Disposition) | everyone | a No., Disposition empty | . |   | Comments: No change set yet | review coordinator | a No., Change Set empty | . |   | Comments: Needs architect feedback | the Feedback Review Committee | a No., every Committee Feedback (initials) column empty | . |   | Comments: Decided (Disposition set) | everyone | Disposition filled | . The “needs feedback” and “stale” views use a custom formula that names columns by letter, so a column move breaks them: after moving columns, the agent checks each view’s formula against the headers. A filter view covers the rows the tab had when the view was made; when rows are added past that, widen its range (Data > Filter views > the view > Options > Update range). Keeping the section list current (agent). The dropdown’s list is the hidden TOC tab, and the script writes it from DATA.TOC in the Config tab on every refresh. So when the document’s chapters or sections change (any PR that changes review-anchors.json, the same moment review:anchors runs), the agent rebuilds the Config rows (--config review/drafting/sheet-sync.json --out config-rows.json) and writes them into each drafting sheet the folio names, in the same change. Nobody edits the TOC tab by hand. How picks stay valid. On each refresh the script repairs Selected Sections before anything else: . | the pick | what the script does | . | a current section, with or without its indent (or a “└ “ mark) | rewrites it to the dropdown’s name, indent included | . | a section renamed or renumbered since it was picked | finds it by its anchor (the TOC tab’s column C keeps the anchors of the names it offered before) and rewrites it to the new name | . | a section no longer in the document | keeps it, so nothing a person chose is lost, and adds a line in Section links: ⚠ “" is not in the document now: pick its section again | . So “Invalid” after a document change clears by itself at the next refresh, except for a section that was removed, which a person repicks. Change-set ids. Any row a person has filled in gets the next CS-nnn at the next refresh, whichever column they started in. A cell holding only “No” (a Yes/No dropdown’s default) and the script’s own columns do not count. Selected Sections shows “Invalid”. Three causes: a pick of a section removed from the document (Section links flags it; pick again); a cell with several sections where the rule does not allow multiple selections (tick it, step 6); or a cell that carries links. Sections must be plain text, the links belong in Section links: clear the cell’s formatting (Format > Clear formatting) and the script keeps it plain. Check it. Folio Assistant > Refresh now. In drafting mode a filled-in row gets a CS id and its picked sections appear, linked, in Section links; in public-comment mode each No. becomes a link. An error names what is missing: no Config tab, a Config row, or a tab the Config names. | mode | template (owned by informatics.avengers) | make a copy | . | public-comment | Folio Assistant - Public Comment Review Template, 14PtLd2U_tBQV5OHoEEVRJK1EKfsbZEBPP_MIqo2E3o4 | https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/14PtLd2U_tBQV5OHoEEVRJK1EKfsbZEBPP_MIqo2E3o4/copy | . | drafting | Folio Assistant - Contributor Template, 1PtcNJgLQIA1BjapU51pAQzqQjGylBHYNKlCPzZkwVag | https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1PtcNJgLQIA1BjapU51pAQzqQjGylBHYNKlCPzZkwVag/copy | . A copy keeps tabs, colours, dropdowns and formulas. It does not keep protected ranges (re-add them: Agent whole tab; the grey and green columns), and its TOC tab is empty until the script’s first refresh. A document’s own sheet is named in its sheet-sync.json as sheet (the spreadsheet id), so the agent’s sync knows where to read and write.

667d8815335b.title: Processes that run this skill
667d8815335b.content: | process | step(s) that name it | . | Contributor feedback on a working draft | Start a change-set row; Propose a direction; Set Ready for agent to Yes; Edit the document in the row’s pull request; Review the preview and answer; QA-review the dispositions; Set Ready for merge to Yes; Merge the pull request | . | Review and publish a folio | Contributor feedback (calls a sub-process) | . | Release a draft for public comment | Set up the comment channels, with instructions and links | . | Review-log watch | Agent pass on the changed rows (calls a sub-process) | .

842242ab8cfd.content: This skill holds no rules of its own. The review skills live in cat-harness (and one in core); each rule below belongs to the skill it names, and that skill is the one to read and change.

0cab640d12d9.doc: Review: a pointer to the review skills
0cab640d12d9.title: The skills, in the order a review uses them
0cab640d12d9.content: | step | question it answers | skill | lives in | . | 1. What changed | Which blocks did this edit-set add, change, move or remove? | staging-review | cat-harness | . | 2. Where to look first | Which sections changed most, have open comments, and are failing or stale on QA? | review-heatmap | cat-harness | . | 3. What it looks like | Before/after pictures of a rendered change, and a measured count | before-after-preview, visual-diff | cat-harness | . | 4. Saying something | How a reviewer comments on a block, and how the comment follows a renamed block | review-comments | core | . | 5. The gate | Who reviews, and what passing means: Technical Officer first pass, Clinical SME clinical sign-off, Content Reviewer approval | content-review | cat-harness | . The data these skills read is core’s content vocabulary, which is why the pointer sits here: . | the ChangeSet, schemas/changeset.ts | review comments, schemas/review-comment.ts | reviewer verdicts and coverage, schemas/review-verdict.ts | .

fc4ef27ab224.doc: Review: a pointer to the review skills
fc4ef27ab224.title: Why the steps go in this order
fc4ef27ab224.content: A large document is reviewed diff-first: start from what changed (step 1), and let the heat map (step 2) say which slice of it deserves a person’s time. Reading a 300-page handbook front to back spends the same attention on an unchanged appendix as on a rewritten recommendation. The heat map’s coverage column measures how far that slicing got. Its meaning, and what it must not be read as, is in review-heatmap, not here.

0d5017330645.title: What is not here yet
