56fe2ee55e18.title: Technical documentation
56fe2ee55e18.content: The register is an SDO’s — W3C, IHE. The reader is an implementer who was not in the room and will not have had the discussion that produced the document. The voice is the enforceable half. The technical-writer voice profile addressing the role carries the machine-checkable rules citing the ingested RFCs and this skill. It applies to DRAFTING and to REVIEW QA. This skill is how a person runs it; the voice profile (which points down at this skill) is what a checker reads.

312e0ab3ebb4.title: Requirement levels are RFC 2119’s, and only in UPPERCASE
312e0ab3ebb4.content: The key words are MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED, MAY and OPTIONAL. RFC 8174 is the constraint that makes them usable: only all-capitals usage carries the defined meaning. So the parser must handle this is narration and the parser MUST handle this is a conformance requirement, and a reader can tell which is which without asking. A writer who meant a requirement MUST capitalise it; a reviewer reads lowercase must as prose. Use them sparingly. RFC 2119 constrains its own key words to what is actually required for interoperation, or to limit behaviour that can cause harm — explicitly NOT to impose a preferred method. A MUST in every paragraph makes the real requirements unfindable. State what departing costs. RFC 2119 asks authors to elaborate the implications of not following a requirement, because most implementers lack the experience that produced it. A SHOULD whose cost is unstated is an instruction the reader cannot weigh, and the commonest reason a correct instruction is ignored. Both RFCs are ingested — library/content/rfc2119-key-words-requirement-levels/ and library/content/rfc8174-uppercase-vs-lowercase-2119-key-words/. Quote them from there, not from memory.

4e6422d1d374.title: Check whether the specification has been superseded
4e6422d1d374.content: Before citing an ingested specification, check whether a later one updates it, and ASK the owner whether they want it. RFC 2119’s own first page says “This RFC was updated, see RFC 8174”, and that update is the UPPERCASE rule above. A voice built from RFC 2119 alone would be internally consistent and superseded, which is the error hardest to notice. Read the front matter for Updated by, Obsoleted by, Superseded, an errata note or a later edition. Where one exists, say so and ask; do not silently cite the older document, and do not fetch the newer one uninvited.

d1e3720bb1e9.title: Three questions for a first draft
d1e3720bb1e9.content: Run these on your own draft, before review: each is cheapest while the draft is still yours. | Have I repeated anything? If so, consolidate: the same fact in two places is free to drift, and the copy a reader finds first is usually the one with no test behind it. | Does the content flow in logical order? If not, apply the detangler (graph-detanglement) rather than reordering by taste — a candidate ordering is MEASURED, not chosen. | Is this Term defined? If not: is it defined later; is it in the Glossary; does it need a Glossary entry? A term used once and nowhere else does not earn one. Glossary Terms are Capitalized on every use, so a reader can tell a defined Term from the same word used loosely. | .

7ae036fedaab.title: Reference a schema by linking to it
7ae036fedaab.content: When the prose names a schema, link to the schema source and to its UML documentation where one exists, because a reader left to guess the file guesses wrong exactly when the schema has moved. Resolve the reference, do not compose it: writing schemas/foo.ts in prose composes a path, while a link resolves one, and a broken link is a finding a checker can raise.

f178cf4fcd3a.title: Documentation and skills share content
f178cf4fcd3a.content: Where a skill states a rule correctly, docs/ SHOULD point at the skill rather than restate it; where they disagree, the skill wins. The skill carries the discipline; docs/ carries what a reader needs to find it and why it exists.

2da5fed4031a.title: What this skill does not cover
2da5fed4031a.content: Glossary mechanics — the content kind, its coding and versioning — belong to the glossary content kind and to the content layer’s glossary-build skill. Model-specific voices are the voice profiles’ own. This skill governs the WRITING; those govern the artefacts it writes about.

5cc04a5e0e2f.title: Technical documentation
5cc04a5e0e2f.content: Generated from cat-harness/skills/authoring/authoring-core/technical-documentation.md — do not edit here. ✎ Edit this page’s source .

37084e725373.title: Term disagreement — the extractor and the terminology disagree
37084e725373.content: Skill id: term-disagreement · Package: library-core . The outcome schema is schemas/content/term-adjudication.ts (folio-term-adjudications/v1). That file holds the table of what each outcome writes, as data. This skill says when to use it and how to choose.

ed0fe5007b6c.title: Two disagreements, kept apart
ed0fe5007b6c.content: . | The extractor and the terminology disagree. This skill. It is a CONTENT decision: what the corpus should say. | Two judges disagree about a mapping. That includes a person who thinks an automated match is wrong. It is adjudication plus untainted-verification, and it is not built; it waits until something maps. Do not answer it with an outcome from this skill: vocabulary-wrong says a vocabulary does not serve a domain, not that one match is mistaken. | .

91dd6c41e09e.title: Which rows are disagreements
91dd6c41e09e.content: check:term-mapping reports each candidate on each target as an exact / concept pair. Only two determined pairs are disagreements: . | exact | concept | reading | a decision? | . | mapped | mapped | the label IS the authorised one | no: agreement | . | unmapped | mapped | the right concept, under a label that is not its authorised one | yes, always | . | unmapped | unmapped | the authority carries no such label | only if the authority is MEANT to cover this | . | undetermined | — | nobody answered | no. Fix the reachability; the schema refuses it | . The third row is the one to be careful with. Almost every candidate is unmapped on both targets, because most are names for this repository’s own assets: skills, Tool nodes, BPMN activities, schema fields. No authority is expected to carry them, so they are not disagreements. They are terms this corpus is right to coin. The test for the third row: would a reader in this domain expect the consulted vocabulary to have a word for this? “Wombat sorter” against WHO SMART base: no, so there is no record. “Immunization” against WHO SMART base: yes. A miss there is a disagreement worth a decision. Never generate records in bulk. One record is one decision somebody took. The rule is the same as for work items, which are not sidecars: a machine-written queue of thousands of “undecided” rows would bury the few decisions that matter. Rows with no decision simply have no record.

b52c3736eb88.title: Choosing the outcome
b52c3736eb88.content: Ask in order. The first “yes” decides. | Does the authority’s concept mean exactly what the corpus means? Then the corpus should use the authority’s word: change-prose. This is the usual answer to a concept-only match. | Is the corpus’s sense real, but narrower, broader or merely related? Keep a word of our own and say how it relates: local-term, with a relation of closeMatch, broadMatch or narrowMatch. These are the predicates an authored term can carry. Use none when nothing in the authority is close. exactMatch is refused: if the concept IS ours, the answer was (1). | Is the vocabulary itself the wrong authority for this domain? For example, a clinical IG consulted for agent-tooling words. Record it: vocabulary-wrong, naming the vocabulary and the domain. Nothing in the corpus changes. | . If none fits, there is no decision yet. Leave no record, and say so where the work is tracked.

4e8d1b2df788.title: What each outcome writes, and where
4e8d1b2df788.content: The table is OUTCOME_WRITES in the schema. In short: . | outcome | writes | where | afterwards | . | change-prose | the authorised label | the source asset the extractor read, listed in changed | re-extraction mints that label, and the check reports exact: mapped | . | local-term | an authored term, with the reason | an authored glossary (localTerm.glossary) | the candidate is promoted (glossary-terms); its mapping to the authority is a person’s | . | vocabulary-wrong | nothing in the corpus | the record itself | the check keeps reporting the miss, and the record says why it is not acted on | . Every outcome also writes the record: one entry in a *.term-adjudications.json file beside the glossary schemes, with the subject (scheme, term, target, and the pair the check observed), who decided, when, and a ref to where it was discussed.

363dd5519c2e.title: Who decides
363dd5519c2e.content: A person. An agent may find a disagreement, propose an outcome and draft the record. Choosing between “our word” and “their word” is a content decision, so decidedBy names the person who took it. Put the proposal to them in the form of interaction-modality §4.1: the candidate, the concept it reached and by which label, the three outcomes, and the one you recommend.

f22454f74509.title: Automated matches and confirmed ones
f22454f74509.content: Each scheme’s SKOS JSON-LD publishes what the check found: skos:exactMatch for an exact match and skos:closeMatch for a concept-only one. They sit in a named graph (<scheme>/_automated-matches) whose PROV says a program produced it (see toSkos in the content core’s schemas/glossary.ts). The default graph holds only what people wrote. That is why local-term is the one route to a CONFIRMED mapping. The authored term’s own exactMatch / closeMatch / broadMatch / narrowMatch is published in the default graph. change-prose makes the label agree, but the candidate’s match stays automated until somebody authors it.

3c85377a03b9.title: Checking the record
3c85377a03b9.content: bun run cat check:term-mapping validates every *.term-adjudications.json and fails on one that does not satisfy the schema. It then sets each record against what it found: . | status | meaning | . | applied | change-prose / local-term took effect: the candidate maps exactly, or is gone | . | pending | decided, but the check still reports what it reported then | . | holds | vocabulary-wrong, and the miss it explains is still there | . | stale | the check now reports something the decision was not taken against. Look again | . stale is reported, never fatal. A decision taken against a state that has moved is still a decision, and it has become a question to look at again.

620b17e053c6.title: Not here
620b17e053c6.content: . | Two judges, one mapping: adjudication and untainted-verification, once something maps. | Which vocabulary is authoritative for which fact: vocabulary-authority. | How a term is authored: glossary-terms. | .

1a96e1795245.title: terminology-management
1a96e1795245.content: Skill id: terminology-management · Package: fhir-ig-authoring · Named by the calling layer’s authoring process, in its Terminologist lane. Bind a DAK’s data elements to standard terminologies, and manage the value sets and concept maps that result. Sourcing. ICD-11, SNOMED CT and LOINC are external code systems with their own licences, release cycles and editorial rules; FHIR’s terminology layer is HL7’s. This skill states how binding is worked in this harness and defers to those authorities for the semantics. Which code to choose for a given concept is the terminologist’s judgement, not this skill’s.

c41ca7e008ef.title: Inputs and outputs
c41ca7e008ef.content: fhir-harness/schemas/skills/terminology-management/: . | in — operation (required), targetStandard, inputFile | out — resources (required), unmappedConcepts | . unmappedConcepts is the important output. A binding pass that maps everything is either a small dictionary or a pass that guessed. Concepts with no defensible code are a normal result, and reporting them is what lets the clinical SME see where the DAK is asserting a local meaning.

c961282f1a7f.title: Why this has its own lane
c961282f1a7f.content: The authoring process gives the terminologist a lane of their own because a wrong binding is invisible downstream: a data element bound to a plausible-but-wrong code compiles, validates, publishes, and is wrong in every derived artefact. The person who chooses codes is not the person under pressure to finish the dictionary. The terminologist role carries this skill and clinical-sme does not: they are different judgements. A clinician rules on whether the concept is right; the terminologist rules on whether the code denotes it.

21a56f9293f2.title: Do not invent a code
21a56f9293f2.content: If no code in the target standard denotes the concept, the answer is unmappedConcepts, not the nearest neighbour. A “close enough” binding changes what the data element means, and cannot be recovered once downstream systems have consumed it.

c6c3b671aaef.title: Tooling
c6c3b671aaef.content: The extractors and generators that read a source dictionary and write vocabularies and schemas belong to the layer whose model they read; its own tooling skill says how to load them. An absent toolchain degrades this skill to skip, never to a clean run. Validation of the resulting artefacts is fhir-validation, not this skill.

7d2d42c84abb.doc: Test Data Sets & SME Case/Verdict Review
7d2d42c84abb.title: Test Data Sets & SME Case/Verdict Review
7d2d42c84abb.content: Governs how test data sets are authored, discriminated, specialized per content type, and reviewed by a subject-matter expert (SME) before a test-plan/v1 binds them into test-plan-execution.

01d9762b0a53.doc: Test Data Sets & SME Case/Verdict Review
01d9762b0a53.title: Two kinds of test data, two declared graph directories
01d9762b0a53.content: Fixed and generated test data sets do not have the same provenance or audit standing, so they live in separately declared graph directories (test-data-fixed vs test-data-generated in schemas/kg/graph-typology-registry.ts) and carry self-identifying $schema and kind tags in schemas/sdlc/test-data.ts: . | Kind | Graph typology | $schema tag | Discriminator | What is stored | Audit standing | . | Fixed | test-data-fixed | test-data-fixed/1.0.0 | kind: "fixed" | Committed records, optional citations, optional SME review sign-off | Usable as certification evidence (isEvidence in schemas/sdlc/test-plan.ts) once review is present | . | Generated | test-data-generated | test-data-generated/1.0.0 | kind: "generated" | Recipe only: contentType, specialisation, template, params, seed, and canonical sha256 | Never stored materialised; synthesised at run time and hashed into folio-test-run/v1 | . Discriminate from the file content, never from the path . A consumer reading a test data node must call discriminateTestDataSet(doc) in schemas/sdlc/test-data.ts, which inspects $schema and kind inside the JSON document rather than inferring the kind from the directory path: . | FixedTestDataSetSchema is .strict() and refuses recipe fields (template, params, seed, sha256). | GeneratedTestDataSetSchema is .strict() and refuses materialised payload fields (records, cases, path, review), and verifies that sha256 equals computeGeneratedSetDigest({ contentType, specialisation, template, params, seed }). | .

bbf3fe2b8739.doc: Test Data Sets & SME Case/Verdict Review
bbf3fe2b8739.title: General curation process and per-content-type specialisation
bbf3fe2b8739.content: The general curation process is sdlc/processes/test-data-curation.bpmn (Process_TestDataCuration): . | Classify the data set (Task_ClassifySet, GW_SetKind) — decide whether the test case needs a small curated fixed set (audit evidence for domain logic) or a deterministic generated recipe (scale, boundary, or combinatorial coverage). | Fixed branch (Task_CurateFixed, GW_NeedsSmeReview, Call_SmeReview) — author the test-data-fixed/1.0.0 node under the instance’s declared test-data-fixed directory; if the set exercises decision support or an indicator definition, invoke sdlc/processes/sme-test-data-review.bpmn (Process_SmeTestDataReview). | Generated branch (Call_ContentTypeSpecialisation, Task_WriteRecipe) — invoke the content-type specialisation as a called subprocess (Call_ContentTypeSpecialisation), then write the test-data-generated/1.0.0 recipe and its canonical sha256 under the instance’s declared test-data-generated directory without committing materialised records. | Verify self-identification and bind (Task_VerifySelfIdentifying) — verify via discriminateTestDataSet and toTestDataRef that the file self-identifies by $schema and kind and bind its digest into the test-plan/v1 case. | . FHIR templating is one specialisation, named as such, not the design . Call_ContentTypeSpecialisation in test-data-curation.bpmn is parameterized by contentType and specialisation (TestDataSpecialisationSchema in schemas/sdlc/test-data.ts): . | fhir-templating (FHIR_TEMPLATING_SPECIALISATION) is one named specialisation for FHIR IG / DAK content (for example, Liquid or FSH/JSON templates producing synthetic patient bundles or MeasureReport cohorts). | Other content types supply their own specialisations — such as markdown-fixture for document folios, lean-counterexample for formal-proof folios, or tabular-cohort for aggregate indicator tables. | Platform schemas and processes never hardcode FHIR resources or DAK structures as the general test-data model. | .

a99565a65123.doc: Test Data Sets & SME Case/Verdict Review
a99565a65123.title: SME review of decision support and indicator definitions
a99565a65123.content: When a fixed test data set tests clinical or scientific decision support or indicator definitions, passing is a domain judgement: a subject-matter expert must confirm that the logic produces the right guidance on a worked case or the right value on a cohort. Two units of review in sme-case-verdict/1.0.0 . SmeCaseVerdictKind ($schema: "sme-case-verdict/1.0.0", graph typology sme-case-verdict) discriminates on subjectKind: . | subjectKind: "decision-support" — unit is a worked case (case): . | id, summary, decisionLogicRef, structured input, systemOutput, and optional expectedGuidance. | Refuses cohort. | . | subjectKind: "indicator-definition" — unit is a cohort plus an expected value (cohort): . | id, summary, indicatorRef, populationSize, inputs, expectedValue, computedValue, and optional period, numerator, denominator. | Refuses case. | . | . Attributable SME identity and review date . An audited review without an attributable reviewer and date is not audited. Every sme-case-verdict/1.0.0 node requires: . | reviewer (SmeReviewerIdentitySchema): kind: "human" (never "agent" or "script"), provider (e.g. "github", "orcid"), handle, role (e.g. "clinical-sme"), and optional displayName and actor. | reviewedAt (ReviewedAtSchema): ISO-8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) or timestamp. | verdict: "pass" | "fail" | "needs-revision", plus a non-empty domain rationale. | . Why the SME lane in sme-test-data-review.bpmn is judgementOnly . In sdlc/processes/sme-test-data-review.bpmn (Process_SmeTestDataReview), the SME review step (Task_SmeJudge) sits in Lane_SME, bound to role clinical-sme (partitionElementRef="clinical-sme"). In scenarios/roles.json, clinical-sme declares "judgementOnly": true and carries no procedural skill on Task_SmeJudge: no procedure yields the clinical or scientific answer, which is the whole reason a person is in the lane. The preparation steps (Task_PrepareWorkedCase, Task_PrepareCohort) and the recording step (Task_RecordCaseVerdict) are mechanical and name test-data-sets; the judgement between them is the human SME’s alone.

e578ab07ce28.title: Role
e578ab07ce28.content: Write and maintain unit tests for the content-authoring pipeline. Tests are TypeScript using Bun’s built-in test runner (bun:test).

bf95ba75c7f7.title: Test infrastructure
bf95ba75c7f7.content: | Path | Purpose | . | scripts/tests/*.test.ts | Test files (bun discovers *.test.ts) | . | scripts/tests/helpers.ts | Shared helpers: paths, project discovery, parsing | . | scripts/tests/report.ts | Test report generator (outputs TestReport JSON) | . | scripts/tests/run-tests.sh | Shell entry point (delegates to bun test) | . | schemas/formalization-types.ts | TypeScript types for test definitions, results, reports, coverage | . | content/schema/ | Content-object types, Zod schemas, builder functions | . | pipeline/validate.ts | Content validation pipeline (schema + constraints + AST) | . | pipeline/render.ts | Block → output rendering + AST validation | . | pipeline/build.ts | Full document build from content objects | .

af9e4a22f119.title: Dependency graph for scoped testing
af9e4a22f119.content: Use the content uses[] fields (and any formalization-import graph) to scope test runs: . | Identify changed blocks — which .ts/.md files were modified | Trace downstream dependents — via uses[] in content objects | Run targeted tests — only validate/build the changed block + its dependents | Report impact — show how many blocks are affected by a change | . The dependency graph comes from: . | uses[] field in content .ts manifests (narrative dependency) | any formalization import statements (formal-layer dependency) | dependency-graph.svg generated by CI | .

be946621fca2.title: When to write a test
be946621fca2.content: . | A bug was found — write a regression test before fixing. | A new script or config file is added — test its contract. | A rendering macro is changed — test extraction still works. | A new formal-layer project is added — auto-discovered, but verify. | A review skill detects a potential error — it will ask the user whether to write a test. If yes, this skill writes it. | .

c397d57ad2be.title: How to write a test
c397d57ad2be.content: // In scripts/tests/<suite>.test.ts import { describe, test, expect } from "bun:test"; import { REPO_ROOT, ... } from "./helpers"; describe("Feature under test", () => { test("specific behavior", () => { // Arrange // Act // Assert expect(result).toBe(expected); }); }); . Conventions . | One test file per concern: create new files for new concerns. | Use helpers.ts: Don’t hardcode paths or re-implement discovery. | Informational vs. blocking: Tests that report data quality (coverage gaps, label mismatches) should log and pass. Tests that verify contracts (JSON validity, required fields, file existence) should fail. | Comment the failure point: Each test should document what bug or failure it prevents. | Types from schemas/formalization-types.ts: Use TestResult, TestReport, CoverageEntry etc. when generating structured output. | . A test never reads test/results/ as a fixture . Derived QA results live on the orphan qa-reports branch: the checkout’s <instance>/test/results/** is an ignored working copy, and the record is the commit-keyed entry qa-publish stores. A test that reads that tree reads a file that may not be there: it fails when the corpus is absent, or worse, passes by iterating over zero files. | Build the fixture, or run the producer in-process over one, and assert on what it computed. A verdict is not a fixture: the corpus is supposed to change (see qa-witness). | If a test must read a stored result, read it through qa-store (readQa) and treat miss, corrupt and unknown as states to assert, never as an empty pass. | A loop over a corpus needs a “there are some” guard beside it, or it is green over nothing. | Never write into test/attestations/ from a test. It is the judgement store on main; a test that needs one builds it in a temporary root. | . Adding a new formal-layer project . When a new formal-layer library is added to the build manifest: . | discoverProjects() in helpers.ts auto-discovers it | the project test suite automatically tests it (directory, files, audits) | No manual test registration needed | . Test categories (from TestCategory type) . | Category | What it tests | . | formal-compile | formal-layer files exist, have imports, are non-empty | . | formal-library | toolchain, build manifest, dependencies declared | . | formal-gap | unproved-gap count per project/file | . | render-coverage | render tags resolve, statement coverage, consistency | . | doc-structure | labels, cross-refs, environments | . | schema-validity | JSON manifests match their schemas | . | infrastructure | server config, scripts, deploy, .gitignore | . | content-validation | content objects pass Zod + constraint + AST checks | . Content-object tests . Test content objects using the validation pipeline: . import { validateObjects } from "../../pipeline/validate"; describe("Content objects", () => { test("all objects pass schema validation", async () => { const result = await validateObjects("content/<paper>/<section>/"); const errors = result.issues.filter(i => i.level === "error"); expect(errors).toHaveLength(0); }); test("rendered output passes AST validation", async () => { // The validation pipeline includes AST checks automatically const result = await validateObjects("content/<paper>/<section>/"); expect(result.valid).toBe(true); }); }); .

799af3e295e9.title: Running a test plan — from a request to a signed certification
799af3e295e9.content: Skill id: test-plan-execution · Package: sdlc-core · Process: test-plan-execution.bpmn · Decision: test-certification.dmn . A system is tested against a plan, by somebody who is not the system, and certified by somebody who did not run the test. Everything below is that sentence made operational. This skill is the PROCESS. How to write a test is test-engineer; how a folio’s content is tested is content-test; why the checker sees only a controlled context is untainted-verification; how a signature is routed by reach is qa-report-signing. Read those for their halves — this one does not restate them.

b7bbee717b84.title: The nodes, and who points at whom
b7bbee717b84.content: | node | schema | where it lives | . | the plan | test-plan/v1 — schemas/sdlc/test-plan.ts | authored content (test-plan kind) | . | the system under test | the systemUnderTest facet on an actor — schemas/kg/skill-package.ts | scenarios/actors/*.json | . | the run | folio-test-run/v1 with plan + sut — schemas/sdlc/test-run.ts | the declared qa directory | . | the report | test-report/v1 — schemas/sdlc/test-report.ts | the qa-reports branch, tests/<plan>/<sut>/<run>/ | . | the certification | a judgement, qa-attestations/v1 | the declared attestations graph, on main | . The run points at the plan; the plan names no run. A plan is reused across runs and systems, so a back-pointer would turn authored content into live state. Same direction for the report → run and the certification → report. The platform model is FHIR-free. FHIR R5 TestPlan informed test-plan/v1 and is a DOWNSTREAM export target, in the FHIR IG layer. Never read a FHIR TestPlan as the source of a plan here.

e940cdd67ff3.title: The system under test is a facet, not a role
e940cdd67ff3.content: Being tested is not a lane anybody takes on. An actor that can be executed — agent or system, never a person or an external — declares: . // an illustration, not a declared actor { "id": "example-mcp-tool", "kind": "system", "reach": "internet", "systemUnderTest": { "kind": "tool", "version": "0.1.0" } } . kind is the closed list SUT_KINDS (skill, agent, tool, machine, ig, process) — the same vocabulary as a plan’s scope.kind, so the two are compared, not translated. Reach is the actor’s own reach, read by sutRefFor; absent is unknown, never internet.

2c9e9b6d4e71.title: The five lanes
2c9e9b6d4e71.content: | lane | role | does | . | Requester / SUT | test-requester | asks for certification of system S against plan P, naming P’s id and version | . | Tester | tester | resolves P, binds its data, executes every case, writes the run and the report | . | Untainted checker | untainted-checker | re-executes a SAMPLE of cases, blind to the tester’s verdicts | . | Certifier | certifier | applies the plan’s exitCriteria table, then records the decision | . | Attestation service | attestation-service | signs, via qa-report-signing.bpmn, and files the certification | . The tester is untainted from the system under test. The SUT may request; it may never be the tester, the checker or the certifier, and it never writes a verdict about itself — test-report/v1 refuses a reviewer whose id or actor is the SUT’s actor, and test-sut-not-self-judged audits it. Tester . | Resolve the plan. P parses as test-plan/v1, names at least one req: requirement, its exitCriteria.decision resolves to a decision in a .dmn that exists, and its scope.kind matches the SUT actor’s facet kind. A plan that does not resolve is not run. | Bind the test data (test-data-sets). A fixed set is a committed path and is evidence only once reviewed (isEvidence). A generated set is a template + params + seed and is never materialised into the repository. Both feed the run’s data hash; runner, configuration and scenario bank feed its process hash, and the two bases must be disjoint (buildTestRun refuses otherwise). | Execute. Every case is executed, or recorded skipped with a reason. A case with no verdict at the end of a terminal run is a finding, not an omission (checkAgainstPlan). | Write the run and the report. The run records plan {id, version} and sut {actor, version, reach}; the report rolls up per plan, never across plans, and testReportPath says where it goes. | . Untainted checker . Re-executes a sample of the cases from the plan and the data alone — never the tester’s verdicts — and reports agree, disagree or unknown. It RULES ON NOTHING (untainted-verification rule 3): the comparison is a fact the certification table reads, not a verdict the checker writes. Certifier . The gateway is computed. Pass the facts; never assert the branch — the engine refuses a hand-supplied outcome on a DMN gateway. | fact | from | . | reportStatus | the report’s status | . | dataHashKnown | the run’s data.hash is not unknown | . | unexecutedCases | checkAgainstPlan(...).filter(kind === "unexecuted-case").length | . | checker | the untainted checker’s agree / disagree / unknown | . | failedCases | rollup.fail | . | passedCases | rollup.pass | . The table returns certified, refused or undetermined. undetermined is the third state — a running or aborted report, an unknown data hash, an unexecuted case, a checker that disagreed or could not run, or a report in which nothing passed. It is never rendered as certified, and it is not a refusal either: it says the evidence does not decide, so nothing is signed. The certification decision is a judgement. The table says whether the exit criteria are met; the certifier — a person, a specialisation of stakeholder — records the decision, and it lives with the other judgements under the declared attestations graph, never on the qa-reports branch with derived results. Attestation service . Call_Sign runs qa-report-signing.bpmn unchanged; its route (API or a human release authority) is chosen there by the signer’s reach. Then the signed certification is filed under attestations.

ad316c58a517.title: The four kg-audit criteria
ad316c58a517.content: Registered in KG_CRITERIA (schemas/sdlc/kg-qa.ts), implemented in scripts/test-plan-audit.ts, recorded on the graph roll-up: . | criterion | fails when | severity | . | test-plan-resolves | a plan does not parse, its exit DMN does not resolve, or a run/report names a plan, version or SUT that does not resolve (or a SUT whose facet kind is not the plan’s scope) | critical | . | test-case-executed-or-skipped | a terminal report leaves a plan case with no verdict, or names a case the plan lacks | major | . | test-data-hash-present | a plan-run’s data hash is unknown, or a report’s run carries none | major | . | test-sut-not-self-judged | any verdict’s reviewer is the system under test | critical | . Each records n/a when there is nothing of its kind to judge — no plan, no plan-run, no report — and never a pass over nothing.

84eb05077f27.title: Processes that run this skill
84eb05077f27.content: This skill has its own process: Test-plan execution. | process | step(s) that name it | . | Test-plan execution | Request certification of the system against plan P; Resolve the plan; Bind the test data; Execute every case, or skip it with a reason; Write the test run and the test report; Re-execute a sample, blind to the tester’s verdicts; Record the certification decision; Record the refusal, with the failing cases; Record why it could not be decided; File the signed certification | .

3e045f18c16e.title: Theme art intake
3e045f18c16e.content: Art arrives — three crops for a theme or an avatar — and the answer is either accepted, with the declaration written, or refused, with what to fix.

182644db63ff.title: This is a step in document ingestion, not a process beside it
182644db63ff.content: Document ingestion already answers the question art arrival poses — something unstructured has arrived; is it acceptable, and if not, why not — with a pipeline and a completeness gate. Theme art is the same event with a different payload, so what exists is a check keyed on the payload, not a second pipeline: a parallel “avatar ingestion” would be a second answer to one question, free to disagree with the first. |   | where | . | the check | schemas/library/theme-art-intake.ts — pure, no I/O, no clock | . | the CLI face | scripts/check-theme-art.ts, bun run cat check:theme-art | . | the arrival | uploads/, per content-acquisition and document-intake | .

9321a63a08d3.title: The constraints
9321a63a08d3.content: Each constraint answers a failure that has happened. Do not add one that has not: a rule with no failure behind it is one whose next maintainer cannot tell whether it still matters. | constraint | verdict | why | . | all three layouts | refuse | resolveThemeBackdrop refuses an incomplete backdrop wholesale, so a theme missing one crop renders with no art — not two thirds of it. | . | distinct content | refuse | two byte-identical files for two named layouts or avatars means one is missing. | . | orientation per layout | refuse | a portrait crop is not a landscape crop scaled down. The quiet area the sticky’s text sits in moves. | . | a declared destination | refuse | art outside a declared directory (at the repository root, say) is seen by no gate: check-declared-assets walks declared→disk. | . | dimensions measured | structural | intake takes bytes and emits the declaration, so there is nowhere for a retyped (or copied) number to enter. | . | weight and format | report | heavy PNGs still render, so refusing them would block work over a bandwidth judgement. | .

2ec2b547e889.title: Refuse, report, or neither
2ec2b547e889.content: . | Refuse when the art cannot do its job, or when intake cannot tell which of two readings is intended. A missing crop and two identical files are both “somebody has to decide something”. | Report when the art works but costs. Weight and format are the cases: a 1.6 MB PNG renders correctly. | Neither — say nothing — for anything intake did not actually measure. | . remedy is a required field on every failure: a refusal that says invalid teaches nobody what to fix. All failures are collected rather than thrown one at a time, because art arrives as a batch, and reporting the first problem of three means three round trips to learn three things.

034ad4ed7aef.title: Do not repair somebody’s art
034ad4ed7aef.content: deletion-requires-confirmation applies, and so does its spirit. When intake refuses, the outputs are the report and a work-plan item — not a re-crop, not a converted file, and not a quietly removed declaration. What looks like a missing crop may be a duplicate that was uploaded by mistake, and that is a question for the person who has the original. check:theme-art:check runs in CI, so a refusal of declared art is a regression.

bdc2a7543a5f.title: Reading the report
bdc2a7543a5f.content: ✓ landing-engineer: 3 layouts accepted · laptop 1672×941 docs/assets/img/harness/landing-engineer-laptop.png ! [heavy] laptop: … is 1560 KB, over the 391 KB budget → convert to webp — the measured gap on this art was about 16× ✗ landing-architecture: refused, 1 problem(s) · [missing-layout] mobile: no file offered for the mobile layout → supply all three layouts … . Three rules for reading it, the same three ci-health states: . | declared-but-absent is not a refusal and not a pass. The declaration names a file that is not on disk. It is reported on its own line because “the file is not there” and “the file is the wrong shape” are different facts, and a reader who cannot tell them apart fixes the wrong one. | A check that fires on every subject is wrong. docs/ is not a declared directory, and should not be — a declared entry names a graph, and the site is the render target — so art under it is not undeclared-destination. When a new check’s first run lights up broadly, ask which of these are correct? before how do I fix the repository?, and test any exclusion in both directions: a test of the excluded case alone passes equally for a check that never fires. A check that fires on legitimate subjects gets switched off, and a switched-off check still reads as coverage. | Warnings do not accumulate into a refusal. Twelve heavy files are twelve reports, not a failure. | .

4f9e16f252f3.title: Adding a constraint
4f9e16f252f3.content: . | Name the failure it answers. No failure, no constraint. | Decide refuse vs report by the line above — can the art do its job? | Write the remedy before the detection. If you cannot say what to do about it, the check is not ready. | Prove it fires, with a test that fails when the check is removed. | Check it against art already shipped. The aspect bands are deliberately wide because the shipped laptop crops run 1.50–1.78; a tighter band would refuse work that is fine. | . The stages of theming, and which owns which question, are in theming.

525b6fc5cc25.title: What is NOT here
525b6fc5cc25.content: The theming code — schemas/ui/themes.ts, schemas/library/theme-art-intake.ts, scripts/check-theme-art.ts, scripts/gen-themes-css.ts, scripts/gen-avatars-css.ts — stays where it is. This is the kg graph: the instructions an agent follows, not the implementation. A skill and the code it describes are different node kinds, and moving code beside its documentation would make the partition meaningless.

5f578839b2f1.title: Theme art intake
5f578839b2f1.content: Generated from cat-harness/skills/ui/theming/theme-art-intake.md — do not edit here. ✎ Edit this page’s source .

9374428df63c.title: Per-artefact specialisation
9374428df63c.content: This is level 3 of the axis, and it is deliberately the narrowest. The general rule lives in its stage — intake, declaration, generation, contrast — and an artefact carries only its difference. The avatar crop boxes are the worked example: the rule that a crop is declared data belongs to theme-declaration; the boxes themselves are navbar-avatar specialisation, and they are below.

0953feeaf63c.title: The surfaces
0953feeaf63c.content: | artefact | what differs | where | . | sticky | the container sizes to its CONTENT, so a text region would reimpose the geometry the sticky removes | schemas/content/landing-sticky.ts, .fa-sticky | . | landing board | text is composited INTO the art, so it needs textRegion per layout and a crop chosen by content shape | docs/_includes/landing.html | . | docs background | the page ground, not a card — a different CSS surface and probably a different crop set | not built | . | navbar avatar | the art CLIPPED to the subject in a square frame — avatarRegion | <name>.json, bun run cat avatar:crops | . | the mark | ONE geometry, TWO inks — a scheme pair, because one ink cannot clear 3:1 on both grounds | <name>.json mark + mark-dark, docs/assets/img/icons/ | .

a5aa86e9d201.title: Sticky: art backs it, text does not sit IN it
a5aa86e9d201.content: Most sticky-backing art carries no textRegion on purpose. A sticky is a container that sizes to its content; a region would fit the text into a cloud interior, which is the geometry the sticky exists to remove. The three landing-*.webp entries keep theirs because the composited landing path still uses them. A floating sticky keeps its theme.fa-sticky-floating’s opaque override is scoped to :not([data-fa-sticky-theme]), because the theme is a property of the sticky and not of the pinned state. That scoping is sound only while every theme surface is opaque, which is why theme-declaration carries the rule and themes.test.ts gates it.

950ebbfbe850.title: Landing board: the crop is chosen by CONTENT, then overridden by viewport
950ebbfbe850.content: The default crop is the one the sticky’s content wants — computed from how much text and how many links the card carries. The narrow-viewport <source>s stay on top of it: content decides the default and the viewport still overrides, which is the right precedence, because the viewport is a hard constraint and the content shape is a preference. <picture> swaps the FILE at 30rem and 48rem, so the card’s ratio and the cloud’s position must change at exactly those widths or the words land in the wrong part of the art. A media query cannot read which <source> won, so both sides are keyed to the same two numbers.

95e49cab88d9.title: Navbar avatar: the box is per-image and measured
95e49cab88d9.content: The avatar is the card art clipped to the cat’s head and torso, not the card scaled down. A whole 1:1 card in a 46px frame makes the cat about four pixels tall and every theme reads as grey mush. Measured off a 5–10% grid overlay of each card, as fractions x y w h: . | card | box | . | landing-card (grumpy-cat) | 0.00 0.46 0.50 0.50 | . | landing-library-card | 0.14 0.40 0.42 0.42 | . | landing-bootstrap-card | 0.27 0.615 0.24 0.24 | . | landing-operations-card | 0.17 0.475 0.27 0.27 | . | landing-engineer-card | 0.00 0.40 0.46 0.46 | . | landing-analyst-card | 0.05 0.48 0.36 0.36 | . | landing-architecture-card | 0.02 0.38 0.44 0.44 | . Only CARD crops carry one. The avatar is cut from the square crop; a box on the laptop or mobile art would be measured against a composition the frame never shows — and it would validate, because squareness is checkable and relevance is not. The schema cannot see whether a box frames the subject — a box can be square, in bounds, and still clip the head or sit on scenery. Render and look: . bun run cat avatar:crops # every declared box, drawn on the card and clipped bun run cat theme:sheet # every theme: palette, contrast, art, both regions .

075708271bd4.title: The page ground: the first paint is DARK
075708271bd4.content: The rule: the first frame of every published page is dark. A light page becomes light AFTER that, never the other way round, and a reader in dark mode never sees a light frame. A dark frame before light is a blink; a white frame before dark is a flashbulb in a dark room — the asymmetry is the whole reason for the default. What that takes, on any page that picks its scheme on the client: . | Decide the scheme before any stylesheet paints. An inline, render- blocking script in <head> sets data-fa-scheme on <html> from the reader’s stored choice (fa-color-scheme, the key docs-ui.js writes), else prefers-color-scheme, else dark. On the Jekyll site this is the fa-first-paint block at the top of _includes/head_custom.html, and it also switches the theme’s stylesheet while the head is still being parsed, so a light reader is light from the first frame too. | Paint html dark from the very first CSS (light only when the attribute says light). A page ground that nothing paints is the browser’s WHITE canvas whenever the theme’s sheet is missing — a slow CDN, or a swap. | Never swap a stylesheet the page is already painting with. jtd.setTheme(name) swaps just-the-docs’ first stylesheet, and a swap UNLOADS the sheet until the new file arrives, which flashes white. applyScheme in docs-ui.js asks jtdShows(name) first, so a stored choice that the page already shows swaps nothing. | . How it is held: the tools layer’s test/first-paint-scheme.e2e.ts lifts the shipped snippet out of head_custom.html, holds the deferred bundle, and reads html’s computed background before the bundle runs; it holds the dark sheet in flight to prove no swap happens; and it checks a stored light choice ends up light. A page you add that emits its own <head> is covered by the same spec’s “generated dashboards” block — add it there. Pages that switch nothing with script cannot flash, and do not need the snippet: the generated dashboards (state-visualizer.ts, gen-translation-status.ts) paint dark from their first CSS, and the viewers that follow @media (prefers-color-scheme) are decided by the browser before first paint. Do not give a dashboard the snippet as a tidy-up: it would switch ON data-fa-scheme="light" rules that are unfinished and fail axe contrast.

cf2155ca3376.title: Adding a surface
cf2155ca3376.content: . | Find the stage that owns the general rule and read it. | Add only the difference here. | If the surface renders art behind text, it inherits theme-contrast unchanged — a measured scrim, AAA over pure black. | If it renders art at all, render it and LOOK. | .

7bf5ebd7023f.title: The mark: one geometry, two inks, and the pair is a MEASUREMENT
7bf5ebd7023f.content: A mark is not a sticky backdrop — it is a small glyph that sits on the sidebar header, on the page, and in the browser’s tab strip. The rule that makes it different from every other artefact above: . One ink cannot clear 3:1 on both grounds. So a mark is a PAIR, and the second file exists because of a number rather than because somebody wanted a darker one. Worked, from cat-harness: . | ink | on white | on the light sidebar #f5f6fa | on the dark sidebar #27262b | . | #596a5b (the supplied art’s own) | 5.77:1 | 5.35:1 | 2.60:1 | . | #9db89f (same hue, lifted) | — | — | 7.00:1 | . 3:1 is the bar for meaningful non-text content, and the light ink is under it on the dark ground. Two inks, never two drawings . Both variants are emitted from one trace, differing in a single fill attribute, so they cannot drift: re-run the generator and both change together. Never hand-draw a second dark mark: it would be a second answer free to drift, the same failure as a hand-written stylesheet beside the theme node. Not a CSS filter . The obvious cheaper move is one file plus a filter: brightness() under the dark scheme. Do not: a filter over an arbitrary path is a guess about the resulting colour, and the entire reason the pair exists is a measured ratio. You cannot measure what a filter will produce without rendering it, and if you are rendering it you may as well declare it. Which surface follows which scheme . They are not the same question and the answer differs per surface: . | surface | follows | why | . | sidebar mark | the PAGE’s data-fa-scheme | it sits on the page; both <img>s are emitted and CSS picks one, because Liquid cannot read a client-side attribute | . | browser tab icon | the OPERATING SYSTEM, via media="(prefers-color-scheme: …)" | a <link rel="icon"> is resolved outside the page’s styling and cannot read the DOM — and the tab strip is browser chrome, which follows the OS, so matching the OS is matching what it actually sits on | . A reader who sets the page against their system will see the two disagree. That is correct, and the note in head_custom.html says so: each matches its own background, which is the only rule satisfiable everywhere at once. Absent is a real state . An instance that declares no mark-dark renders its one mark in both schemes. imageForRole returns undefined and both templates fall back; nothing downstream special-cases a folio that never opted in. Tracing supplied art . When somebody hands over a raster mark, trace it rather than approximating it by hand: a hand-drawn approximation can differ in kind from the original (a solid silhouette where the art was line work). Three things to know: . | potracer treats ZERO as foreground, the inverse of what the name suggests. Passing the ink mask directly traces the background. | Crop to square with an explicit canvas, not Image.crop past the edge: PIL pads with black, and the tracer reads that as ink. | Measure the result. Rasterise the traced path and compare it to the source bitmap — IoU against the original is a fact, “it looks right” over a 2 KB path is not. | . Check the reduction too, rather than assuming a small variant is needed: thin strokes vanish at tab size, but fill-only art has no such floor. Measure the ink fraction from 16px to 32px.

696c06adbcb9.doc: Contrast: measured over the darkest thing that could be there
696c06adbcb9.title: Contrast: measured over the darkest thing that could be there
696c06adbcb9.content: Consumer stage. generation emits the ink; this says what the ink has to clear, and against what.

ea993b7acce7.doc: Contrast: measured over the darkest thing that could be there
ea993b7acce7.title: The measurement is over PURE BLACK
ea993b7acce7.content: Ink over this scrim laid on pure black — the darkest art any instance could declare, and the binding case. Arbitrary art sits behind that text. An instance can declare its own art for a role, so the art a value was tuned against is not the art it will meet. A ratio measured over one picture is true of that picture; one measured over pure black is true of any. The shipped scrims measure 9.25:1 to 9.36:1 over pure black, against roughly 14:1 on pure white — the dark end is the binding one, by a wide margin. The floor is AAA, 7:1, and it is a floor rather than a target: a value below it is not a slightly worse theme, it is a theme that fails. Re-measure, never nudge. When a scrim changes, recompute the ratio and write it down beside the value: a scrim whose ratio nobody recomputed does less work than it appears to.

a10833aaf70d.doc: Contrast: measured over the darkest thing that could be there
a10833aaf70d.title: Why a comment carries the number
a10833aaf70d.content: A contrast ratio asserted in prose is a claim. The numbers live beside the values in schemas/ui/themes.ts because the alternative is a reader trusting a sentence, and themes.test.ts computes them rather than restating them: . Parsing proves a theme is well-formed. It does not prove the palette is legible, so the contrast ratios are computed here rather than asserted in a comment — a high-contrast theme whose contrast nobody measured is a claim.

b6ff51aa118d.doc: Contrast: measured over the darkest thing that could be there
b6ff51aa118d.title: The high-contrast pair declares NO backdrop, deliberately
b6ff51aa118d.content: high-contrast-light and high-contrast-dark carry no art, and that is not an omission to be filled in later. Art behind ink is the thing those two exist to remove. A scrim strong enough to make an arbitrary photograph safe at their ratios would hide the photograph anyway, so the choice is between a theme that fails its own promise and a picture nobody can see. They also carry no gradient: a gradated surface has a range of contrast against its ink, and the weakest point is the real one.

14a28397de51.doc: Contrast: measured over the darkest thing that could be there
14a28397de51.title: Colour is never the only channel
14a28397de51.content: The priority stripe is a width as well as a colour. Colour alone carrying a signal fails WCAG SC 1.4.1 and a monochrome reader cannot see it at all, so ThemeSchema has no field with which a theme could set the width to zero. A theme is a palette and a geometry, not a licence to remove a non-colour channel.

c3b9a727cc1c.doc: Contrast: measured over the darkest thing that could be there
c3b9a727cc1c.title: A new surface inherits this, it does not renegotiate it
c3b9a727cc1c.content: A todo sticky gaining backdrop art inherits the requirement exactly: it must not reach the board by skipping the measurement the landing stickies pay. A surface that renders art behind text and has no measured scrim is a contrast finding whatever it looks like on the reviewer’s monitor.

44cd28118ffc.doc: Contrast: measured over the darkest thing that could be there
44cd28118ffc.title: Contrast: measured over the darkest thing that could be there
44cd28118ffc.content: Generated from cat-harness/skills/ui/theming/theme-contrast.md — do not edit here. ✎ Edit this page’s source .

be2b05863198.title: Declaring a theme
be2b05863198.content: Producer stage. Intake decides whether art may enter; this decides what is written down about it.

a9f6eb527898.title: A theme is a palette AND a geometry
a9f6eb527898.content: schemas/ui/theme.ts — ThemeSchema. Four palette roles, never colour names: surface, ink, edge, accent, plus an optional gradient pair. A rule reads as what it does and a theme swap touches one file. A theme sets the priority stripe’s HUE and never its width. The stripe is a width as well as a colour because colour alone carrying a signal fails WCAG SC 1.4.1 and a monochrome reader cannot see it at all. ThemeSchema has no field with which to try. A theme is a palette and a geometry, not a licence to remove a non-colour channel. A gradated theme supplies both stops or neither — the schema refuses one, because a gradient with a single stop is a flat fill claiming otherwise. Surfaces must be OPAQUE. ThemePaletteSchema.surface is z.string(), so rgba(…, 0.4) parses — and themes.test.ts refuses it anyway, because the floating-sticky rule depends on it (see theme-artefacts). A premise a schema cannot hold is a premise that needs a test.

8d67583ff41c.title: All three layouts, or the theme is invalid
8d67583ff41c.content: laptop, mobile, card — the set <name>.json’s images[].layout uses. Missing a layout is invalid, never degraded. There is deliberately no fallback to another layout’s geometry: a theme that renders wrong on a phone ships, while one that will not load is noticed.

eaad79c7964c.title: Nothing derives a theme
eaad79c7964c.content: ThemedTodoFields.theme and the landing sticky’s required theme are the whole selection surface: an id, set by an author. This is a rule, not a gap. | A role is a swimlane, not a property of a thing. Nothing is a reviewer; somebody acts as one for a lane. A theme keyed on role would make a note’s appearance depend on which process happened to be reading it. | It makes the choice unarguable and invisible. With a table, “this one should look different” means editing something that governs everything else. | It is the conflation the layering already refuses. Themes live in the harness layer while the todos referencing them stay in todos/. | . Absent theme means nobody has chosen — a statement about an author, not a lookup that failed.

0fcc8617f2c3.title: Geometry over art is DECLARED, never derived
0fcc8617f2c3.content: Two regions, both on KgImage, both fractions of the image so the declaration survives a re-export at another size. | region | what it marks | the rule | . | textRegion | where the picture is quiet — where words may be drawn | per LAYOUT, because the same cloud sits elsewhere in a portrait crop. Absent means do not overlay text, never “anywhere is fine” | . | avatarRegion | where the subject is — the box a square frame clips to | per IMAGE and square in pixels. Absent means no avatar can be cut from this image, never “use the whole frame” | . Both are judgements about a composition, and that is why they are authored — found by rendering candidate boxes and looking at them. avatarRegion is square in PIXELS, checked against width and height. Equal fractions are square only on a square image: on a 1671x941 landscape crop the same numbers are a box 1.78x wider than tall, and a fraction-only check passes it. A square frame scales width and height by 1/w and 1/h independently, so a non-square box stretches the subject by w/h. An image declaring no dimensions may not declare an avatarRegion at all. Refused rather than accepted unchecked: one unverifiable box among verified ones reads as verified and is not.

29c140255710.title: What the declaration cannot tell you, ever
29c140255710.content: Whether the box is on the right thing. Square, in bounds, and framing a patch of sky are compatible. So: . Whatever declares a region is looked at, not diffed. bun run cat theme:sheet and bun run cat avatar:crops exist for that one job. See theme-artefacts for which crops carry which region today.

58e6d6835eba.title: Declaring a theme
58e6d6835eba.content: Generated from cat-harness/skills/ui/theming/theme-declaration.md — do not edit here. ✎ Edit this page’s source .

ae87d52924d3.title: Generating a theme’s CSS
ae87d52924d3.content: Consumer stage. declaration says what a theme is; this says what a stylesheet gets told about it, and what happens to a reader when it is not told.

fb9a398e40e6.title: One command — run it
fb9a398e40e6.content: bun run cat themes:css # regenerate site-chrome/assets/css/themes.css bun run cat themes:css:check # fail the build when it is stale . scripts/gen-themes-css.ts reads schemas/ui/themes.ts and writes site-chrome/assets/css/themes.css. Never hand-edit the output.

98a6de19df45.title: The failure: a theme with no rule paints over its own art
98a6de19df45.content: .fa-sticky paints var(--fa-sticky-grad-from, var(--fa-sticky-surface, rgba(128,128,128,0.08))) as its background. A theme’s [data-fa-sticky-theme= "<id>"] block is what sets those custom properties. If the generated stylesheet has no block for a theme, the sticky does not render unthemed — it renders with the FALLBACK surface, opaque, over the art. So the symptom is “the art is not showing” and the cause is “the stylesheet was not regenerated”. Those look nothing alike, which is why the cause gets rediscovered rather than read. This is a CONSUMER fact, and the producer/consumer axis is what makes it one. The generator did its job — it was not run. The reader of a missing rule is where it goes wrong, and a reader that falls back to something opaque hides the very thing whose absence it is reporting. A fallback that is INVISIBLE is the design error, not the missing run — the same reason a theme missing a layout is invalid rather than degraded: the degraded one ships and the invalid one is noticed.

33e71f1a2056.title: The default block is for “nothing has selected a theme”
33e71f1a2056.content: .fa-sticky-board:not([data-fa-sticky-theme]) { … } . An unthemed board is a state, not an error — leaving it unstyled would make “no selection yet” look broken. Note the scope: it is the BOARD, not every element, and a rule that matched everything would beat the per-theme blocks.

21e0155fd214.title: Every value is a named role
21e0155fd214.content: --fa-sticky-surface, -ink, -edge, -accent, never a colour name. Emitted by themeCssVars, so a theme swap touches the generated file only. Per-layout geometry (--fa-sticky-min-width, -padding, -font-scale) is emitted three times per theme: base, a max-width: 40rem media query, and a [data-fa-sticky-layout="card"] block. A phone sticky is not a laptop one scaled down, which is the whole reason the three layouts are declared rather than computed.

ba9cfba8d7c3.title: Before you believe a rendering
ba9cfba8d7c3.content: . | bun run cat themes:css — then look again. | bun run cat themes:css:check — 0 means the committed file matches the source. | Only then is “the art is not showing” a real finding. | .

80dae1aeb065.doc: At ingestion, and only at ingestion
80dae1aeb065.title: At ingestion, and only at ingestion
80dae1aeb065.content: This skill runs in exactly one place: theme-ui-review.bpmn, called from ingest-theme.bpmn Task_Review, whose agent lane is ingestion-agent. It is not part of a post-MVP SDLC step and is not called from crdm-deliver.bpmn.

7299c4991fb2.doc: At ingestion, and only at ingestion
7299c4991fb2.title: What it reviews
7299c4991fb2.content: It looks at the arriving graphical assets laid out in the design they are for, so a finding is a decision about what the assets will be, taken while it is still cheap. The questions: accessibility measured rather than asserted, branding against the instance’s own declaration, and every declared locale. Theme choice is an authoring judgement. There is no role-to-theme mapping (theme.ts records why), so nothing here checks a binding. What gets reviewed is the ingested art in its design context.

3588638ae6f6.doc: At ingestion, and only at ingestion
3588638ae6f6.title: What this gives up — accepted
3588638ae6f6.content: An ingestion review answers “what will this turn into?” only as far as the assets can be laid out in their design before the site exists — not how a crop reads in the finished page. That gap is accepted; do not add a post-MVP review call on your own initiative.

cbbf22cdbd73.doc: At ingestion, and only at ingestion
cbbf22cdbd73.title: A person is in the loop, inside ingestion
cbbf22cdbd73.content: R_Judge is a human step: a person looks at the assets laid out at a web and a mobile width, so ingesting a theme source is attended at that step. Ingesting anything else stays unattended — Gateway_ThemeSource in document-ingestion.bpmn routes non-theme documents past ingest-theme.bpmn entirely.

f3539dac52b4.doc: At ingestion, and only at ingestion
f3539dac52b4.title: Measure; do not assert
f3539dac52b4.content: Contrast is computed, against the real ground. A theme with a backdrop has no single ratio — ink over a photograph varies pixel to pixel — so the number that matters is the worst case the art can present. Every shipped scrim in this repository is measured over pure black for that reason, and the check is written so it can fail: without a case that fails at a thin scrim, passing assertions prove nothing about the value. Colour is never the sole carrier (SC 1.4.1). Where it carries meaning, look for the second channel — the priority stripe is a width as well as a hue precisely so a monochrome reader still sees it. An automated pass is necessary and not sufficient: . | axe accepts a non-empty placeholder as an accessible name, so a label removed from the accessibility tree can pass the automated check. | A CSS selector that matches nothing raises no error in any tool, and can leave a backdrop at its intrinsic size across the viewport with every gate green. | . So a person looks at the assets laid out in their design (R_Judge). That is a step in the diagram, not an optional extra, because no automated check catches either case above.

75416c835f3f.doc: At ingestion, and only at ingestion
75416c835f3f.title: Branding is a question about the INSTANCE, not about taste
75416c835f3f.content: Marks, palettes and art are checked against the instance’s own declaration rather than a remembered style. The sharpest form of the question comes from downstream: would a folio depending on this platform inherit something it did not choose? landing.html states it as a rule — “a downstream folio should not inherit a grumpy cat it did not choose” — and it is why a theme names an image role rather than a path.

11d9a879d45c.doc: At ingestion, and only at ingestion
11d9a879d45c.title: Languages: new UI is where untranslated strings enter
11d9a879d45c.content: Check that every user-facing string reaches the .pot, that each declared locale renders without clipping, and that right-to-left is laid out rather than mirrored by accident. The distinction worth keeping: a name is translatable and a value is not. A theme’s display name goes through the pipeline; its palette does not, because a colour is not language-dependent and translating one invites a locale to diverge on a value the CSS must agree on.

ca08cb242e75.doc: At ingestion, and only at ingestion
ca08cb242e75.title: Raise findings; do not fix them
ca08cb242e75.content: A finding goes back to whoever authored the choice, because the choice was theirs. There is no mapping to correct instead, and a reviewer who quietly re-themes a note has substituted their judgement for the author’s without saying so — which is the same objection decision-audit makes to editing a finding rather than overruling it with a note. The one exception is the one this repository already allows everywhere: a defect that is not a judgement call at all — a selector matching nothing, a string missing from the .pot, a contrast ratio below the floor — is a bug, and bugs get fixed.

9cf0f7dfa3a0.doc: Theming, split on the stage it fails at
9cf0f7dfa3a0.title: Theming, split on the stage it fails at
9cf0f7dfa3a0.content: Every file here is named for the skill it declares. servableSkills() in scripts/kg-audit.ts derives a skill’s id from its FILENAME, while package-manifest.json lists its name:, so a file whose basename differs from its name: is reported as manifest-skill-exists. This map is a skill, not a README.md. isSkillMd is declaration-over-location: a markdown file in a cat-harness directory that does not declare $schema: is a skill, so a README here would enter the graph as one with no name, unreachable through skill_fetch. This is a PACKAGE under skills/, not a top-level declared directory: kg-audit’s skillFiles() walks skills/, so a top-level topical directory would drop its skills out of skill QA.

d1467d3875a1.doc: Theming, split on the stage it fails at
d1467d3875a1.title: The axis, and the ordering matters more than the names
d1467d3875a1.content: Three levels: pipeline stage first, producer/consumer as the direction each stage faces, and per-artefact specialisation last. |   | stage | faces | what it owns | . | 1 | theme-art-intake | producer | art arrives; accepted with its declaration written, or refused with a named reason | . | 2 | theme-declaration | producer | what a theme IS as data — palette, three layouts, textRegion, avatarRegion | . | 3 | theme-generation | consumer | themes.css, and the fallback that paints over its own art | . | 4 | theme-contrast | consumer | scrims, WCAG, and why the measurement is over pure black | . | — | theme-artefacts | specialisation | sticky, landing board, docs background, navbar avatar — only what DIFFERS | . Stage is primary because that is how failures arrive: each one is at one stage. Going artefact-first would duplicate intake and contrast into every artefact, and a rule kept in one artefact’s prose gets rediscovered rather than read. Stage-first with specialisation last means a new artefact inherits the stages and declares only its difference. The avatar crop boxes are the worked example: the rule that a crop is declared data belongs to declaration, and the boxes themselves are navbar-avatar specialisation in artefacts. Producer/consumer is not a second partition of the same set. It says which direction a stage faces. It is what makes “a theme with no CSS rule falls back to an opaque surface and paints over its own art” a consumer fact rather than a generation detail: the generator did its job, and the reader of a missing rule is where it goes wrong.
